GraniteMaulBoon.Description.src: Uses a unique WARHAMMER COMBO that excels against SINGLE TARGETS

Rune.Water.SpecialEffect.src: Water spells excel at CROWD CONTROL, dealing lower DAMAGE but SLOWING enemies and providing HEALING to allies

DragonBreathResist.Description.src: When actively BLOCKING, this shield is able to BLOCK incoming DRAGON FIRE.

RingOfLife.Boon.src: When close to DEATH, TELEPORTS you to your current BED

PharaohsSceptre.Bane.Description.src: While a SUMMON is ACTIVE, you regain STAMINA slower than normal

Trinket.Amulet.Of.Plenty.src: Whilst mining or woodcutting there is a chance to double the received resources

CookingSkillcpae.src: You cannot burn food while wearing this cape.

TitansWrathBane.Description.src: You cannot cast additional ENCHANTMENTS on this weapon

FishingSkillcape.src: You have a small chance to instantly catch a fish.

WoodcuttingSkillcape.src: You have a small chance to instantly finish chopping a tree

MiningSkillcape.src: You have a small chance to instantly finish mining an ore rock.

AgilitySkillCape.src: You have a small chance to not consume stamina for the following actions: Jump, Dash and Evade.

ConstructionSkillcape.src: You have a small chance to not use building materials when placing a build piece.

RunecraftingSkillcape.src: You siphon double the number of runes from Anima Vents

Vestige.Name.Cape.Fire.src: An Ember Edged Remnant of Cloth

YewLog.src:
"How many yew logs could you log if you were a yew logger?"

There is nobody that hates you/yew puns more than a yew tree. Whenever a passing human makes one of these puns, the yew tree remembers. They let their hatred form a knot in their trunk. Look closely at the knot and you will see that it bears a striking resemblance to the punning offender's laughing face. 

That yew will crush one of its berries which, I am sure you are aware, is toxic to humans, and will daub it onto a twig. When the human passes by later, they will wait for a passing gust and whip the twig across the face. If the yew tree is lucky, it will be a fatal blow. 

When the crime scene investigators arrive to find out what happens, the yew tree smirks and says to itself "YEW DID IT".

AgilitySilverMedal.src:
"Nobody remembers second place", they say. Well, Zaros came second-place to Zamorak, and Zaros is doing pretty well for himself. Lougrim was second-place to Kuldra and people still remember her. I mean, sure, they're not perfect comparisons (they're both gods and at least one of them is dead), but you get the intention. You're special.

Plus, there's the small matter that a gold medal could still be in your future. There is still time for you to become Zamorak and Kuldra in the above scenarios.

BerryDrizzlePanSeared.src:
"Pan-seared what?", you may ask. Well, pan-seared herring and anchovies, my good fellow. That might sound like a lot of fish in one meal, but some dwellberry acts as a sweet binding agent, making the whole eating process rather delightful. It's a meal that's been around for generations, and you will often hear battle-worn adventurers wishing that they were back home for "some of mammy's pan-seared". 

We suspect that the berry drizzle pan-seared that you've made is NOT from mammy, however. We may be wrong: it's very possible that there's a quest that we've forgotten.

MithrilGreatsword.src:
"You see a mithril greatsword, I see a mithril dagger," Vannaka would say. He would then pick two up from Doric's forge, one in each hand, and try not to register effort. It was a routine, a little play, between Vannaka and Doric. 

This time, however, the joke was on Vannaka. Doric had made his mam's rock cakes, and folded some mithril round them – one for each hilt. 

Vannaka wobbled. "Cripes," he said.

LoyalHellhound.src:
"Loyal" hellhound implies that the other hellhounds aren't, in some way, loyal. Which is utterly correct: the other hellhounds are as loyal as a dagger to the back. Given half a chance, they would play fetch with your larger intestines.

But Houndmaster Rexiton knows their secret. They are impossibly vain. If you tell them that they are good boys – such very good boys – then you can get them to do anything.

UndeadDelight.src:
"Undead Delight" sounds like an audio track from a long-forgotten Halloween event, but NO – it's an unexpectedly tasty meal. The very dead flavours of an undead bass are meshed with the very alive flavours of a tomato, and the combination is capital-D Delicious.

We will admit that it's off-putting that the un-alive also find the Undead Delight tasty. Put it in front of a skeleton, zombie, demon or other wretched being and they will gobble it up like there's no tomorrow.

WeakFocusedFishingPotion.src:
"Wea" and "focused" may seem like an oxymoron, but you have to look at the terms from a different perspective. When we say "focused" we mean you – the angler – and your concentration. It is a measure of how much you narrow your eyes, quell your breath and attribute all of your senses to the timeless art of poking hooks into fish. This potion increases those faculties. You become so focused that nothing else in the world matters. 

And by "weak" we mean that the potion is a little bit rubbish at doing all of the above.

FishFry.src:
'Fish fry' is something of a misnomer, as only the eel is a fish, and even that's questionable now that it's undead. The lobster is most definitely a crustacean, and a cabbage is a holy orb of sustenance, delivered by the majestic Brassica Prime. Therefore, not a fish.

We give a fish fry a pass, mainly because it's a Fellhollow delicacy, once favoured by Ravanna. It was invented after a sailor saw a lobster and eel fighting and threw a well-aimed cabbage. He fried the result and lo, 'fish fry' was born.

WhisperingCapeGolden.src: A Golden Whispering Cape is a very special achievement, especially considering that you can't see where you're going half the time. I struggle to move fast anyway, but doing it in fog? Nah, you can keep your cape.

ZamorakWarriorPack.src: A bag of personal effects carried by the warrior class of Dowdun Reach. Rummage around inside: you've earned it.

StoneClub.src:
A big stone attached to a stick; not terribly durable, but surprisingly handy. This simple weapon has saved the lives of many warriors. When caught between a rock and a hard place, why not take advantage of the rock? 

Goblin children play a game called bonk-bonk-bash, a rather unpleasant little pastime that acts as a form of population control. Each of the goblins takes a rock, attaches it to a stick and then takes it in turns to thwack their friends with it. This is a traditional household game that keeps the costs of feeding the family low.

RawHerring.src: A bit too floppy to be useful for lumberjacks.

Harralander.src: A bitter tasting herb that makes for a poor tea, yet is often used as a morning pick-me-up by people with no tastebuds. It’s useful in crafting certain potions.

TokTz-Xil-Ak.src:
A blade forged from obsidian, in the heart of a great volcano.

The KotHaar of Ashenfall are ancient beings, whose existence dates back millennia ago to when the elder gods first created the region. At the end of their lives, they would take themselves on long pilgrimages through underground tunnels, back to the mainland, where they would be reborn anew in the Elder Kiln.

Fuzan put a stop to that, by destroying those tunnels.

Once these obsidian swords would have been reforged alongside their owners, each sword containing the ancestral memory of the swords that went before it. They would absorb fragments of KotHaar knowledge, learning, in their own strange way, how to be better weapons.

These swords are not alive, in any true sense. There is no soul within them. No mind you might ever speak with. But the KotHaar and their kin are strange creatures, born of fire and stone,  so their weapons carry some of that strangeness with them.

StoneBlock.src: A block of stone... there's not really much more to say here.

PaddedCloth.src: A bolt of cloth that has been reinforced. Makes for sturdier armour than normal cloth.

CapeOfVelgar.src: A cape depicting a powerful dragon.

TatteredCape.src: A cape made from tattered strips of cloth.

PinkCape.src: A cape worn by those with a love of pony clubbing. Which is not as sinister as it sounds…honest.

GraniteMaulHead.src: A chunk of granite imbued with powerful magic. On its own, this hunk of stone isn’t useful, but when combined with other components it becomes part of a much stronger weapon.

MeatStew.src: A classic meal across multiple realities. The aviansie enjoy a version of this using insects called Tobi’it. Goblins make their meat stews out of anything they can find… results vary.

SaradominCape.src: A cloak embroidered with the symbol of Saradomin, the human god of order. You'll be the envy of priests everywhere.

SpectralChinchompaCape.src: A cloak of stitched furs taken from spectral creatures. It is uncertain how one might craft such a thing, and perhaps it would be impossible anywhere other than Fellhollow – where the world of the dead and the world of the living eerily coincide.

AnimalHideScraps.src: A collection of pelt scraps collected from smaller creatures. Some druids would insist on crafting cloaks made only from smaller animals that died of natural causes. This meant that each cloak often took months, or sometimes even years, to craft. Naturally this wasn’t particularly helpful on the cusp of winter.

GypsumWax.src: A combination of gypsum powder and dihydrogen monoxide, gypsum wax contains the worst of both materials. It's as claggy and hard to remove as gypsum powder, and as deadly as dihydrogen monoxide.

StandardFarmingPotion.src:
A common misconception is that a farming potion is poured onto your crops, rather than into your mouth. While it might sound sensible - it's the crops that are growing, not you - it fundamentally misunderstands what the farming potion does.

The farming potion increases the experience you receive when you farm. It achieves this by making you sensitive to the wants and needs of your plants. You become intensely aware of them. You will know when even a single aphid lands on a leaf; when the last drop has been siphoned from the soil; when a potato wants to hear you sing. You are attuned to your crops, to the point that you might even find kinship with them. If you begin sleeping in your cabbage patch, you should consider lowering your consumption.

LeggingsOfLightness.src:
A cousin to the better-known Boots of Lightness, popular on the Gielinor mainland. These leggings were created by Shana, a Bramblemead villager who hated the cold. While the boots were functional and useful, making it easier to carry things round the village, she always felt the wind's chill, no matter what she wore.

Her solution was simple. Since enchantment created an excess of energy, at least when she did it – she was never going to become a wizard – she laced the leggings with a lightness charm.

The effect was twofold. Firstly, she could carry things around town as easily as if she were wearing the boots. Secondly, the enchantment kept her legs nice and warm.

Fortunately, the design for these leggings has improved over the years, removing the overheating problem that Shana was so fond of. Although she was probably less fond of it after her house caught fire.

Progress demands sacrifice.

MenaphiteCape.Red.src: A crimson cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

CrystalOrb.src: A crystal sphere containing a shimmering fog. It’s part of a magical ritual needed to craft a powerful staff, one that is infused with celestial power. The Icyene, of Hallow, once gifted these orbs to the followers of Saradomin, so that they might better serve the god of Order.

ZombiePack.src: A decayed and blighted sack. Contains the meagre belongings of the restless dead.

WildPie.src: A delicious pastry crust seals the flavours inside. Warm and filling, each bite designed to fill you with comfort. The flavour is earthy and rich, letting you shrug off almost anything.

MeatPizza.src:
A delicious pizza, covered in juicy tender pieces of meat, and seasoned with a delicious sauce. You might ask yourself where the cheese comes from, but it’s best not to think too hard about it. Ashenfall has many secrets and those who survive here must do many strange things. No one will judge you for this “cheese”. It’s fine.

Just enjoy the delicious flavours and try not to have an existential crisis.

BlueDragonhideLeather.src:
A discerning archer would do well to craft blue dragonhide leather. The colour is fetching, the defence against magic is second-to-none, and the material has an elasticity that makes it perfect for the nimble stuff that archers tend to do.

If it has a downside, it's a little tight. There's no hiding in blue dragonhide chaps, for example: all the lumps and bumps are out there.

RedCape.src: A fashionable scarlet accessory for the most daring fashionistas.

KalphiteFlyBait.src:
A fish can't swallow an entire kalphite. They might want to, as elastic as their mouths are, but a fish cannot cross the line from admiring a kalphite to digesting it. 

That's where you come in. With a slice here and there, suddenly a fish gets to try am morsel of antennae or mandible. And let me tell you: if the size roles were reversed, the kalphite would be wiped out in a week.

DragonKiteshield.src: A five-headed dragon and a hidden island took spot #1 and #2 respectively, but the presence of dragon metal was the third most surprising thing that Zilyana found on Ashenfall. Dragon metal meant a sequence of things to the icyene. It meant that the dragonkin had not only lived here, but lived here long enough to create their own dragons and combine their dragonfire with orikalkum. She noted it as something that she wanted to investigate further - once the malevolent dragon-queen was stopped, of course.

SkeletonPack.src: A foul-smelling sack, with threads frayed by the cruelty of time. Contains whatever strange possessions were being hoarded after death.

FriedSardine.src:
A fried sardine, also known as a charred pilchard or 'pilcharred', is the go-to snack for a fisherman's pocket. If you see a stoic fisherman who talks very little, it's likely because they've got a mouthful of fried sardine and don't want to reveal the bones between their teeth.

Fried sardines were also the subject of a failed business venture by a dwarf called Drorkar. He tried to manufacture "tins" that would contain these sardines, with smithed "rings" to open their tiny metal coffins. It was roundly rejected and cost the dwarf a great deal.

RedDragonhideChaps.src:
A garou hunter called Mayev was the first in Ashenfall to wear the skin of a red dragon, though she did so not out of malice, but in respect for a dear friend. To the garou, the hide of a slain foe is a mark of great pride, and the bones of a warrior are worn with great honour.

Dragonfire was little concern to creatures birthed in lava, and garou arrows bounced harmlessly off obsidian flesh. Yet, despite all this, it was the madness in their eyes that terrified Mayev the most: as if something else stared back at her. Something bright, radiating a heat greater than the sun and it took every ounce of willpower not to fall to her knees in worship.

Yet, she was prey now. The hunter became the hunted and the KotHaar fell on Mayev and her dragon before she could ready a defence. She fought bravely, desperately, but it would not save her and she readied herself for a death that never came.

Vakar dived into the fray, grasping her in jaws that could have severed her in two as easy as breathing. He carried her to safety. When she came to, she saw the spears, blades and shards of obisidian pressed deep into her friend and she held him in his last breaths, thanking him for her life.

She buried the heart of her friend, as was garou custom, and crafted armour and bow from his scales and bones. Her friend would be with her, always, as companion in her hunt.

RedDragonhideBody.src:
A garou hunter called Mayev was the first in Ashenfall to wear the skin of a red dragon, though she did so not out of malice, but in respect for a dear friend. To the garou, the hide of a slain foe is a mark of great pride, and the bones of a warrior are worn with great honour.

Dragons are not pets. They’re violent creatures, prone to random acts of aggression, driven by a rage that burns in their very soul. Still, Mayev was patient and she lured the dragon hatchling away from the corpse of its parent and out into the desert sands. Moonlight transformed the desert from gold to glittering silver, yet the ruby-red scales of the dragon seemed brighter than before.

Over the days, weeks and months to come, she kept the dragon secret. She brought it scraps of food, and kept it company on lonely days, and it came to see her not as a parent, not as a master, but as a friend. She saw him as the same. She named him Vakar – the flame-wrought song – and they would hunt together.

Over time, they knew each other’s strengths and could balance out their weaknesses. They hunted stronger prey, earning the respect of her tribe with the offcuts. Life was set to be everything they had both dreamed – until they met the KotHaar, and it all turned to ash.

MenaphiteCape.Yellow.src: A golden cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

PersonalChest.src:
A good bag is surprisingly difficult to make in Ashenfall. First, leather must be obtained by hunting down deer and the deer of Brynmoor are skittish creatures. They flee at the first sign of danger and chasing them can be more trouble than it's worth. Wood, on the other hand, stays pleasantly still and so it was that the druids invented this very useful little spell. 

Now, they no longer need to traipse through the forest in search of deer, when they can simply summon a chest to wherever they are. Much faster. Much easier and you don't have to lug around all those heavy resources all the time. 

This spell made druids very popular among locals, less so among hunters.

VegetableSoup.src: A good soup won’t just fill your stomach, it’ll lift your spirits. Warm and comforting, the taste of home. Popular across all of Gielinor with anyone with a pan and some vegetables.

GrilledMushrooms.src:
A great meal for a real fun guy… sorry.

Popular with terrible pun writers and villagers alike, roasted mushrooms were a staple diet across much of Ashenfall. Wild Knights would forage for the best mushrooms to enjoy on their long hunts.

The fortifying effect of mushrooms made them even more popular with those braving poison-filled Bloodblight Swamp.

ChefsHat.src: A hat worn by masters of the culinary arts. There are no special enchantments, no mysterious contraptions, indeed nothing that should make this hat stand out. Yet, it remains one of the most well regarded and respected pieces of clothing across the whole of Gielinor.

VaultGuardianCore.src:
A heart of alchemically modified rune essence. Layers of complex enchantments, and anima veins run through this core. It allows it to absorb ambient anima from its surroundings, which in term power the various functions of the vault guardian servitors.

This marvel of dragonkin science had revolutionary potential. The ability to create power sources that thrived off of the ambient anima of the region. Ashenfall, with it’s surfeit of magical power, was the perfect place for such a technology and the dragonkin would apply it to all of their arcane machinery.

LumberBackpack.src: A hefty bag, heavily  reinforced, this backpack is everything a budding lumberer needs in order to carry large quantities of wood from one place to a different place.

GypsumBoulder.src:
A large rock, full of delicious, delicious gypsum. Smash it with a pick and then fry up the delicious pebbles of a grill. Excellent if combined with a good marinade.

Of course, if you’re not a troll, I don’t recommend eating gypsum. Instead, apply it to various crafting projects for best effect.

ZogrePack.src: A large sack covered in mould and mildew. Once belonged to the terrifying zogres that wander Fellhollow.

LeatherShield.src:
A leather shield consists of a thick piece of leather stretched across a wooden frame. Wooden shields are bulky and heavy, making them more unwieldy. In contrast, a leather shield’s relative lightness makes it much easier to move into position. 

Leather shields were popular with the villagers of Bramblemead since the materials were comparatively easy to gather. Young warriors often wielded them as they accompanied druids into the woods, where the druids gathered the herbs for their medicines and rituals. 

The Children of Shadows also enjoyed leather shields, which they decorated with Zamorakian symbols, hoping to intimidate anyone who saw them.

AdamantWarhammer.src:
A little know tradition among Moon Garou blacksmiths, is to gather up all the bits of scrap metal from their workshops and create from them little figurines. They then sit beneath the shade somewhere, with various paints and turn these tiny creations into little pieces of art.

That was, until, Thraag learned of the game. Thraag was a blacksmith only so much in that he liked seeing metal melt. Something about the glow, the heat and the sheer sturdiness of the cooling metal, filled him with a sense of pride he never put into his personal hygiene.

Reeking like some unholy nightmare, Thraag was never invited to the gatherings of other blacksmiths, and over time the slight of being shunned festered within him, slowly mutating into something nasty.

He crafted a great hammer of pure adamant, sturdier and heavier then any hammer ever crafted before and he brought said hammer to the blacksmith gathering. There are few sights quite so tragic as grown blacksmiths weeping over smashed figurines.

It certainly did nothing to improve Thraag’s social standing.

DreamShard.src: A little like a conch, you can put this infernal shard to your ear. But instead of hearing the sea, you might hear the mumblings of an ancient mind. It's no less soothing, though. If you ever have trouble sleeping, we recommend the calming white noise of a fractured malevolent soul.

YewSapling.src: A little version of one of the only pieces of vegetation to bloom in the desert. They say that yew trees come into the world full of innocence and wonder, but this is a lie. They come into the world full of malice and mischief, if you turn your back on them for too long...well... nothing will happen, because they're trees, but they will say horrible things about you behind your back.

Soulscourge.src:
A long time ago, a cataclysmic event struck Ashenfall. It split the land and poisoned the air, sending clouds of tainted dust up into the atmosphere, where it was caught by Guthix's veil. Over the years this dust has seeped into the water of Ashenfall, tainting it with a dark sort of energy. Now, if someone drinks from this tainted water, and their ancestors didn't spent their lives being slowly warped by the strange anima of Ashenfall, they build up Soulscourge, whereby the anima within their soul is damaged. 

A soul is a container of anima within a person, shaped and enriched by their experiences. It is not piety, nor devotion, that grants a strong and robust soul, but adventure. Heroes, wanderers and explorers have strong and durable souls, allowing them to withstand Soulscourge buildup for longer. 

Should someone gain enough Soulscourge buildup, they will be afflicted by the condition of the same name. Their soul rips, tears and starts to unravel, dealing constant damage, until it can be healed. This can be fatal, as one needs an intact soul to survive. 

Fortunately, souls heal surprisingly quickly. Soulscourge buildup will fade over time as the soul repairs and enriches itself with the adventures of Ashenfall. 

To avoid Soulscourge buildup from drinking water, you need only boil it at a campfire. The taint in the water can be separated from it by boiling it and letting it evaporate off, where it harmlessly disperses into the atmosphere.

MysticRobeLegs.src:
A long-held frustration of the Zamorakian magi, the magical sect of the Children of Shadows, was that Zamorak never came to them. At no point did Zamorak ever set foot on the shores of Ashenfall. This fact is key to understanding the resentful mentality of the shadow mage: they feel a constant undercurrent of abandonment. It also explains why they believe that mystic cloth, "came from Zamorak himself".

As mystic cloth became more available at Dowdun Reach, Lord Rasmodel made the decision to allow its trade. The trade partners would be carefully chosen – no Saradominists, obviously. It led to the first interactions between the Children of Shadows and an offshoot of the garou. They showed no animosity to the Children; more a kind of unbridled curiosity. A friendship, of sorts, grew between Rasmodel and their merchants.

Over the span of that friendship, Rasmodel learned about their affinity to the moon, and their need to remain untethered, nomadic. He did not pry at their religion, but wondered whether this offshoot shared the same god as their counterparts.

It frustrated Rasmodel that he could not infiltrate the moon garou, as he did all other civilisations: he had no one in the Reach with the physiology. So, he resolved to meet with Alric, something he deemed a last resort. 

Alric suggested something interesting. He could not change the appearance of a human to resemble a garou: that was beyond his capabilities. But the mystic cloth: within that fabric dwelled an opportunity. The material was known to hum, to resonate. But, like a parrot, it could also retain resonance and repeat it. With work, the mystic cloth could survey the moon garou.

Perhaps Rasmodel could infiltrate them, after all.

MysticRobe.src:
A long-held frustration of the Zamorakian magi, the magical sect of the Children of Shadows, was that Zamorak never came to them. At no point did Zamorak ever set foot on the shores of Ashenfall. This fact is key to understanding the resentful mentality of the shadow mage: they feel a constant undercurrent of abandonment. It also explains why they believe that mystic cloth "came from Zamorak himself".

Mystic cloth was only for use by the archmage and his council. It was not only a sign of standing within Dowdun Reach; it was a sign that you should probably get on with your work. If you heard the hum of mystic cloth behind you, you had better not be doing something untoward.

The role of mystic cloth changed when Archmage Alric and Lord Rasmodel agreed to meet an attaché of Imaru and Xikotal. It was some cleric from Emberwood, looking to renew an annual trade agreement. 

It was to be a routine meeting, and Alric thought nothing of it. He planned to look at the cleric with disdain and sign the contract provided. But to Alric's scorn, the envoy turned up in mystic cloth. A mystic cloth waistcoat along with a jauntily worn mystic cloth cap. She was good-natured and jovial, which only made the interaction more painful for Alric.

Alric dared not look at Rasmodel, but he knew that there would be a smirk on that smug face. Alric burned the contract and blasted the envoy off the top of Dowdun Reach. The contract would have to wait.

From that point on, mystic cloth was not reserved for the greatest magi. It was free for any common magi to wear. Alric resolved to wear a different cloth.

MysticHood.src:
A long-held frustration of the Zamorakian magi, the magical sect of the Children of Shadows, was that Zamorak never came to them. At no point did Zamorak ever set foot on the shores of Ashenfall. This fact is key to understanding the resentful mentality of the shadow mage: they feel a constant undercurrent of abandonment. It also explains why they believe that mystic cloth "came from Zamorak himself".

The story goes something like this: a Zamorakian apprentice-mage resolved to hang himself. He looked about his room but, so poor was he, he did not have the tools to perform that simple task. His chair could not bear his weight. His bedclothes ripped when he hung from them. He crumpled to the floor in misery. 

In that moment, Zamorak came to him. The mage was awestruck. In Zamorak's hands was fibre that vibrated with magic. It hummed audibly – the mage felt that he could hear chanting from it. When the mage stared at it, the blue shimmered through hues of the rainbow, and then returned to blue.

"Take it, young mage," said Zamorak, and he handed the mystic fibres to the mage. "I will see you in the next life."

In a kind of prophetic panic, the apprentice carried the fibre to an archmage. He relayed how Zamorak had come to him and brought him – alone – this mystical new fibre. He was overjoyed. He wished for the Children of Shadows to have the fabric, and he asked permission to study it.

The apprentice was tried by a council of his peers and stoned to death. His crime was denying the will of Zamorak.

The fibre? The archmage reverse-engineered its properties, and a new fabric was born.

RuneEssence.src:
A magical stone with the ability to absorb the ambient anima around it. On Ashenfall, the rocks hover in the air as if resting on some invisible structure, held aloft by invisible currents of magical energy.

With the right equipment and skill, rune essence can be infused with certain magical resonances, taking on the elemental power of the air, or the flame.

This discovery is one of Guthix’s greatest triumphs and perhaps his longest lasting miracle.

AshTree.src: A mature ash tree, strong and sturdy and a great source of timber.

MithrilCrossbow.src:
A mithril crossbow is the standard issue for any modern Black Knight. If you showed ability, then you might be promoted to Black Knight Sniper, and that came with the Black Sniper Crossbow. But for the average Black Knight, the crossbow was a long-kept friend. 

The crossbow's main purpose was to stop demons in their tracks. The Zamorakian magi claimed to keep their demon hordes under control, but demons tested that claim.

The crossbow had other uses. Remove the bolt, rest the crossbow stock-upwards on the floor, and you had a stool. Sit on the floor and it was a headrest. 

You could also waste time shooting ravens. Shooting the red, glowing ravens meant immediate dismissal, however. Alric demanded they were protected, for reasons that he never expanded on.

RedDragonhideCowl.src:
A moon garou hunter called Mayev was the first in Ashenfall to wear the skin of a red dragon, though she did so not out of malice, but in respect for a dear friend. To the garou, the hide of a slain foe is a mark of great pride, and the bones of a warrior are worn with great honour.

As a cub, Mayev was never one to stay in one place. She ran round and round the caravans without a care in the world, always bringing the frustration and ire of her elder. “Be still!” were the words she heard first thing in the morning. “Be quiet!” the command she heard each night before bed. Yet, stillness and silence were as alien a concept to her as the magic of the druids - something far out of her reach.

One day, she left her camp in search of wild adventure, much to the chagrin of the camp guards. She risked the harsh sunlight of the dunes, clinging to shadows, exploring caves and passages revealed by the passing sandstorm of the day. Each morning her world was different, new paths appeared while familiar ones were hidden, and on this day she found a cavern deep underground.

There she found a red dragon, breathing her last breath, and the hatchling beside her breathing his first.

LargeWardstone.src: A more powerful and refined wardstone, this one allows you a much greater return on investment. When activated, it draws energy from the soul more cleanly and efficiently, reducing the impact of Soulscourge on the user.

MenaphiteCape.White.src: A pale cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

SoulFragment.src: A piece of a soul, half devoured by Imaru. Death seeks these to restore what he can of the lost, so that they might move on to the afterlife.

BluriteDeposit.src: A rock containing the most blue ore you've ever seen.

Sandstone.src: A rock with a grainy texture. I really don’t know what you’re expecting here, there’s no deep lore about sandstone.

CoalRock.src: A rock, with coal in it. The implications of so much coal would cause any Gielinorian historian a headache, reminding them that there is so much about the world that they may never know.

ImarusHead.src:
A rotting and twisted dragon head, momentary twitches still flicker through it, the last remnants of necromancy at play.

The tragedy of Imaru is that she was once a sweet and gentle creature. Cruel dragonkin experiments had robbed her of the only thing she had ever wanted, to be a mother. So when the humans came to her land, she saw in them the children she never had. Xikotal, her mate, encouraged this nurturing behaviour, knowing the joy it would bring his beloved.

She could have been happy, and the people of Fellhollow could have been happy with her.

But Kuldra could not allow it. The queen’s hatred and rage became an infection that took hold of Imaru’s grief and, like some foul parasite, twisted it into something worse.

It is better that Imaru is no more. There is none who would argue otherwise. Yet, whilst we should not mourn the monster, perhaps we should take a moment to mourn the mother she could have been.

MenaphiteCape.Blue.src: A sapphire cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

BandosianAmulet1.src:
A seemingly simple amulet carrying the symbol of Bandos. It feels strangely warm to the touch, and a faint sensation like the memory of a heartbeat thrums through your fingertips.

Zanik would be very interested in this.

DragonbaneCape.src:
A seer once dreamed about brave warriors who walked across Ashenfall in another time. An age both past and present, where the rules of the world were different. These great heroes challenged and slew an echo of Velgar, saving a land that never was. 
While the seer’s memory of that dream fades with each passing moment, she was able to embroider the event into a cape, so that all might know of these legends from another time.

MenaphiteCape.Black.src: A shadowy cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

VaultGuardianShard.src:
A shard of rune essence, refined and manipulated by dragonkin alchemy. Tiny lines, like veins, run through the shard in very specific patterns, allowing the precise control of anima flow through the construction. When used correctly, these shards can create magical circuits, allowing the vault guardians to move, sense and attack with impunity.

It was the dragonkin Lacrussa that discovered this technology and it paved the way for powerful servitors to be constructed. Ultimately she would consider the technology a failure, albeit a useful one.

TokTz-Ket-Xil.src:
A shield of obsidian, forged and reforged countless times in the heart of the Elder Kiln. Aeons of experience defending against anything that might seek to do its bearer harm, this shield now stands as one of the sturdiest defences on the planet.

Yet, within this shield, are myriad cracks and fractures, imperceptible to the human eye, yet strained across the entire structure, down to its core. A last cry of the desperate KotHaar that wielded it, as their will was subverted by the dragon Fuzan and turned to cruelty.

If you were to gaze upon those fractures with the eyes of the KotHaar you would see a warning to all. Beware the fire, fear the sun, she whispers through the luminance from worlds of kindling ash.

ImaruDragonfireShield.src: A shield with the visage of Imaru the devourer welded to the front. Holding the shield feels cold to the touch and instils within you a hunger for battle. Your blood pumps faster with a terrible need to rend your enemy limb from limb.

MithrilPickaxe.src:
A sign of mining distinction, the mithril pickaxe will get you noticed if you hang out with the right mining crowds. Doric in particularly will give you an appreciative wink. He might even toss you a rock cake or two. 

The mithril pickaxe is cold to the touch, incredibly reflective and – most importantly – strong as an ox. You will no doubt have already realised that it makes short work of any deposit you find.

BandosianAmulet2.src: A simple amulet bearing Bandos’ symbol. Every once in a while you could swear you hear strange whispers from it, like a song you can’t quite remember. It’s cold to the touch and makes the hairs, on the back of your neck, shiver constantly.

AdventurersBody.src:
A simple tunic brought with you from the mainland. It barely classes as armour, but it’s better than no armour at all. 

When you joined the expedition, you had nothing but the clothes on your back. All your worldly belongings were lost, and all your gold drained away. Debt collectors would appear out of the shadows, swarming toward you like rats seeking cheese. What choice did you have but to leave? 

The expedition offered you a chance away from all your troubles. An opportunity to escape the cruel hand that fate has dealt you. These clothes once represented everything you ever lost, but now they represent the threadbare start of a new beginning.

LesserHealingPotion.src:
A step up from the weaker version, this potion allows the body to absorb more of the ambient anima, which in turn ramps up the healing. The potion allows the drinker to shrug off greater physical trauma than before.

For years herblore masters have worked on versions that might work on emotional trauma, but to these days there has been little success.

UnfiredClayVessel.src: A sticky clay container in need of a kiln.

SuperQuarrymaster.src: A super quarrymaster potion will give you supernatural stamina when it comes to mining rocks, but you should be careful. Potions have the annoying habit of wearing off, and it's only then that you realise you've got killer cramp, pins and needles, or miner's cough. There's no comedown quite like a quarrymaster comedown.

MapleLongbow.src:
A supple wood, is the maple. When cut into long, reed-like lengths, it can be formed into a worthy longbow. The process also releases syrup – a treat after a day's fletching. Not enough to make a maple toastie, mind, but enough to leave a sweet taste in the mouth.

Bramblemead was often the venue for archery competitions, and the maple longbows would be out in force. Etched into the trophy, you would find many Rasmodels. They were a noble bloodline on Ashenfall, and would often add to their reputation by earning combat trophies.

Marrentil.src: A sweet smelling herb that is used as an ingredient in many poison remedies.

PumpkinSoup.src: A taste of autumn reduced to slurry and warmed over the fire. In Fellhollow, pumpkin soup was a popular dish when the temperature started to drop. Locals would gather together and share enormous cauldrons full of soup, as a way to build bonds with their community. It is said that once the villagers created an enormous cauldron, so that Imaru and Xikotal could join in the tradition, though for the great dragons it was barely an appetiser.

Fellhollow.ForgottenTemple.src: A temple, to a long forgotten god of man. This place is abandoned, fallen into ruin, with no remnants of who it was dedicated to before. Sometimes even places can die, as the last memories of their purpose fade into nothingness. Now, it has become the property of Death and he resides here on the edge of Fellhollow, waiting for someone that can assist him with his problems.

DwellberryGlazedFlank.src: A thick and juicy steak, combined with a rich and sticky dwellberry sauce. Each mouthful is like a taste explosion, and it can be difficult to hold yourself back. Orik the Bear was a Wild Knight who excelled in this dish, and other Wild Knights would seek him out at the gatherings for his culinary expertise.

HeartyStew.src: A thick and tasty stew, rich in flavour and nutrients. Bramblemead’s head chef, Leander, use to say that eating this stew was like sitting around a warm fire with friends. The aroma of the rich gravy filling your nostrils makes you feel like you’re home. Villagers would gather when he made a big cauldron of the stew, each of them ready for an evening with friends.

UnfiredClaySlab.src: A thick slab of clay, not very useful without being baked in a kiln.

ClaySlab.src: A thick slab of clay. Used in construction projects.

RedberryGlazedFlank.src: A thick, delicious and juicy flank steak, glazed with subtle redberry tones. Delicious and nutritious.

OakSapling.src: A tiny little oak tree. Don’t be fooled by its size, it still wants to kill you. All trees do.

DireWolfHide.src: A tougher, more resilient hide, obtained after slaying a deadly dire wolf. It is said that if you wear the hide of a dire wolf, during the light of a full moon, then you’ll rapidly reduce the size of your circle of friends.

MapleTree.src: A tree full of bounties, whether it's maple logs for your crafting needs or maple syrup for cooking. The maple tree knows how much you need its wares and it keeps a ledger. You are indebted to the maple tree, and it will come to collect.

YewPlank.src:
A tree is a beautiful and wayward thing. It grows in twists and contortions, curling towards light and water. Place a seed and you cannot predict which way it will grow, if at all.

So, what do you do? You cut it into a precise 2x8 format and line them up next to each other. If one has an imperfection, you toss it away as waste.

The yew tree's revenge is coming. And it may well take the form of cutting humans up into a precise 2x8 format. Then it will go back to growing into beautiful, wayward shapes.

Opal.src: A very shiny stone. Prized by magpies around the world, who are drawn to it’s magnificent luster.

MenaphiteCape.Pink.src: A vibrant cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

MenaphiteCape.Purple.src: A violet cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

LostSoul.src: A wandering spirit, desperately clawing at any hint of life. Pity them and move on, you cannot help them.

MagicShortbow.src:
A warning for a very particularly kind of ranger: magic wood has a tendency to twinkle. Now, if you're the creed to hide in the shadows, then you might want to reconsider the magic shortbow. It is phenomenally accurate and a delight to use, but it doesn't half draw attention. 

Of course, you can embrace the problem. I remembers stories about The Glittering Assassin in Varrock. The last thing you would see before dying is something fabulous in your peripheral vision.

SwampWeed.src: A weed found in desert regions – haha just kidding, swamps. It’s a weed found in swamps. I don’t know what else to tell you.

AdventureCape10DowdunReach.src: A wise purchase. While it doesn't make you invisible or grant you super powers, this cape does make a delightful swishing noise as you sashay.

AdventureCape1DowdunReach.src: A wise purchase. While it doesn't make you invisible or grant you super powers, this cape does make a delightful swishing noise as you sashay.

AdventureCape2DowdunReach.src: A wise purchase. While it doesn't make you invisible or grant you super powers, this cape does make a delightful swishing noise as you sashay.

AdventureCape9DowdunReach.src: A wise purchase. While it doesn't make you invisible or grant you super powers, this cape does make a delightful swishing noise as you sashay.

AshSapling.src: A young ash tree, easily torn down by just your bare hands. Doesn't provide much wood, but it's a good start.

PumpkinSpiceInfusion.src:
Across dimensional rifts this drink calls out to a part of us we try and hide. That piece of us that wants a touch of whimsy, when the world turns darker than we feel comfortable with. As the approaching shadow of winter looms, its cold chill reaching into our souls, drinks like these offer a little warmth against the oncoming frost.

Still, its allure can be overwhelming. There are some who succumb too heavily to its charms, becoming thralls to the flavour. Their entire personality clasps onto this mixture with frightening zeal.

It is tasty… but at what price?

EnchantedAdamantCrossbowBolts.src:
Adamant is a special metal, responding well to magic and allowing it to be shaped into durable and deadly forms. Adamant bolts are the bane of many creatures, their sharpness and their hardiness lets them pierce through almost any defence.

Yet, what if you didn’t stop the magic in the crafting process? What if you added more and more, creating bolts enchanted with murderous wrath? The answer to that is in these enchanted bolts, that sap your life in order to deal greater damage to your foe.

Sacrifice for vengeance, the gods would approve. 

Except Guthix, but his opinion is somewhat moot these days.

AdamantiteBar.src: Adamantite is one of the most durable and impressive metals, that would have revolutionised the human populace of Ashenfall if they’d survived long enough to find it. The Moon Garou have learned to make good use of it, but they are comparatively few in number and have little desire for the industrialisation such metals could bring.

ObsidianDevice.src:
After being beaten to a pulp by a KotHaar, you might find it difficult to believe that they are a cultured race. Or, more specifically, they WERE a cultured race, and that culture has eroded away to almost nothing over the centuries. There are records of KotHaar libraries, with books written on stone. It is hard to believe, but at least one play has been performed by the KotHaar, although no KotHaar can remember to what it pertained.

While the life of the modern KotHaar doesn't leave room for culture and entertainment, it is common to find them fiddling with the remnants of it. They fidget with old stone pamphlets, fragments of toys, and materials that were used in KotHaar sports. These obsidian devices mean little to the KotHaar, but they get a semblance of reassurance from tinkering with them.

AdamantPickaxe.src:
After settling in the Umbral Sands, the Moon Garou needed to adapt to static lives not driven solely by the hunt. Their druids used magic to acquire adamantite ore from the rocks around the sands, but it was inefficient, messy and occasionally deadly.

Garou smiths used the ore to create the first tools of their new civilisation, the adamant pickaxe, so their druids could relax.

Now, because of these tools, the garou could mine ore and reshape the land, creating the very foundations of a new way of life for their people.

AshRod.src:
Ah, the ash rod. It's been here from the First Age and will be here for many ages to come. Ever reliable, it gets the job done. Line up all the tools in the world and the ash rod will likely be named the most productive and certainly the most loved. 

All hail the ash rod!

UmbralKebab.src:
Ah, the humble, versatile kebab. It can be a handy, portable dish, or it can be a sprawling, sloppy one. It can be a snack or a meal; a low-effort munch or a high-end dish that you would serve to in-laws. It can be skewered or open; spicy or mild.

About the only constant is a sense of fulfilment, that you've eaten well and more than enough, alongside a vague, far-off worry that you might be attached to a toilet bowl later on that night.

BlackDragonhide.src:
Ah, the last words of many a ranger: "It's a black dragon! Hide!". 

Dad jokes aside, you really SHOULD hide from a black dragon. They have some kind of deep-seated grievance that means they are horrible to EVERYONE. And they're not the kind of bad person that can be ignored or left off invite lists: they will seek you out and immolate you for even thinking about them. They really are awful.

MapleToastie.src:
Ah, the sweet gooey goodness of a maple toastie. On its own, the maple syrup might have been too much, but the dried redberry? It ties it together with a little red bow.

There's the added bonus that it's bursting with natural sugars. Now you can use that energy to go mine and chop some natural resources.

SuperFocusedConstruction.src:
Ah, to be a zen-like architect, focused on nothing but crenulations and scaffolding. Such thoughts were nought but dreams before this potion, yet now you have a chance to soar to new heights of… err… masonry?

It’s hard to write about a potion that enhances your desire to build things. To wax lyrical about a liquid that grants greater XP when you craft new decorations and bigger stairs. Yet, here we are.

KalphiteShell.src:
Ah, very good: you have cottoned onto something that mainland Gielinor has failed to understand. The way to make armour as strong as a kalphite's exoskeleton  is not to hammer it into shapes that are suitable for humans. The carapace is too resistant, and you will get an armour that is ill-fitting for the human form. There will be plenty of gaps for someone to slip a Keris into. 

What you need to do is break the shell into its component fragments. You need to make a kind of kalphite mosaic, then adhere it with something acrid to make it into an armour. That's how you become as hardy as a kalphite.

GroundDragonTooth.src: Alchemists and specialists in herbal remedies would be lying if they said they hadn't considered the medicinal properties of Kuldra. They imagine what it would be like if they could get hold of one of her teeth, crush it, and then use it in place of the traditional ground dragon tooth. Just how much of a kick would that give their concoctions? They're self-aware enough to know that it's just a fantasy, but they like to daydream about it anyway. Sure, it would be lovely to rid the world of a tyrant dragon, but think of the potions!

WeakHealingPotion.src:
Alchemists have long strived to create potions to rid mankind of all their ills. Normally these potions are regeneratives, that boost the body’s ability to repair itself by drawing in the ambient anima and infusing it into the blood and tissue of the drinker. On the mainland this changes healing from a matter of days, to a matter of hours. On Ashenfall the results are far more pronounced.

The ambient anima of the region is so strong, that wounds heal in moments. Cuts vanish as if they never were, the wounds healing so quickly that even scars cannot form. The weaker potions burn themselves out before they can heal massive injuries, but the results are impressive none the less.

StandardConstructionPotion.src: Alchemy is a magnificent thing. With innocuous ingredients like ground sandstone and irit, you can make a concoction that is focused on something as singular as construction. One rock and one herb can make you better at making an architrave or lintel.

KalphiteWing.src:
All kalphite are capable of flight, but its rare to see a kalphite flying. We can't communicate with the kalphite to find out why, but zoologists have had a punt regardless. The dominant theory is that, because the Kalphite Queen can transition to a flying state, the wings are seen as a sign of status. If you were to fly as a kalphite, you would be challenging the sovereignty of the Queen herself. Which would be unwise. Have you seen the size of her?

The other theory is that the wings are used in the mating ritual, which - you would hope - would explain why you, personally, haven't seen a kalphite flying.

GoldHelm.src:
All that glitters is gold, is factually inaccurate but a fun song lyric. However, golden armour is most certainly glittering. Forged from gold bars, melted down and refined into plate armour, there are few who can deny the sheer audaciousness of an outfit like this.

Golden armour was first created by the King of Bramblemead, who felt that he really needed to stand out as much as possible when riding into battle: a stance that demonstrated a complete failure to understand even the most basic of military tactics.

His version had the armour encrusted with glittering gemstones that only further served to make him the most desirable target on the battlefield.

GoldLegs.src:
All that glitters is gold, is factually inaccurate but a fun song lyric. However, golden armour is most certainly glittering. Forged from gold bars, melted down and refined into plate armour, there are few who can deny the sheer audaciousness of an outfit like this.

Needless to say, the fate of Sir Leigh is entirely predictable. Even though his armour lacked the gemstones of his sovereign, it was still armour forged from solid gold. This meant that not only did it lack the defensive capabilities of sturdier metal, but it also meant that every opponent went straight for him.

He was torn to shreds, and his armour sold off in pieces.

His sacrifice, however, did save the king’s life. After witnessing the horrid destruction of his most loyal commander, the king decided that future battles would be waged in steel armour… very very thick steel armour… and, preferably, from very far away.

GoldBody.src:
All that glitters is gold, is factually inaccurate but a fun song lyric. However, golden armour is most certainly glittering. Forged from gold bars, melted down and refined into plate armour, there are few who can deny the sheer audaciousness of an outfit like this.

The second person to wear gold armour was knight commander Sir Leigh, who donned the glittering monstrosity out of misplaced loyalty to his liege. His belief was that at least he could act as a decoy for those that would aim straight for the king. He had attempted to coopt other knights to don similar garb, but the expense of such equipment grew too costly to attempt it.

Shrimp.src:
Almost all fishing careers begin with these little critters. Their number is practically infinite, so the universe responds by gifting them with the survival instinct of an inebriated moth approaching the most magnificent flame.

Many a new fisherman has found their diet consisting almost exclusively of these crunchy little things.

RedberryCrunchies.src: Although a crude facsimile of gnomish cooking, the Redberry Crunchy is a pleasant snack that will get you through the day.

LesserMagicPotion.src:
Although humans cannot use magic without runes, they can become quite proficient conduits for power. A wizard and a farmer, when possessing the same runes, do not produce the same results, the former far outshines the former. 

This made some farmers pretty upset. For years they had ranted to their cows and sheep about how wizards were just snooty uppity types with shiny rocks. Yet, faced with this revelation, there was no denying that a farmer and a wizard simply weren’t equals in disguise. 

One farmer wanted to level the playing field and brought in a local witch who was had a grudge against the snooty men in blue robes. 

Between the two of them, they found a way to improve a person’s connection to the magic within them via a magical potion. Those who drank it cast spells more efficiently and with greater skill than they ever could before. 

The farmer wanted to use this new advantage to put the wizards in their place, raze down the tower and claim magic a tool of the people. Unfortunately, the witch saw a different future, one that sparkled with glittering gold coins. 

She died happily, wealthier than she had ever dreamed, surrounded by adoring young suiters who wanted a piece of her inheritance. The farmer died after being trampled to death by cows that were tired of his grumbling.

RawLobster.src: Although some people insist that a lobster must be boiled alive to get the best flavour, you have already put it out of its misery – fortunately for the lobster. Now you can look forward to boiling it guilt-free for a much gentler flavour.

DarkMageBody.src:
Although the name may be sinister, the robes and the people who wear them are not automatically evil. 

Brynmoor had a string of so-called “dark wizards.” Most were little more than bandits with a penchant for magic. The guards were enough to deal with most troublemakers, but a small group of them caused real trouble. 
They were members of the “Children of Shadows”, a Zamorakian cult that began to spread through the population. The cult fed on distrust, paranoia and greed, some very human traits. Among this number were three apprentices of the wizard’s guild, who were frustrated that they were not given the promotions they felt they deserved. 

In their quest for power, the ‘Children of Shadows’ stumbled upon ancient vaults, repositories of the dragonkin’s long-forgotten secrets. Here, they discovered the remnants of a forbidden text, a relic of immense power. Driven by their arrogance, they chose to follow its instructions, unaware of the horrors they were about to unleash.

DarkMageHead.src:
Although the name may be sinister, the robes and the people who wear them are not automatically evil. 

The first set of dark mage robes were so named because the technique to craft them required cloth that had been dyed by a unique alchemical mixture. As the years passed and Guthix introduced runes, the mixture was replaced with subtle enchantments, though the appearance was kept the same for tradition’s sake. 

Naturally, many practitioners of magic preferred this armour because of its darker aesthetic. Indeed, many rogue “dark wizards” would don this armour and use magic to engage in sinister undertakings, earning this armour’s moniker a more sinister meaning.

DarkMageLegs.src:
Although the name may be sinister, the robes and the people who wear them are not automatically evil. 

The most infamous dark wizards became a fairytale for the people of Brynmoor, a cautionary tale about greed and the desire for power. They sought power in the darkest of places, and it turned them into something monstrous. 

They appeared in the village in the dead of night as twisted versions of themselves—mindless creatures infused with a shadowy essence. Those who found themselves in their path had their lives ripped out of them until nought but an empty husk remained. 

It took all the visiting Wild Knights to take them down. Arrow after arrow, spell after spell, the task seemed almost insurmountable until the light of the sun made the creatures vulnerable. In their death throws, it was as if some horrible chill fell across the world as if a door somewhere had been opened into somewhere it shouldn’t.

FriedOnions.src: Although the preparation leaves you weeping, and the smell makes it worse, fried onions are a delicious meal to get you through a difficult day.

SacredOil.src:
Although the recipe is significantly different to the oil created in Morytania, this oil serves a similar purpose. The priests of Emberwood created this oil to assist in funerary rites, the strange scent of the oil would help the dead pass on when cremated and, crucially, in the time of the Withering, the bodies would be reduced to ash, unable to get up and cause further trouble.

Originally this oil used pressed olives, and the influence of the gods to create an oil that would burn a body sufficiently to avoid the dead rising. As the Withering increased and civilisation began to fall into ruin, the priests found alternative methods to create a sufficiently strong flame.

Seeds.Toadflax.src: Although they prefer the toxic atmosphere of the Bloodblight swamps, these seeds can grow just about anywhere with the right care paid to them.

LesserAshes.src: Amid the sulphurous pile are some items. Don't be scared: reach a hand in and claim what's yours.

BlackKnightHoundmaster.src:
Among all the ranks and roles of the Black Knights, the one that is most sought-after is houndmaster. It is not difficult to see why: life as a Black Knight is lonely and life-expectancy is low. Having a four-legged friend can make life an increment brighter, particularly when the hellhound is its own source of light.

It's also notable that, among all the enmities that exist in Dowdun Reach, there is none bigger than that between hounds and ravens. The ravens taunt the hounds, and the hounds would dearly love some raven between their teeth.

AshShortbow.src:
An ash shortbow is the first weapon most young archers train with. It’s easy to make and, therefore, not so problematic if it breaks during training. Human villagers would often craft their first bows together under the tutelage of a visiting Wild Knight. They would use branches that had naturally fallen from the trees and carefully whittle them into the bow’s limbs. Bowstrings would be created by gathering flax from the nearby fields and spinning them into thin but hardy threads. 

Most would break on first use. Some would break before the first arrow was fired. Still, village youngsters would laugh at their misfortunes and start the whole process again. Each time improving. Each new bow sturdier than the last.

PioneerScarf.src: An attractive scarf, worn by those who first ventured forth into Ashenfall.

MenaphiteCape.Orange.src: An autumnal cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

BlueCape.src: An elegant cloth cape in a delightful azure hue.

PioneerCape.src: An embroidered cape, commemorating the first who explored the untamed wilds of Ashenfall.

MenaphiteCape.Green.src: An emerald green cape in the Menaphite style. Though not technically Menaphite in design, these Moon Garou creations were heavily influenced by the “River Mother”, a visiting goddess with a strong connection to the Menaphite deserts.

BronzeBar.src: An ingot of a copper-tin alloy. Highly prized by blacksmiths.

UndeadRat.src: And you thought the giant rats were bad enough!

BoneClub.src:
Animal bones are surprisingly durable, especially those found on Ashenfall. The magic of the continent seeps into their marrow, slowly strengthening them and making them tougher. This goes some way to explaining the ferocity of ordinarily docile creatures, but it also helps when crafting tools. 

Cows and similar beasts were celebrated in the age of Guthix. The people of Brynmoor preferred to take an animal’s life only on the hunt or after long years of service. When an animal passed, it was thanked for its sacrifice, and the materials helped strengthen the village. 

A club forged of bone was a simple tool but one that made defending the village much easier. Roving beasts were easily pushed back, and the village was protected by the animal’s last gifts.

AnimalHides.src: Animal hides have a variety of uses and have made hunters very popular throughout history. In Bramblemead there was an annual competition to see who could find the most interesting hide. While anima twisted animals were plentiful, many hunters turned to cheating, leading to a rise in the dye trade.

SubjugationStaff.src:
Anyone who worked with Alric knew about the Subjugation Staff. It would thud, thud, thud on the cobblestone floor as he approached. It was a welcome warning that Alric was arriving, but it came with notes of dread. 

The power of the Subjugation Staff came from that which had been rolled up and inserted into its core: a demon pact – but one that had been defaulted on. A demon, not a human, had failed to keep their side of the bargain, and that gave the contract a radiating power. Alric captured that power within the staff. While he held it, it was as if all of demonkind owed him something.

AgilityFlag.src:
Are you one of those people who wakes up with an inexplicable need to run or bend into strange shapes? Do you find it impossible to sit still for more than five minutes, instead hopping up to do some stretches? Are you one of THOSE people?

Well, may I interest you in the ability to make your very own agility courses? With an agility flag and orb, you can turn any situation - a family gathering, a funeral - into an obstacle course. Slap on some tight shorts, do some lunges, and feel the burn.

ZamorakianAcolyte.src:
Are you sure you want to be an acolyte? It's long hours, thankless, and the Staff of Subjugation will be constantly whipping your shins. People don't usually volunteer for the position. 

You'd be doing yourself a favour. The life expectancy of a demon summoner is longer than that of an acolyte. You might not even make it into your thirties.

Defence.src:
Armour will make life easier, reducing the damage you receive. The better the armour, the greater the damage reduction. Be sure to upgrade your gear at every opportunity. 

You may also want to avoid damage from time to time. A well-timed block will  parry the attack, negating all damage and staggering the enemy granting you a window to perform a visceral counterattack. While, if like me you prefer to avoid a knife in the stomach, you can always dodge an attack and get out of the way.

Perhaps the best way to protect one’s most precious internal organs, is to get out of the way of an attacker before they can stab you. Dodging is the key to this. Dash, roll and scream incoherently as you whiz away from an enemy’s attack before I can reach you. You can dodge in multiple directions, so make sure to keep an eye on your surroundings so you don't dodge off a cliff or anything. 

I did that once. Not fun.

HeartySoup.src: When Bramblemead villagers discovered heartier vegetables, their recipes improved just as much. The simple soup became richer, tastier and more filling. A nice, hearty meal to get them through the tough work on a farm.

AdamantLoggingAxe.src:
As the anima infused them more deeply, the trees of Ashenfall sought ways to create stronger defences against their hated foes – the lumberjacks. Yew trees, hardened after surviving the cruel rays of the sun, developed bark that would shatter lesser axes.

They felt invulnerable. Unbeatable. They could take the time to plan their war against the logging axes, so that they might rise up and strangle the world with their roots. Yet, the lumberjacks had a friend in the earth, and adamantite rose up to aid its allies.

The metal was harder than any before it, and the yew trees didn’t stand a chance, falling to the new weapons in droves.

WillowShortbow.src:
As the dead rose in greater and greater numbers, the villagers needed stronger weapons to defeat them. Their ash and oak longbows failed to unleash sufficient force needed to stem the relentless tide of the undead. They needed a stronger material, that was also flexible enough to deliver arrows of great enough force.

Willow was their solution. It is said that the first willow shortbow was gifted to a villager by a spirit that dwelled within the grove. Legends say that the spirit had an unnatural beauty, and would lure foolish villagers into the waters where they would be drowned. Yet, somehow, one villager earned not the spirits ire, but their admiration.

The spirit gave up their immortal life, to court the villager. They brought gifts of flowers, fish and finally they gifted a shortbow made from the willow trees in the spirits grove. The validity of this tale is hotly debated, with most assuming it is little more than myth, yet willow groves are still considered spiritual places, where one must be careful who they talk to.

DowdunReach.TheCathedral.src:
As the god of chaos and rebellion, you’d expect Zamorak to discourage churches, yet hypocrisy is chaos too, so he’s always pleased to see a temple in his name. Especially one with expensive windows, carefully crafted sculptures and an adoring army of priests, chanting his name.

One must have an ego to be a god, and Zamorak has more followers than most.

The priests of the Cathedral spend their days and nights in quiet contemplation… well they did, before everything went wrong. Now they wander the rooms muttering to themselves and hurling deadly spells at anyone who approaches.

Zamorak enjoys all this chaos just as much.

WitherReductionPotion.src:
As the hunger of Imaru spread across Fellhollow, it tore the souls of its victims from the bodies they had been previously so attached to. It was impossible to work out who would suffer the affliction next, and that created great unrest among the people, since their friends and family could become mindless undead at any moment.

The priests of Zamorak, surprisingly, were the first to discover a temporary solution, creating a potion infused with the rebellious nature of Zamorak. As Imaru attempted to draw the souls from the bodies of people, they would drink this and then she found this meal much harder to digest. The souls fought back against her hunger, locking themselves to their flesh with chains Zamorak would not have approved of.

The effects weren’t a permanent end to the problem, but they delayed the condition long enough for people to spot the signs and remove the problem from the Emberwood border. Infected villagers would be cast out of the protective barrier where they would face their fate alone.

SteelAxe.src:
As the war against the trees continues, more and more power weapons are needed to bring the bark-clad oppressors to their knees. As the wood hardens, preparing for attack, stronger materials are required to shatter their defences. 

Steel is a newer weapon in the lumberjack's arsenal. A sturdy metal, durable and strong, capable of felling the mighty willow strategists who whisper their deadly battleplans to the other trees. If the woodcutter army can destroy these wispy, willowy, strategists, they might yet turn the tables in this arboreal conflict.

Tiny.src: As with 90% of pets called Tiny, the 'Tiny' is ironic. She just thinks she's tiny, jumping onto Rexiton's lap when he hasn't even got the flame-retardant sheet ready.

SuperQuarrymasterPotion.src:
As with many physical activities, you can over-exert yourself when mining. Lactic acid builds up in the muscles, sweat clouds the vision and an accidental pickaxe swing can lodge in the head. A mining potion addresses all of these shortcomings. Lactic acid and sweat form slowly. The likelihood of accidents is reduced.

What it can't do is improve the quality or amount of ore. Pour it in your mouth or pour it on the deposit: it won't matter. No mining potion is going to help you there.

VisFibres.src:
Ashenfall is a fascinating experiment. It has largely developed on its own, away from the influences of the mainland. If people arrive on Ashenfall in great numbers, you can be sure that scientists will enjoy exploring how Ashenfall's independence has affected its wildlife, magic, geology and more. 

Those scientists will take particular glee in vis wax. On the mainland, it's thin, derived from runes and struggling to offer much value. Some wizards have used it to augment magical auras, but that's about it. On Ashenfall, though, the vis wax is thicker. So thick, in fact, that it can be concentrated and then spun into fibres. Fibres mean cloth, and cloth means magical armour. That gives it a combat use, and nothing excites a scientist more than military capability.

FocusedRunecraftingPotion.src:
Ashenfall is the birthplace of runecrafting. When Guthix settled here, he discovered the strange anima pouring out of the ground: different strands of magic resonating with certain concepts and natural laws.

This potion lets you see the world as he did, just for a while. You can spot the colourful flows of anima as they shimmer in the air, and you learn how to trap them in rune essence more effectively, creating the potential for future magic.

InspiringRingOfRunecrafting.Runecrafters.src:
Ashenfall was the first place that Guthix created runes, but he never passed those secrets on to his followers. It wasn’t until the legendary human, V, discovered the secret, that it was taught to the general population.

Still, something about Ashenfall makes the process easier. No altars are needed, nor talisman’s required, yet runes can be crafted with an abundance that would make the mainland guild’s jealous.

This ring taps into that ease, infusing the soul with some of that ancient knowledge of the island. Be careful sleeping with this on, as you may dream the memories of runecrafters past.

Or of a dog made of cheese. No one knows why.

Alric.src:
Ask the demons about Alric. There will be a pattern among the goading, lies and chaos to return. The demons believe that Alric has signed a pact with a foremost demon on Infernus. The contents of that pact are unknown, but it's fun to guess.

Alric has been alive for many centuries. That immortality could be tied to a demon pact. His abilities in the realm of demonology are also unparalleled: he can summon them at a rate that would make Bilrach weep. It makes sense that a pact would amplify this ability. 

There are far-fetched guesses that seem less likely. One posits that the "foremost demon" is, in fact, the god Zamorak. Demonic translation is an imperfect art, after all. That pact has kept Zamorak away from Ashenfall, so that Alric can claim it as his own. 

And the last is that Alric asked to be a demon himself. The immortality, the affinity to demons, the burgeoning power: all of these could be attributed to a centuries-long transformation. Even if it's untrue, it's a fascinating thought.

AstralRune.src: Astral runes borrow resonance from the stars, that silent hum when looking up at the night sky. They embody the power of distance and displacement, action from inaction, movement in the dark. Astral runes are used primarily in spells designed to summon an object to the caster’s location, making it a very popular rune with the lazier magicians.

CadavaberryInfusion.src:
At first glance you might just assume this is poison, for the cadavaberry is a dangerous fruit. Yet, with careful preparation, and an appropriate amount of boiling, the berry can become a sharp, yet not fatal addition to any dessert.

Mixed with water, it becomes an empowering infusion, that puts a sprint in your step. Partially because your body is reminded at just how close it came to death in drinking it, so makes the most of the life it has left.

SteelSword.src:
Atilius Rasmodel was a proud and powerful knight. Her skill with the sword was without compare and her bravery seemingly infinite against the dangers in Fellhollow. She was chosen by Imaru as one of her guards, not that a dragon needed such a thing, and she was made responsible for the defence of the dragons when they fell into the weeks long torpors they were known to suffer.

She called herself the Dragon Knight, even though such a title was unofficial and self-proclaimed, it soon stuck among the village people and they would bow and nod in appreciation of her skill as they passed her.

When Kuldra descended on the region, demanding humanity’s destruction, Atilius climbed on Xikotal’s back in hope to drive her steel blade through the Godeater’s heart. She died beside the dragon she had sworn to protect, free of all remorse, in the line of duty.

AvasAccumulator.src:
Ava is the apprentice to Dr Oddenstein, an eccentric scientist who lives in Draynor Manor, and a skilled inventor in her own right. She whiles away her limited free time by studying the lesser-known field of necroballistics, and creating strange and wonderful gizmos to further her studies. 

Perhaps her proudest achievement, is the invention of the attractor. By harnessing the energies of an undead chicken to the harmonic frequencies of a common bar magnet, her device can snatch grounded projectiles and bring them back to the quiver before they can be lost. This money saving experiment is not only great for hunters, but for anyone looking for an excuse to fill their enemies full of sharp sticks of wood. 

Always the generous sort, but one with little head for marketing, Ava has decided to pass on her genius invention to others. Rather than publishing a paper, or passing the methodology onto the Varrock library, she has instead written the instructions in a bottle and sent it adrift in the ocean for anyone to find. Fate, she believes, will draw it to where it is meant to go. Like magnets, probably.

AcensionShard.src:
Avisk was many things, arrogant, manipulative, cruel, but he was also a genius. Within the dreamscapes of the nightmare crucible, he found a way to reshape matter, reforging it into its ideal form. He took weapons and moulded them into stronger versions. He took a staff and re-imagined it stronger and more deadly. Using the stuff of nightmares, he found a limited way to reshape the world. We are, perhaps, fortunate that it was limited to such small scales. 

These shards are a part of that power. When combined with a fully realised core, they can upgrade legendary equipment into stronger versions of itself. A power we should hope Kuldra never finds.

AncestralStaff.src:
Avisk weighed the staff in his hands. The Kobalios he had killed lay on the ground beside him, deflating into a pool of anima. Like a waterskin purged of its contents, he thought.

The Kobalio's staff fascinated him greatly. He knew that he was standing here, holding it, in this chamber of the Wellspring. But he couldn't shake the sensation that he was somewhere else, too. There was two of him, somehow; one here, and one not here.

Avisk knew of a sensation called 'phantom limbs', where one could lose a limb, from an accident, perhaps, but still feel that the limb was present. It was an adequate description for what he was feeling now: except, he felt like his body was elsewhere, and he was its phantom mind.

Avisk dropped the staff and the sensation dropped with it. A grin spread across Avisk's face. Oh yes, this was a discovery that deserved some investigation.

Movement.src:
Back in my day movement was much more civilized, everyone worked in neat little squares, moving entire steps at a time. Yet modern adventurers feel a much greater need for precision, yearning to swap between tiny steps and enormous leaps.

Here on Ashenfall you can walk, run, jump and crouch around to your hearts content. Certain spells can also allow you to jump further, or even teleport short distances.

Efficient, yes, but it’s just not as elegant as the grid-like movement of my day.

Seeds.Avantoe.src:
Back on the mainland, the avantoe has a reputation for being a little high-maintenance. It only grows after a heavy bout of rainfall, and - even then - the bloom only lasts for a matter of hours. Get distracted, and you can miss the plant's entire life-cycle. Luckily, the climate and soil of Ashenfall means that the avantoe is less flighty than its mainland equivalent.
