You can see why avantoe is the perfect reagent for stamina and agility potions. It lives its short life at speed, and leaves something of itself behind that does the same for you. As in, it can boost your stamina rather than give you a short life.

Potato.src:
Baked, fried, mashed, there are few vegetables as versatile as the potato. Buried beneath the soil, these tubers absorb the nutrients around them, ready to be ripped from the soil and consumed.

Some mages noticed that you could pass certain magical currents through them, and one even attempted to enchant one and fashion it into blades. Suffice to say their plan was not successful, but it did create the very first chip, so was largely considered to be a good thing.

GreenCape.src: Be the envy of druids everywhere with this fabulous accessory.

MoltenGlass.src: Beautiful, yet hard to handle, the creation of molten glass was a turning point for Gielinorian civilization. It allowed the creation of vials, windows, and those pretty little animals that grandmothers love to collect and put on shelves.

FineThread.src: Because “corpse thread” is far too sinister a title, this thread is referred to as fine thread. It’s stronger, thinner and more malleable than cotton threads. The villagers of Emberwood enjoyed this thread in their clothing, creating garments that would suffer greater strain than their previous gear. Farmers were particularly fond of it.

BoneDagger.src:
Before he learned to use the bow, Ulv survived with simple daggers of bone. He lived outside the village, cast out for his silence and strange ways. Ulv did not follow the polite nonsense of human society, nor did he seem to care for their troubles. The boy was happy just to survive and whittle small carvings of animals from fallen branches. 

He hunted silently, using the daggers to slay small prey such as rabbits and chickens. He ate what he needed and sold the excess at the markets for enough coin to purchase simple clothes and tools. 

When he was thirteen, he was beaten by bandits and left for dead. But a Wild Knight found him and brought him to safety. Recovering in the knight’s home, Ulv would be taught how to use a bow, a skill he soon mastered. 

When a wolf attacked Bramblemead, this outcast slew it. Villagers thanked him for his bravery and asked him what he wanted as a reward. He refuted their offers and asked only for the wolf’s skull in return. He fashioned it into a mask that he chose as a new face, one he wore away from the village that had spurned him.

ScornedWilderness.RasthinsRest.src:
Before the cataclysm that shattered the region, Rasthin held a forum here for the other dragonkin to air their grievances. Mostly, it was an excuse for them to rant. They saw each other only every few years, if they could help it, and, when they got together, all they ever really did was complain.

In the times that Rasthin was left alone, she would cultivate a garden. She had seeds that had been preserved from worlds that existed before this universe came to be, and she dreamed of what they might look like in full bloom.

Alas, Rasthin was attuned to the flame, not the leaf, and one by one the plants ignited into embers and vanished into ash.

She should perhaps have seen it as a warning. Viika, after all, had warned her of impending doom and destruction, exclaiming how all her plans would end like the plants she so carefully cultivated. Yet, Rasthin never listened.

Like her garden, Rasthin is naught but ash, and all that remains of her legacy is embers.

MasterStaff.src:
Before the master wand, there was a staff of such power that the mages of the wizard’s tower decided it was too dangerous to keep. They placed the staff in teleportation circle, scrambled the coordinates and hurled it through the Abyss to settle far away from Misthalin.

In truth, it should have ended in the depths of the sea, sinking down and down into the darkness, but something caught it instead.

A powerful elven mage had found their way to Ashenfall, and they had already indulged in powers darker than what their kin traditionally allowed. They felt the staff hurtling through the Abyss and used their unnatural sorcery to pull it to them, so that they might benefit from its power.

This elf and his retinue found their way to the Umbral Sands, where they challenged one of the Moon Garou’s mages to a magical duel, over some perceived slight or other. The battle was magnificent, power that shook the dunes and cast a great sandstorm into the skies. The garou was defeated, but not before her spells shattered the master’s staff.

In his arrogance he cast the remains aside and continued his journey into Ashenfall.  Moon Garou would find the remnants of the staff and found a way to recreate it. Weaker than the original, true, but still possessing a power that would make lesser mages tremble.

BlackKnightBrute.src:
Being a Black Knight Brute wasn't just an acknowledgment of fortitude. Lord Rasmodel used them for tasks where conscience was a burden. 

They would be called upon for public executions when a message needed to be sent. They were always on call for demon outbreaks. Lastly, they would deal with extreme outbreaks of the madness. It was all too common for the voice-infected to move in chorus with the goal of killing indiscriminately. Brutes would quickly put a stop to them.

BlackKnightElite.src:
Being an Elite Black Knight wasn't just an acknowledgment of fortitude. Lord Rasmodel used them for tasks where conscience was a burden. 

They would be called upon for public executions, where a message needed to be sent. They were always on-call for demon outbreaks. Latterly, they would deal with extreme epidemics of the madness. It was all too common for the voice-infected to move together in a chorus, a large group whose aim was to kill indiscriminately. Elites would quickly put a stop to them.

BerryCompote.src: Berries and more berries, what could be better? A sweet and sour sensation in each mouthful. A refreshing, yet enjoyable meal. Well, more like a dessert, but no one’s judging you.

AdamantGreataxe.src:
Big axes are always popular among the violent crowd. In the Umbral Sands, a gathering of warrior Moon Garou gathered to show off who had the larger axe. Whilst the obvious innuendoes dogged the experience, in truth it was a competition among blacksmiths to see who could create the most powerful blade for the warriors to wield.

The adamant greataxe was created to showcase the raw power of the metal, and it was used with great zeal against a contingent of rampaging kalphites on hot summer. Seven warriors strode into the hive, axes held high and for the first time in a very long time, seven warriors emerged mostly unscathed.

Now, the greataxe is considered a good luck charm by any warrior Moon Garou who are strong enough to wield one.

BlackGreataxe.src: Black metal was most commonly used for armour, crossbows and swords. On occasion, it was used for a greataxe. The reason for this is not a pleasant one. Greataxes were almost exhaustively the tool of an executioner, when a crime merited a public execution. The black metal was a message: you have betrayed the Children of Shadows and your death will come from the metal of our own.

IronArmourHead.src:
Blacksmiths everywhere favour iron as a material to forge with. It is strong, durable, and malleable when hot and yet rigid when cool. It has been used to create weapons and unbreakable containers. Yet, it is most popular when turned into protection for those forced to ride into battle.

During the third age, the blacksmiths who travelled with the Saradominist priests brought the technique of iron to the people of Ashenfall. Previously relying on leather, bone and more easily extracted metals, the introduction of iron brought great change to the village's way of life.

They crafted more robust tools, mightier weapons and armour that practically erased the natural fear of heading into the woods. Only the Wild Knights opposed this new material, fearing its sudden popularity would impact the continent's ecosystem.

IronArmourLegs.src:
Blacksmiths everywhere favour iron as a material to forge with. It is strong, durable, and malleable when hot and yet rigid when cool. It has been used to create weapons and unbreakable containers. Yet, it is most popular when turned into protection for those forced to ride into battle.

From the outset, the search for iron ignited a fierce conflict between the humans and the Garou. Each incursion escalated the tension, pushing both sides perilously close to the brink of war. However, the situation reached a critical juncture when Bandos dispatched an emissary to the villagers of Brynmoor, offering a solution to their Garou predicament.

The Saradominist priests met with emissaries of Bandos and came to an alliance. The humans would claim the mines of Ghornfell, as long as Bandos could claim the head of the Garou goddess, Lougrim.
A win-win, as far as the priests were concerned.

IronArmourBody.src:
Blacksmiths everywhere favour iron as a material to forge with. It is strong, durable, and malleable when hot and yet rigid when cool. It has been used to create weapons and unbreakable containers. Yet, it is most popular when turned into protection for those forced to ride into battle.

The desire for iron was so strong in the village of Bramblemead that they exhausted all the iron deposits in Brynmoor. The Wild Knights cautioned them to look for more sustainable methods. Still, the villagers had become too accustomed to the luxury of iron.

Militia groups began to form to search Ghornfell for the precious metal ore. They marched in large groups, crushing plants beneath their metal heels and destroying whole areas of woodland in search of iron ore.

Their noise and bluster drew the ire of roving Garou, who saw the invasion of their forests as a violation of their treaties.

BlueDragonhide.src:
Blacksmiths hate this one simple trick. They spend their lives mastering interlocking chains and plates, only for dragons to be born with them. A third of the blacksmith's punters are now gone, hunting for dragons rather than dropping some coin at their forges. It's enough to make a blacksmith sob into their anvil. 

Blue dragons hate this one simple trick too, of course. Their Venn diagram overlaps with the blacksmith's: they'd rather people got their armour from somewhere other than dragons.

BloodwoodSap.src:
Bloodwood trees are a genuinely horrible creation. Their very existence a wound in the decency of the world, because this tree grows only in places steeped in violence and death.

The biggest bloodwood trees tower over battlefields. Sinewy spiderlike branches cast shade over the homes of serial killers, and you should never trust anyone that can grow one in their garden.

Leech-like roots soak up the suffering, sorrow and cruelty that has seeped into the soil, and then converts that misery into a sticky red sap of raw emotion. This sap can be used to amplify feelings, to convey anger, fear or hatred, across a much greater range.

The dragonkin Lacrussa was very fond of this medium, and used it’s power to shackle dragons to her will.

BluriteBar.src: Blue concentrated and refined, melted down and reforged into a cuboid shape so that you may carry around purest blue with you wherever you go.

BlueDragonDust.src:
Blue dragon dust is one of those things where you wonder who invented it and what curious sequence of events led up to it. Some unknown person had the wherewithal to strip a dragon of its scales, crush those scales in a pestle and mortar, then apply the resulting dust to a potion. Not only that, they downed said potion and stood in the path of a dragon. Does that not seem inexorably mad to you? 

But thank you, inexorably mad person, because now we have this potent ingredient which can protect a person from dragonfire. You have been forgotten in time, but your blue dusty legacy lives on.

BlueDragonHatchlings.src:
Blue dragon hatchlings are mercurial things. Their lives are filled with a whimsical desire to cause destruction and chaos. Among dragonkind, they favour elaborate pranks, such as collapsing a cave roof on their siblings. For anyone else, however, their mischief turns to malice and they seek nothing but to rend and rip and reduce their target to naught but bubbling pools of viscera.

All in all, not the nicest creatures.

BlueDragonhideCowl.src:
Blue dragons are not native to Dowdun Reach. Blue dragons are not native anywhere. They are the creations of the dragonkin, and this particular strain is Lacrussa's work. Lacrussa did not consider them a failure, but she did not consider them a success, either. They were a means to an end and, as such, she let them rest in Dowdun Reach.

Avisk initially had no use for them. His focus was on lower species, humans and the like. He saw room within human minds to crawl and make them his own. Their consciousness was a hall of prisms, and he could turn them all so that they focused on him. The human mind reflected back his narcissism. 

To Avisk, the blue dragons were nuisances, liable to kill his test subjects while he was distracted. He penned them in and forgot about them, cursing Lacrussa for letting them stray into his domain. Their number grew, but Avisk tutted and continued his work.

BlueDragonhideChaps.src:
Blue dragons are not native to Dowdun Reach. Blue dragons are not native anywhere. They are the creation of the dragonkin, and this particular strain is Lacrussa's work. Lacrussa did not consider them a failure, but she did not consider them a success, either. They were a means to an end and, as such, she let them rest in Dowdun Reach.

Avisk manoeuvred the multi-faceted prism within the blue dragon's mind. He observed it using his mastery of air, but no permutation would focus the blue dragon's thoughts, no orientation would align the chaos. He resolved to break parts of that giant stone, but its power was diminished with each snap and shatter. He crumpled to the floor of the blue dragon's mind-space in frustration. 

The breakthrough was borne from that frustration. Just as he would move into the consciousness of a living being, he moved into the consciousness of the stone. Perhaps he forgot where he was. Against all his expectations, he was able to step into the stone itself, as if it itself had a consciousness. There was a second layer to the blue dragon's mind.

It is impossible to comprehend what Avisk saw there. But he was forever changed. He no longer cared for healing the blue dragons of their crystalline blockage, of restoring them to sapient thought. Instead, he wished to recreate the prism, the crystal, in the corporeal world.

BlueDragonhideBody.src:
Blue dragons are not native to Dowdun Reach. Blue dragons are not native anywhere. They are the creation of the dragonkin, and this particular strain is Lacrussa's work. Lacrussa did not consider them a failure, but she did not consider them a success, either. They were a means to an end and, as such, she let them rest in Dowdun Reach.

Rasthin changed everything. She came to Avisk with a gift: "Jas Moksha", in the tongue of the kin. It was a device that imbued Avisk with the element of air. Avisk accepted the gift politely. Rasthin could have overpowered him with ease. He played supplicant and took the gift, hoping that it wasn't a trap or curse.

That disdain shifted once Avisk realised that the powers were not limited to the material realm. He could move with alacrity, purpose and strength in the minds of others. Minds that were once closed to him blossomed like a flower. He dabbled with ogres and then moved on to blue dragons.

Within the minds of blue dragons, he found a secret. There was a blockage – a multi-faceted prism – that kept their potential at bay. It redirected their thoughts in wild directions, made them unruly. It seemed that their animalistic nature was a product of mental hindrances, rather than physical. With his new powers, he could solve a problem that had frustrated Lacrussa for centuries.

Boggs.src: Boggs would like to sit on your head and pull your hair so that you make HELL-RATATOUILLE.

FerociousInfusion.src: Boiling away the tainted material in water, while infusing it with an animal bone, causes the mixture to draw in some of the primal resonance of the bone. Drinking the infusion temporarily allows the drinker to feel some of that animalistic ferocity.

CleanWater.src: Boiling water separates out the tainted elements present in the liquid, allowing you to scrape them off and enjoy a more pleasant beverage.

WoolenCloth.src: Bolts of durable woolen cloth, popular with mages and anyone that likes a little thermal insulation in their armour.

LinenCloth.src: Bolts of sturdy linen cloth, excellent for crafting magical armour with.

AnimalBones.src: Bones are not just the favoured materials of necromancers, they can be incredibly useful to a skilled survivalist as well. Designed to withstand great force, while still being as light as possible, bones make excellent components in an array of crafting recipes.

GhornfellHighlands.src:
Bones of ancient wyrms litter this region. Gargantuan dragons that are now mercifully dead. Forged by the mad science of the dragonkin Lacrussa, these titans could well have ended the god wars themselves. Fortunately, none still live in this region.

A great storm rages across the region, the result of desperate sorcery in a long drawn-out war. The thunder here is hateful and spiteful, striking any that walk the land, as if driven by the vengeful fury of its long-dead caster.

Watching over the Highlands stands a great monument to a fallen garou monarch. A king who challenged impossible foes. A lasting memory of the garou people, hewn out of stone.

The garou here are well trained and merciless, seeking nothing but the death of all who dare step foot in these sacred lands.

RawTrout.src: Bonier than some of the other popular fish, the trout is nevertheless one of the most regularly consumed freshwater fish. Its flavour is heavily influenced by its diet… which, on Ashenfall, is more than a little worrying if I’m honest.

DragonCrossbow.src:
Brakka presented the cache of weapons to the other dragonkin. For himself he chose the kiteshield: he didn't care much for combat, and he felt a strange kinship with its resilience.

Avisk chose a scimitar with a growl. He turned the metal in his hands and licked it. Brakka knew Avisk well enough that Avisk would be more interested in the material and its properties for his studies. Avisk chose the scimitar simply because it contained the greatest weight of the metal.

Rasthin was next and chose a crossbow and some bolts. She walked immediately to her workbench and began exposing the metal to the elements. She lit a bolt on fire and seemed satisfied that the fire failed to extinguish.

Lacrussa took a kiteshield. She tossed it to the corner, disinterested with these trinkets.

Brakka didn't know what to expect from Viika. He wondered whether they would turn down the gift, perhaps, or pick a kiteshield - something of a more pacifist bent.

Viika picked the dragon crossbow. "I know someone who will have need of this," they said.

FracturedCape.src:
Brakka’s hubris was a marvel to behold, perhaps more impressive than any monument of his construction. When Rasthin shared with him the elemental power she had wrung from Ashenfall’s mysterious vents, Brakka became a master of the earth itself.

With the power to shape stone and soil, by will alone, Brakka could have created great villages. He could have constructed aqueducts and watermills that could brought Ashenfall into a new, golden age. Instead, he made a tower.

A single tower that rose as far as the eye could see. Forged through his own power, and the blood, sweat and tears of garou slaves. It is, perhaps, fitting, that this is where he died. Kuldra, the godeater, crushed him beneath her great claw and feasted on his anima-rich soul. Stealing Brakka’s power for herself.

She gifted Velgar, her most trusted general, with the elemental mastery of the fallen Nodon architect, and, to mock the dragonkin further, Velgar took Brakka’s monument as his new lair.

Now the tower stands for all to see, as a reminder of dragonkin hubris, and rightfully deserves its new moniker; Brakka’s folly.

BramblemeadValley.src:
Bramblemead valley is home to the village of its namesake, a once tranquil location bustling with life. It was founded in the first age by the god Guthix and his followers, and converted to the worship of Saradomin sometime in the third age.

The Keep of Blue Flames, was built in the popular style of the Saradominist faithful. The ordered shape a symbol of the god of order’s will. Powdered metals were cast into the braziers, so that the flames would burn in the hue favoured by Saradomin. Here the lord of the region would watch over the village and surrounding areas, under the careful guidance of the high priest of the church.

To the northwest stands a symbol of mankind’s thirst for knowledge, a great guild dedicated to uncovering the secrets of the runes that had been first discovered on Ashenfall by Guthix himself. Here, powerful wizards learned spells and enchantments, pushing the boundaries of mankind’s knowledge.

Ashenfall is rife with danger and the need for heroes has always been strong. A guild was created, to the east of Brynmoor, where heroes and champions would gather together to seek out the deadliest monsters and slay them where they stood.

Once this valley was the hub of human activity, but now it sits silent, and overrun with monsters. Goblins spread across the region claiming it in the name of their new god. Rats swarm through the ruins with sharp and deadly fangs. Soil that was once fertile farmland, is now soaked to the roots in blood.

VeggieSandwich.src:
Brassica Prime approves of this sandwich.

Although, the mushrooms are a little much: they could probably have been thinned out. Maybe removed? Yes, remove them. The bread, too. Is it needed? Would you perhaps consider removing the envelope of bread that houses the sweet cabbage missive? Your dribbly jowls will thank us.

FriedCabbage.src:
Brassica Prime – the god of cabbages – gifted the world with this delicious vegetable, to lead the faithful on the noble path of nutrition. In his infinite, leafy, wisdom, he taught the early settlers about how one might fry the leaves, so that they would be even more delicious.

Now these fried cabbages offer those who consume them, the strength and stamina needed to brave the hardships of Ashenfall.

MysticNet.src:
Brassica on a Bullock, that net is garish. You're not going to lose that, are you? I bet that your eyes lock onto it every time you open your inventory. First thing you see. Boom – MYSTIC NET.

It has the same effect on marine life, of course. They're merrily swimming about, doing whatever lobster and shrimp do, and then boom – MYSTIC NET. Not much they can do, is there? They're transfixed, drawn in by the brightest of blue colours, like moths to a mirror ball. 

Which explains why the mystic net is rather formidable as a net. Not the most fashionable, mind.

BoneArrowBroadhead.src:
Broadhead arrows are more dangerous than their standard counterparts. The tip is like a razor blade designed to make the target bleed. It was a favourite of the Children of Shadows, especially when turned on their White Knight opponents. 

One such cultist, a woman known only as The Athame, would hunt down priests using the arrows to bloodlet them before going in for the kill. She delighted in watching them run as they bled, only to chase them into a quiet corner and end their life at the edge of a blade. 

She was an aberration in the cult. Most members treated it as little more than a social club, and few actually enjoyed the Zamorakian ideal. But the Athame lived for chaos. 

She was never caught.

BronzeArrow.src:
Bronze arrows offer greater armour piercing than their non-metallic counterparts. Copper and tin were relatively uncommon in Brynmoor, so using the resources on arrows seemed like a waste of money. One faction of bandits delighted in this premise; their leader, a man known as the Auburn Ocelot—for reasons he would never explain—took great amusement in their use. 

The Auburn Ocelot would laugh as his bandits hurled expensive arrows at the villagers, pilfering coins worth far less than the ammunition used to corral them. To him, it wasn’t about the money but the look of confused terror on their faces and the knowledge that no one could stop him. 

He was above it all. Better than everyone. 

It was a rat that killed him. Not even a giant one. Just a tiny creature carrying a virulent plague. Money could not save him, no matter how much he flaunted it. He was cremated, and his ashes buried in the middle of nowhere so that no one might risk catching the infection that cost his life. 

Now, he’s almost completely forgotten.

BronzeDagger.src:
Bronze is a common enough alloy, a combination of copper and tin. Durable, defiant, and deadly in the right hands. For Mia Larsdottir, it was a bronze dagger that pierced her heart, cutting her life short at the age of twenty-one. 

As the first of the Amalgamated, she had never expected to reach any of the milestones her peers traditionally followed. She did not expect to be married, and she never let herself dream of being a mother. She thought, perhaps, that she might be allowed to carve a quiet little place for herself, somewhere with room for cats. 

But a bronze dagger stole that dream from her. 

Her killer was never brought to justice, though there were rumours about who they were. Her father, being the chief suspect, ashamed as he was to bring the first of the unnatural Amalgamated into the world. He denied it, of course, but he never held a funeral for her. Instead, her body was left in the forest, where nature might put her at peace.

BronzeArmourLegs.src:
Bronze was once a secret held by the ancient dwarves. It is a more robust metal forged from an alliance of two others. 

As the Saradomin faith became more popular, the bronze-clad inquisition enforced Saradomin’s laws, even when they conflicted with the Guthixian faith. It was a slow change, but they went from clearing shrines of monsters to clearing shrines of the Guthixian heresy. 

When the druids finally rebelled, the bronze-clad enforcers were called against them, not the White Knights. The cruel irony of being arrested by the force created to protect them.

BronzeArmourBody.src:
Bronze was once a secret held by the ancient dwarves. It is a more robust metal forged from an alliance of two others. 

The alliance of two different faiths had its own warrior force to defend its shared ideals. Clad in polished bronze armour, these warriors stood out against the stark green of Brynmoor’s fields. They upheld traditions and punished those who blasphemed against either faith. 

The bronze advisors, as they were known, would offer advice from both a Saraodminist and a Guthixian viewpoint—order and balance side by side. Such was the intention, but the scales were already tipped. Policies began to slip more and more in favour of the Saradominist approach until the Guthixian faith slowly dwindled as the Saradominist view took centre stage.

BronzeArmourHead.src:
Bronze was once a secret held by the ancient dwarves. It is a more robust metal forged from an alliance of two others. 

This union of metals was often used as a symbol of cooperation. Alliances would store the signed documents in bronze scroll cases or sign them with a pen made of tin and another of copper. 

On Ashenfall, it was used to show that the old ways could stand beside the new. For a while, in the third age, druids wore pins of copper, and the Saradominist priests wore tin pins. They would then stand together, side by side, in village council meetings, a promise that neither one stood stronger than the other.

IronMedHelm.src:
Bronze, it's so last region, isn't it? It's weak, it's gaudy. Why, you can do so much better than that. Iron, that's the future: a ferromagnetic cage around your cranium is guaranteed to prevent almost some damage to your squishy brain. 

Strangely, none of the residents of Brynmoor wore medium helms: they all went straight for full helms. Probably because they wanted to protect their face from deadly weapons, the cowards.

SplitbarkWand.src:
Brynmoor's School of Magic was little more than scattered rubble. There is very little as flammable as a wizards' school, thick as it is with books, potions and staves.

Rescue parties saved who and what they could, but seven casualties were tallied. They were mostly wizards whose luck had run out, who were practicing spells that left them incapacitated. They were in the midst of astral projection or alterations of the mind when the fire swept through.

Under the rubble, however, the rescue parties found something unusual. There was a room that wasn't on any plans, located beneath Arnuld's Sanctum. It wasn't particularly large: only a handful of wizards could have stood upright within it. But in that room was a plaque, lacquered to protect it from fire. On it was written "You have passed my trial. I have underestimated my fellow wizards. Take what is earned - Holly Arnuld".

On the walls, around the plaque, was row upon row of wands. Splitbark and maple wands in their hundreds.

CourseAnimalFur.src: Bundles of animal fur, scratchy and thick. While not an ideal trait on pets, this sort of coarse fur has a multitude of uses in the wild.

WeakFocusedAgilityPotion.src: Buy a potion from your local apothecary and they'll give you a warning. Drinking an agility potion will make you more nimble, sure, but your brain will be working on old information. You will think you're reaching for a bowl of cookies, only to find that you've over-exerted and done a front-flip over them.

GroundClay.src: By grinding clay down into powder, you can create a much smoother medium for crafting. The grinding process gets rid of various impurities and allows for more resilient results.

DesertThread.src: By spinning desert weed into useful fibres, you can create yourself a nice bundle of desert thread. This thread is useful for all manner of tailoring enterprises.

SkeletalArcher.src:
By the time you’ve heard their creaking bones, it’s already too late. Despite their lack of sinew, sensory organs, or anything that should make them this dead, the skeletal archer is surprisingly deft.

In life they were scouts, hunters or Wild Knight archers, in death they’re simply something best avoided.

BarrelCactus.src: Cacti survive the desert by collecting as much moisture as possible and hoarding it like greedy little dragons. Slice them to pieces and claim the delicious juices for yourself! It’s nature’s way.

NecromancerRobeTop.src:
Callius Waithe created an army of the undead and marched them on Emberwood. Or, rather, he called his shambling little horde an army, even though it consisted only of five skeletons in various degrees of disrepair.

The village guard took aim at the skeletons, but their arrows lacked the strength to shatter bone, and Callius marched them through the gates with barely any opposition. Still, once he had made it through, he was not met with the terror he had hoped for. While shambling skeletons were certainly a fright that caused much shock, their limited number helped mitigate the terror.

A small child even giggled and tried to offer one skeleton an apple. An act that filled Callius with unreasonable rage.

AdventurersCape.src:
Capes are stylish and protect against the weather. They can be elaborate symbols of stature, or simple cloth to act as a ward against the cold. This cape is the latter.

Simple, elegant, and functional. Worn by adventurers and explorers across Gielinor’s mainland and beyond.

After the dragon attack, there are few of these capes worn on Ashenfall. The rest sink beneath the ocean waves, are torn to pieces on the cliff rocks, or have long since burned to ash beneath draconic hate.

ZombieAxe.src:
Captain Artorius Flamhanger was a brave man, who stood against the rampaging forces of the damned even as his defences crumbled around him. He never wavered, never faltered, and he never left a man behind.

In a better world, there would be songs about him. But Fellhollow scorns legacy, leaving only ruin and despair where hope might take root.

He held the line against the encroaching horde far longer than anywhere else in the region. Days turned into months and months grew into years. As the rest of the region vanished into death, despair and rot, Captain Flamhanger stood strong. As his children died and rose again, the captain returned them to the earth with sombre compassion. When his wife joined them in death, he gave her a final kiss of polished silver that cleaved her head from her shoulders.

In a better world he might have held back the darkness, stood as the single ray of light in a world of shadow. But this is not our world.

There are no sagas of this man. No great texts telling of his heroic deeds. The only sound he made in the time after his death, is the bubbling song of digestive acids within a zogre’s belly.

History is penned by the survivors and the victors, yet the deeds of the dead echo across time. This axe, simple as it may appear, is infused with vengeance against the dead that had taken so much from  a good man.

Cathan.src:
Cathan would be the first to tell you that he was raised in privilege. Wealthy family. Loving parents. Everything a growing boy could need. Yet, like for so many of us, it wasn’t enough. He craved excitement, exploration and adventure, yearning more than anything to discover the wonders of the world. 

As a child he slipped away from his family, in search of adventure and monsters to slay. He found more than he bargained for, and the lesson for his hubris cost him a leg. 

In the months that followed, the boy fell into a deep darkness. Life offered little meaning, when he could barely walk a few steps. His parents hired him a tutor, so that he might rekindle that spark of adventure that had once burned so bright. 

It worked. In Vannaka, he found someone who dragged him out of his melancholy, who taught him how to wield a blade and exploit his foes' weaknesses. Vannaka brought in others, who helped train him further. From Zanik, young Cathan learned how to survive in the wilds. From Doric, he learned to craft weapons and armour to fell his foes. Finally, the Wise Old Man taught him a little bit of magic, and young Cathan’s curious excitement burned bright once more. 

When the opportunity came to explore a new land, Cathan was the first to sign up and convinced his mentors to join him. As they sailed to Ashenfall, he stood at the bow of the ship, smiling at the adventures ahead. 

In the chaos that followed, he became keenly aware of the age-old saying, “Be careful what you wish for.”

HerbBakedTrout.src: Cathan was known for his love of herbed baked trout. He would often claim it was, "the best thing you could do with a 'tater". That was until Vannaka picked up a potato, threw it halfway across Temple Woods and knocked the party hat off of Dionysius' head. Cathan subsequently admitted that herbed baked trout was, "the second-best thing you could do with a 'tater".

SummoningHorn.src:
Cathan’s challenge horn design is a collection of materials hastily thrown together. A dragon’s tooth, carved with dragonkin sigils as well as metal wires used to connect them together –  like a spiderweb lattice, glistening with traces of magical power.

When placed in the dragonkin altar, the horn acts as a focus point for the magical power stored within the tower, sending an invisible beacon off into the air, in a perfect draconic pitch.

Velgar has been summoned many times before. By heroes, kings, warriors and gods, and yet still the tower stands.

Be ready, when you send out the call.

StormtouchedCape.src:
Centuries ago, a spell was cast over the Highlands that changed it forever. Once temperate skies became pendulous clouds filled with lightning. Electric hate that strikes at anything and everything that dares step beneath their gaze.

War changes everything, even the sky.

The land itself is strewn with the dead. Ancient skeletons of colossal wyrms, the monstrous creations of dragonkin science, lie across the terrain, dead eyes watching over everything. Lacrussa considered these monstrosities her finest work. Yet she shed no tears at their destruction. She could always make more, or so she believed.

It was a lone girl, a necromancer of great power, who turned the sky into a curse. A last act of vengeance for a fallen friend. She dug into forbidden magic, drawing power from the countless dead slain in constant conflict. The garou, lords of this region, were not prepared for the power of grief, for it was a concept alien to their primordial nature.

These stories weave into the threads of this cape, barely remembered, yet never quite forgotten.

BlackKnightGuardian.src:
Chaos is an attractive philosophy until you're the one organising guard and patrol rotations. Chaos gains a little asterisk: you need a little organisation to facilitate the chaos. 

Those on guard rotation know that threats are just as likely to come from within than without. For this reason, veterans would advise newer knights to glue a mirror to the back of their shield.

Snapdragon.src: Children are often disappointed that this plant does not resemble an actual dragon. There are no snapping motions in these colourful leaves, and a depressing lack of firebreathing lizards in the stems.

ClayDeposit.src: Clay can be found in deposits around Ashenfall and can be recovered with just a few pickaxe swings. It is said that the Elder God created the universe out of clay, albeit of a more interesting vintage, and the unwanted remains hurled into the abyss. The truth of this claim is hard to establish as the Elder Gods are rarely prone to a friendly chat. Not least because, were you to hear them speak, your head would explode. This makes conversation tricky.

WhiteCape.src: Cleanliness is next to godliness, so some of the white knights claimed. Live your bleached dreams with this immaculate accessory.

GroundLimestone.src:
Clearly, all limestone is ground limestone, as it comes from the ground. In many places it IS the ground. But this is specifically limestone that has been ground down into a dust. 

Ground limestone's primary use is in glassblowing. Should you have the crafting capability and a healthy, strong puff, you can use ground limestone to make molten glass and then produce glass.

BlackSniperCrossbow.src:
Climb the turrets of Dowdun Reach in its prime and you would have found the Black Knight Snipers. These were the elite marksmen of the Black Knights, tasked with looking outward while the rest of the order looked inward. They would scan the skyline for threats – for the beating wings of a dragon. There was no greater trophy for the Black Snipers.

On one occasion, a bolt was loosed at Imaru. She had travelled to the keep on a diplomatic mission, and was rewarded with a bolt to the neck. You could see the conflict within her, as she swallowed her urges. For a second, a disdainful eye moved to the Black Sniper. But she reset and continued to talk to Lord Rasmodel and Alric like nothing had happened.

Restraint was certainly beaten into the Black Snipers that night.

Coal.src:
Coal is the petrified memory of a long dead ecosystem. Plants and animals, who lived countless aeons ago, crushed down into rocks of rigid carbon and becoming a powerful fuel that changes civilisations.

When you burn the coal, imagine the worlds that came before and the lives forgotten. Let each piece become a funeral pyre for a long-lost age.

Or enjoy shiny new steel armour, your call!

DemonicOil.src:
Combine corrupt bonemeal and vile ashes and the result is demonic oil. We should be specific about what kind of oil this is: please do no pour it into a frying pan or use it on a squeaky hinge. This is potent oil, as the "demonic" prefix will attest. It is used for crafting, and solely for crafting.

Now you've got us wondering what would happen if you did actually add it to a frying pan or a squeaky hinge. Obviously, please don't do it. But if you do happen to do it, through an accident or momentary lack of wisdom, could you let us know what happens?

BlackMetalBar.src:
Congratulations on killing enough Black Knights to forge a bar from the resulting scraps. Don't think about the children you have orphaned or the dreams that you have impaled on the sharp end of a greatsword. Don't think about the concentrated misery you hold in your hands. 

It is rather shiny, though, is it not? Black metal, particularly if you have the draconic sort (more chromatic, less matte), is mesmerising.

AgilitySkillcape.src:
Congratulations! Like the nimblest of ferrets, you can scoot up drainpipes and scurry across ledges.

Now you have mastered the Agility skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the rank of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

PristineMonkfish.src: Congratulations! Of all the monkfish in the world, you have come across possibly the most dapper. You may wish to spend some time forging a monocle, to really tie the look together. That is, of course, one of those things that is funny to write in a journal like this, but will lead to disappointment and frustration if you actually try it in game.

CookingSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! There is no flavour you have not found, no edible you have not eaten.

Now you have mastered the Cooking skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

RangedSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! They say that you can split a garou's whisker from a thousand paces.

Now you have mastered the Ranged skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

WoodcuttingSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! Trees tell stories about you to their saplings. "Fear the Tree Killer".

Now you have mastered the Woodcutting skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done.

AttackSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! While you may have 99 problems, Attack isn't one of them. 

Now you have mastered the Attack skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill. 

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

ConstructionSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! You can look upon your constructions and see that they are good.

Now you have mastered the Construction skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

FarmingSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! You could grow seeds in lava, saplings in ice and bulbs in the neck folds of a golem.

Now you have mastered the Farming skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

MagicSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! You could pull a hat from a rabbit, you're that magical.

Now you have mastered the Magic skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

ArtisanSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! You're a Master Maker, a Crafting Connoisseur, an Artisan Fartisan.

Now you have mastered the Artisan skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

FishingSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! You're a fishing colossus, conquering rivers and seas with nowt but a net and rod.

Now you have mastered the Fishing skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

RunecraftingSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! You've crafted more runes than a roomful of crafty runecrafters.

Now you have mastered the skill of Runecrafting, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

MiningSkillcape.src:
Congratulations! Your veins are glittering ore; your eyes are diamonds; your deposits are clumps of rock.

Now you have mastered the Mining skill, what will you do next? You could trim your cape, of course. Or you could rise up the ranks of another skill.

For now, take a moment. Enjoy the satisfaction of a completed skill. Well done!

DowdunReachCapeGolden.src: Considering that Black Knights are some of the least nimble warriors in all of Ashenfall (it's the clunky black armour), you might be the most agile person to set foot in the Reach. Congratulations!

Swingslash.src:
Contrary to popular belief, a goblin is as smart as any other species. It was Bandos that instilled within them the notion that intelligence is a sin, and that demonstrating your education is something to be discouraged. As a result, goblins often go out of their way to make themselves seem less intelligent than they really are.

Hence Swingslash – the name given to this axe because of how it swings through the air, slashing anything it hits. It’s so reductive and silly, it can only be an overcorrection, a desperate attempt by the creator to seem dumber than they are.

The name encourages you to ignore the curve of the blade and the sharpness of the edge, created by carefully thought-out techniques that make the weapon deadlier than those that came before. The name, so chosen by the blacksmith so none might accuse them of the crime of being smart.

NatureRune.src: Contrary to popular belief, the nature rune does not solely govern plants, roots and the natural world. That is only part of its design. Instead, nature is about the connection of things, threading together the way things could be, rewriting them to a state more desirable. Favoured by wizard’s for their ability to adjust the flow of time to an entity, dragging it back to a point when it was in a more preferable state.

DowdunReach.TheGrandLibrary.src:
Contrary to the name, this isn’t just a great big corridor. Indeed, this is the place where the knights would gather to discuss battle tactics, hold religious debates and unleash exceedingly angry chickens upon the new recruits.

We have tried to work out what the point of the chickens was, but so far the historical documents have been annoyingly sparse on answers.

BraisedCatfish.src:
Cooking braised catfish is no mean feat. The process involves removing the armoured shell while managing to avoid the nerve-endings that, once severed, can release a poison that is fatal to humans. Then a chef needs to achieve precisely the right temperature to neutralise the latent poison without – again – activating it. 

Of course, if you want fewer friends, braised catfish is easy as pie to cook.

InspiringRingOfCooking.ChefsRing.src:
Cooking is a form of magic that few people truly master. Meals can return lost memories, shatter dour moods and rekindle friendships long since abandoned.

This ring was created by accident, when a parent was trying to teach a child how to cook. They were holding the unfinished piece, absent-mindedly, as they explained to their progeny about all the steps needed to understand a recipe.

This knowledge, infused with the emotion of a parents instruction, enchanted the ring so that all future wearers might benefit from their knowledge.

BronzePickaxe.src:
Copper and tin conspire well together, forging an alliance to destroy their former friends. The bronze pickaxe can shatter the mightiest stones and can mine through more durable ore than bone and stone could ever dream to battle.

The dwarves that Guthix brought with him to Ashenfall, were fond of the bronze pickaxe. While iron and steel are sturdier, the bronze pickaxe was more readily available, and they could risk a little decoration. Many would customise their pickaxes with symbols of their family crests, or a nickname that embodied them well. Often these would make the pickaxe impractical, yet they became a popular heirloom handed down between family members.

CactusSteak.src: Cows are fans of these, because it’s a steak that isn’t made of them.

SodaAsh.src: Created by burning plants with a high salt content, such as swamp weed and other marine plants, this powder if a vital part of glassmaking. When mixed with ground sandstone and charcoal, it creates the alchemical reactions that allows the creation of molten glass.

VeganFryUp.src: Crisp and delicious vegetables, neatly fried mushrooms, there are few breakfasts quite as delicious as a fry up, even for those who abjure bacon.

CrystalBow.src:
Crystal bows are not crafted but sung into existence. Harmonies are layered over one another to teach the weapon a story so that it might understand why it needs to be strong. Traditionally, the plight of the elves, their loneliness without their goddess, and the many dangers they must face are sung. 

The shimmering substance they’re made from is traditionally a shard of the elven goddess Seren, left behind when her crystal form shattered at the end of the Third Age God Wars. 

This bow isn’t the same material, and the song is different, too. There’s no divine essence in the crystal, no lament of the elves. Instead, it is sung memories of a lifetime together, distilled down into facets reflecting in the crystalline flaws. In the moonlight, those facets sparkle like tiny stars held within glass—moments of hardship, conflict, happiness, and grief. 

It is music as a weapon, with memory as the handle and sorrow as the string.

Curly.src: Curly resents being called curly. Her hair merely bends back towards her body because she is SO HELLISHLY ALLURING.

GarouChits.src:
Currency is a relatively new concept for the garou who, through most of their history, relied on a barter system based around hunting. As the Moon Garou settled into less hectic lives, they needed a means of trade that everyone had access to, and so created the chits to do so.

These chits are formed from tiny scraps of adamantite, melted down and then stamped with the branding of the tribes. A fun fact about them is that both sides have garou heads on them, one male and one female, so you can flip as many heads in a row as you want.

CursedEssence.src:
Cursed essence is a magical agent often used in tanning. It is also something of a curiosity, one that a simple tanner can't readily explain. It goes further than simply binding itself to material; it latches onto it, almost parasitically. 

Demonologists have a theory that, although cursed essence drops from the avernic demons of Dowdun Reach, it is actually cthonic in nature. It would explain the tendril-like tenacity.

AdamantShovel.src:
DAMN IT MAN, CAN'T YOU SEE THAT I AM A SPADE?

I give you: an adamant spade. 

Do you get it? You get it, right? Don't make us dig a hole and hide in shame.

FireBronzeArrows.src:
Deadly arrows made deadlier with fire. Each arrow burns with the fury reserved for the most unpleasant parts of Infernus. They sear, they singe, and they melt the flesh, turning their victim into little more than ashes floating away on the wind.

In the days of the great war against the Garou, the priests of Saradomin encouraged the use of these weapons. They saw it not just as a means of eradicating the hated beastmen, but to purify the world from their taint. Lougrim was a false goddess, in their eyes, and her followers had to be cleansed from existence.

Modern scholars would doubtless be confused at their monotheistic mindset, considering that the literal god of war, Bandos, walked beside them into battle. The mental gymnastics employed by the Brynmoor priesthood, could have rivalled any athlete in the Gielinor Games.

CadavaberryBush.src: Deadly, poisonous berries. Delicious deadly berries.

DowdunReach.TheCrypt.src:
Death doesn’t seem as inevitable in Ashenfall as it does everywhere else. Even here, in Dowdun Reach, the knights and mages seem to have forgotten about limited human lifespans, and persist through the centuries in a deranged sort of haze. This leaves the crypts beneath the keep largely forgotten, the perfect hideaway for demons and the dead.

There are many Zamorakian heroes that rest within the stone of the crypt. Powerful mages, mighty warriors and clever tacticians alike. There are chaos poets, and shadow writers, each bringing art into the faith, because art is rebellion and Zamorak was always fond of that.

Now, however, the dead rise form their graves, animated by the lingering magic of the shattered Dreaming Stone and the remnants of strange sorceries that imbue everything with a strange sort of power.

Tread lightly through these halls, for those that dwell within are very light sleepers.

DriedDwellberries.src: Delicious berries. They make a great snack. Very popular among garou druids as a seasoning for their latest quarry.

RedberryGlazedRoastMeat.src: Delicious roasted meat, with a redberry glaze. The fruit flavour combines with the meat in a sublime manner that makes it hard to eat this slowly.

MithrilCrossbowBolts.src: Demons are hardy creatures. The Black Knights had a habit of calling them "Rackers", as they'd often require a whole bolt rack to bring down.

BarbedMithrilArrows.src:
Demons dealt with wounds and ailments on their own. There was no such thing as a demon surgeon or sick bay. If wounds were fatal, then the demon would die; if wounds were survivable, then survive they did. 

This was an observation of Summoner Flament, who passed it on to Alric, who idly mentioned it to Lord Rasmodel in one of their weekly meetings. As with most information, Lord Rasmodel examined it for opportunities.

If demons sought no help for their wounds – no remedies, no medical assistance – then his knights would carry weapons that took advantage of that. Arrows were poisoned, since no demon carried antipoison. And arrows were barbed, as demons would pull them roughly from their hides, rather than remove them carefully. 

It was a small advantage, but Lord Rasmodel took it. As he would often say, "stack opportunities, one on top of the other, and soon you will have an impregnable tower."

VileAshes.src:
Demons do not leave bones behind on death. That would require a skeleton, a prospect that would make a demon queasy. Instead, demons are magical entities, composed of essence and energies. On death, they disperse, leaving behind an ashy composite.

Don't be mistaken in thinking that it's similar to the ash left after a fire. Dab your tongue in Vile Ash and you'll soon understand where the "vile" comes from.

DesertSole.src:
Desert sole is not the music genre of choice for Moon Garou. Instead, the desert sole is a rather flat fish that likes to nestle at the bottom of sandy pools. Being sandy-coloured themselves, it makes for a rather difficult fish to spot, let alone catch.

The flatness of a desert sole once drew the attention of the dragonkin, Lacrussa. She noted the evolutionary benefit of being paper-thin, camouflaged and having organs spread out across the body. So she dabbled with the idea for dragons. Needless to say, her 'flat-dragon' years were some of her least productive.

DesertNet.src: Desert waters throws up some interesting challenges for a net. There are fish that like to nestle into the sand, both below the surface and where a net would not usually reach. To counter this problem, a desert net is weighted on one side but not the other. The weighted side trawls the sandy floor, while the unweighted side catches the fish that attempt to get away. It does lead to some unwanted catches - be prepared to find a wealth of bones in the Umbral Sands - but that's testament to how effective it is.

BronzeArrowBrutal.src:
Designed to deliver a ruthless punch, the brutal arrow is not to be trifled with. It was used by the warriors of Brynmoor to take down more dangerous foes, such as roving garou or dangerous wolves. 

One cold night in autumn, a creature appeared in the valley and massacred a local farm. The villagers were horrified, running screaming to the guard, who rallied the forces as quickly as they could muster. The beast was large and lumbering, and its red eyes shone out in the night. Its flesh was covered in mangy black fur, and its teeth were sharp as daggers where they hadn’t rotted away. 

The creature tore through the guard, leaving a trail of fallen warriors in its wake. It took the courage and skill of a Wild Knight, Aurin, to stand against it. Armed with brutal arrows of polished bronze, he launched a relentless assault. The creature, despite being struck by a whole quiver of arrows, refused to fall. Instead, it let out a chilling howl and vanished into the shadows, leaving the battlefield in a state of eerie silence.

UndeadMeat.src:
Despite the appearance of their former owners, and the deeply unpleasant smell emanating from it, undead meat is not rotten. It, like the nature of its former owners, is preserved in a state between life and death, as if it’s on the cusp of souring, but never quite getting there.

This unique nature gives it some very interesting properties, but sadly taste isn’t one of them.

SalvagePile.src: Detritus is a wonderful word. "Detritus". It even sounds dirty and worthless. But rummage around in it if you will: there may be something worth salvaging.

RuneCrossbowLimbs.src:
Did you hear about the crossbow limb shop? They were always out of stock!

People used to chase after me because of my bad crossbow jokes, so I had to make a bolt for it.

WillowSeed.src: Did you know that a willow seed is called a 'salix', and looks a bit like the stuffing out of a toy bear? Now, we appreciate that doesn't reconcile with the icon we have chosen for the willow seed, but we would have got complaints that 'the willow seed icon looks like the stuffing from a toy bear'. Honestly, there was no good option here. If you're a botanist, close your eyes and imagine the fluff.

BlackCrossbowLimbs.src: Did you know that someone who fires a crossbow is often considered an 'arbalister' or 'arbalist'? Don't say that these journals don't teach you something.

DriedKrill.src: Did you know that, for a short period in the First Age, time was once measured in Krill Hours? If watches had existed back then, you would have been able to set it by the migratory patterns of krill. The dominant shoal would take precisely one hour to pass from one side of Bramblemead Valley, round Temple Woods, to the other side of Bramblemead. Children would often try to match their speeds, attempting to see who could notch up the greatest KH (krill hours).

WiseOldMan.src:
Dionysius was once a legendary adventurer. In his youth, he single-handedly defeated the troll invasion of Keldagrim. He crushed the enemies of one of the mountain tribes and taught the people of Karamja how to use powerful herbs that might aid them in battle. He committed great deeds throughout his life, and the world is a better place with him in it.

Or it was.

After he settled down, finishing his book on destructive magic, Dionysius began to feel that the world was a little unfair. He had tirelessly given his youth for the betterment of the world, and he had nothing to show for it. Even his devout faith in Saradomin wasn’t making his life more comfortable.

So, like so many do, he turned to crime. He targeted the nearby bank, his magic making quick work of their security, and he lifted himself a great deal of gold as well as a snazzy blue party hat. Content to consider this repayment for saving the world so often, he now sits back and enjoys his well-earned wealth.

The Temple Knights consider him an ultraviolet archangel threat and watch him very closely... from very far away.

Naptha.src:
Distilled from Swamp Tar and Charcoal.

Once known as “thick water”, naptha is liquid fire in waiting. It takes little to bring this substance to ignition, even too bright a sunny day can bring the raging flame from within.

As such, this material is widely sought by anyone with a strong desire to set things aflame. Pyromaniacs, alchemists and dragon cultists alike yearn for this liquid.

Lobster.src:
Do not be fooled by the traders on the street who preach of rare black lobsters worth unparalleled wealth. These are lies. For the rare black lobster is, in truth, a source of great darkness and evil.

Forged from black stone found beneath the waters of the Cursed Archipelago, the rare black lobster whispers terrible, terrible secrets to its bearer. It urges them towards darker and darker acts, until nothing of the host is left except an overwhelming urge toward evil.

Seek thee not the rare black lobster, for it will bring nought but despair!

DraconicHide.src:
Do not pity the dragonwolf. Oh, you don’t? That’s fine then. Yes, horrible little blighters aren’t they? Their teeth are too jagged and they’re far too aggressive for my tastes. Still, apparently deadly critters don’t just want to roll over and die so you can harvest their skin, who’d have thought?

The dragonwolf is an experiment that didn’t quite go right. It wasn’t wrong, exactly, it was certainly a step in the direction their creator wanted, but like most Dragonkin experiments, they was never “good enough”. Too warm-blooded. Too fluffy. Too weak.

Fortunately, the crafters in Emberwood were not quite so picky. They found that hide to be incredibly durable and hardy, whilst remaining surprisingly flexible. They would craft wonderous outfits from the tanned leather, trying to emulate their winged overseers.

IronRock.src: Do you know the riddle of iron? No, me neither, asking for a friend. Iron is a durable metal, capable of creating some of the strongest arms and armour available.

EggsRoyale.src:
Do you know what they call eggs royale in Asgarnia? "Salmon and egg". Barbarians.

There aren't many flavours that go together as well as salmon and egg. Pork and cheese. Bread and butter. Fishing potions and a hangover.

AmylaseCrystal.src:
Do you really want to know what amylase crystals are? I know this is a journal and you would expect some elaboration, but sometimes a little mystery is best when it comes to alchemical reagents. 

Ugh, you're still here? Fine. Amylase crystal is a concentrated deposit of saliva. There's no way of sugar-coating it: you're holding some sun-dried spit right here. And just as it does wonders for digestive processes, it's pretty good at breaking down roughage in potion-crafting.

Infusion.CoolingEvasion.src: Dodging an enemy's attack is already 'cool' - just ask any of the top-ranking thieves from the Thieves' Guild, back on mainland Gielinor. But evading enemies while ice-cold yourself: that is the epitome of style.

Cadavaberries.src:
Don’t eat them. No, seriously, don’t. At least not raw. Cadavaberries are poisonous and deadly, often used in sinister ceremonies of ritual sacrifice. The cadavaberries on Ashenfall are equally toxic, but can be coaxed into good behaviour with the judicious addition of fire.

The toxins can be burned away, providing a surprisingly pleasant tasting berry beneath. But, one must be careful, for preparing them wrong is the last mistake someone is likely to make.

MincedUndeadMeat.src:
Don’t think about it. Just burn it until it’s unrecognisable and try not to think about the implications of consuming the flesh of rotting zombie animals.

I’m sure it’s fine.

Do I want a bite? No, no, I’m good… err… trying to watch my figure. You go right ahead.

MithrilShield.src:
Doric insists that you should be able to see your face in a mithril shield. That's the mark of quality: if you can check for rock cakes in your teeth before battle, then you've made a good one. 

There's at least a little science behind that. The more tempered mithril is, the more it reflects. Doric isn't being a narcissist here, he knows what he is doing.

Doric.src:
Doric is a master smith who trained in the dwarven capital of Keldagrim. He owns a smithing shop in Asgarnia alongside his son Boric. The two of them have a strained relationship because Boric took it personally when Doric sent him to Keldagrim to complete his training. 

To rebuild trust and show his son that he has the uttermost faith in his abilities, Doric has left the running of the shop to Boric in his absence. Now, Doric comes to Ashenfall in search of new metals, lost smithing techniques, and the blueprints of ancient weapons. 

Not much of a fighter himself these days, he prefers to stay out of harm’s way, but he knows how to wield a hammer if push comes to shove.

MithrilDeposit.src:
Doric is peeved that mithril is predominantly in Zamorakian territory. Dwarves feel a kinship to the ore: it means a little more to them than the other metals. In his view, Zamorakians don't deserve it.

He won't admit it if you confront him, but it's a big reason that you can find him in Dowdun Reach. One eye on the mithril. If he had it his way, he'd be laying minecart tracks all the way from Dowdun Reach to Temple Woods. Then he'd have to fight the urge to make mithril platebodies until the end of his days.

MithrilDagger.src:
Doric likes to remind Vannaka that you wouldn't find a dwarf making daggers.

As Doric says, "It's a very human thing, a dagger. A dwarf never hides their weapon: we're polite enough to show what you're up against. An' you won't find us attacking from the back or sides. No sir, we bonk you from the front."

BronzeWarhammer.src:
Doric would be the first person to praise the simple hammer. It is a large solid chunk of metal attached to a long haft, allowing the weapon to benefit from the unmistakable might of physics. Weight and speed are a terrifying combination. 

Dwarves, in particular, favour this weapon. They feel it speaks to their long-held desire to shape metal by pounding into shape by sheer strength alone. They apply the same logic to their enemies, beating them into a shape that the dwarves feel suits their enemies better.  

There were once dwarves on Ashenfall who were masters of this technique. However, when the humans began their infighting, and Guthix turned away from them, they vanished deeper into the continent, leaving behind a shroud of mystery in search of something extraordinary. 

They found it and have never returned.

ConstructionSkillcapeTrimmed.src: Double congratulations! You have achieved a Construction Cape with all the trimmings. Precious few can claim that distinction.

CookingSkillcapeTrimmed.src: Double congratulations! You have achieved a Cooking Cape with all the trimmings. Precious few can claim that distinction.

MagicSkillcapeTrimmed.src: Double congratulations! You have achieved a Magic Cape with all the trimmings. Precious few can claim that distinction.

MiningSkillcapeTrimmed.src: Double congratulations! You have achieved a Mining Cape with all the trimmings. Precious few can claim that distinction.

RangedSkillcapeTrimmed.src: Double congratulations! You have achieved a Ranged Cape with all the trimmings. Precious few can claim that distinction.

RunecraftingSkillcapeTrimmed.src: Double congratulations! You have achieved a Runecrafting Cape with all the trimmings. Precious few can claim that distinction.

WoodcuttingSkillcapeTrimmed.src: Double congratulations! You have achieved a Woodcutting Cape with all the trimmings. Precious few can claim that distinction.

AttackSkillcapeTrimmed.src: Double congratulations! You have achieved an Attack Cape with all the trimmings. Precious few can claim that distinction.

DragonScimitar.src:
Dragon metal is not, as the name might imply, made of dragons. Well, not directly. It's a composite of a material called orikalkum (or orichalcum, depending on whether you prefer to use the dwarven spelling) and drakolith, which no longer resides on Ashenfall. The dragonkin, notably Brakka, exhausted whatever deposits were left on the island. 

Once an alloy has been formed by these two materials, it needs to be forged in dragonfire. That, unlike drakolith, was in abundance on Ashenfall. The result was dragon metal, and Brakka could make precious little of it. There was enough to make a throne, perhaps, or a motherlode maw. Realistically, Brakka couldn't use the metal to make much of material use, so he a forged small armoury of kiteshields, scimitars and crossbows. If the dragonkin were to ever be threatened, then they would at least have the best weapons on Ashenfall to respond.

GreenDragonHide.src:
Dragons are never fond of surrendering their natural armour, a natural feature they’ve used to great advantage.

In the earliest days of the Dragonkin experiments, the scales of a dragon were something to be proud of. They would turn away blade and arrow with equal skill, and even magic struggled to pierce their natural defences.

Still, this wasn’t good enough for their makers. Lacrussa, herself, saw the hide of dragons as a promising start, but little more, and she would strive to forge newer and more resilient scales on her creations. The green dragons were, in her opinion, some of the weakest of the dragons, and she only kept them around because her sibling enjoyed the glittering green reflections of the sunlight on their scales.

WitheringWater.src:
Drawn from pools of wither-rot water, lakes and streams poisoned by the waters of the river Noumenon – the river of the dead.

These waters have become corrupted by Imaru’s hunger and each drop longs to devour one’s soul.

BlackCape.src: Dress like a creature of the night with this sinister cloak.

YellowCape.src: Dress like a king with this fabulous yellow cape.

Shrapnel.src:
Dropped by Bleed inflicting enemies.

Small collections of sharp little objects. Stone, metal, bone, each of these combines to create a little bit of hate in the palm of your hand. The brutal points of these bits of shrapnel can tear the skin and rend the flesh, making them perfect for crafting weapons to make things bleed.

PoisonIchor.src:
Dropped by poisonous enemies.

Nature is full of malicious little critters who carry toxins. Snakes, spiders, politicians, each of them has ways to make other creatures suffer.

This ichor is prized by poisoners and alchemists, as it can be used to create deadly concoctions that will give someone, or something, a really bad day.

WoodenArrow.src:
Druids dislike violence but understand its place. The natural world is full of blood, murder and death. The strong consume the weak. Predator against prey. This they understand, though they seldom like it. When they must resort to violence, they choose the simple approach. Man’s strength comes not from their muscles but from their creativity and ingenuity. Just as a wolf has claws, a hunter has a bow. 

When a bow must be drawn, the druids prefer arrows made of simple wood. Gathered twigs and branches, whittled down to sharp points. They see it as the forest giving them the blessing to go on the hunt. Traditionally, feathers are gathered from around the forest floor, taken when dropped or from a bird’s moulting. This keeps the number of arrows low, forcing a hunter to be accurate and precise, lest they run out of chances. 

Thus, death is swift at the hands of a bow, and balance isn’t damaged. This the druids preached to the villagers.

RangerHat.src:
During the final years of Bramblemead corruption had run rampant. Nobles took more than their share and the priests who watched over them turned a blind eye in exchange for their own share of glittering coin. Those who did not possess noble blood, found that their lives became harder, their earnings became smaller and joy became a much more fleeting feeling than it had done before.

One woman decided to change that. She would attack trader caravans marked with goods for the castle, taking from their purses of coin. Tax collectors would also feel the sting of her arrows, surrendering their wealth to the woman clad in green. She was given the name Nightingale, because of the whistling noise her arrows made as they flew through the air, an almost musical tone that sent fear through her targets.

Villagers would then wake in the morning following an attack, to find purses of coin in flowerboxes, window shelves, or resting neatly under the fattest, laziest, cats.

DwellberryGlazedRoastMeat.src: Dwellberries boiled down into a sticky sauce and liberally trailed across the meat. You may not expect the combination to work, but upon that first mouthful, your tastebuds will squirm in delight for this delicious combination.

DwellberryCrunchies.src: Dwellberries on Ashenfall are heartier than their mainland counterparts, and make for excellent ingredients. The Wild Knights were particularly fond of this recipe, though they referred to them as “dwellberry splats” because Olis, their creator, wasn’t a particularly good chef.

DriedRedberries.src: Easier to eat on the go than standard redberries. Tastier too.

Choppertunity.src:
Edgar was a lazy lumberjack, who was good friends with some of the wizards at the guild. He would skive off work, to visit the taverns with his blue-robed buddies, where they would laugh and discuss the fundamentals of magic, whilst their world blurred out of focus. Yet, Edgar always listened to his friends and he picked up on concepts that his more academically minded companions would miss. Magic, whilst it could be wielded like a scalpel, was also perfectly capable of being used like a club. 

With some runes in his pocket and laziness as his shield, Edgar created a spell that would make his job go much faster – shattering tree trunks into useful logs, in a matter of moments. 

He was later fired, when he tried the spell when drunk – demolishing the beams of his master's cabin.

EyeOfOculus.src:
Elias Oculus was an avid birdwatcher. He delighted in nothing more than seeing sparrows, falcons and corvids nest. In the spring, he would wake just before the sunrise, so that he could watch the flocks of birds emerge from their nests and take to the skies in a cacophony of song. How he longed to join them, to fly beside them and witness their world in the skies. But, alas, as a human, he was chained to the floor by the unbreakable bonds of gravity.

When he started studying to be a wizard, he realised a way to live his dream. A spell that would move his vision outside the confines of his mortal flesh, and allow him to soar among the heavens. In addition to creating a spell found invaluable by architects, Elias also published the most comprehensive studies of bird flight patterns.

When he passed on to the next life, a statue was created in his honour.  It isn't found on any ruin, nor on grand display, but resting in the branches of a great tree, so that his beloved birds could remember him fondly.

AmuletOfMagic.src:
Emberwood had its fair share of spellcasters, though lacking the funding of the tower to the south. With more limited resources the mages of Emberwood found other methods to strengthen their art, and the Amulet of Magic was popular among all of them.

Druids worse these amulets while performing rituals around the standing stones, hoping that it might strengthen their bond with nature. The self-proclaimed warlocks, of the Children of Shadows, would sit in darkened basements wearing these glittering amulets as they intoned dark rites that had no effect. The Wild Knight mages would use them more pragmatically, wielding magic against all the threats that the villagers were unaware of.

Fellhollow.Emberwood.src:
Emberwood was the perfect village, at least for a time. After years of monotheistic rule turning them against one another, the villagers sought strength in variety. They created churches to each of the four major gods - Saradomin, Zamorak, Guthix and Armadyl - and each had a voice at the table, whenever discussions were had.

Amalgamated walked side by side with those who had not been touched by the anima of Ashenfall. Whilst it would be naïve to claim there was no prejudice, it was much more frowned upon and the Amalgamated could find themselves rising to any height of society, with only a little more effort than their peers.

It was far from perfect, but it was trying to get there. It could have been a wonderful place to live.

Kuldra’s cruelty put a stop to that, and Imaru’s grief-filled rage corrupted it all into a nightmare of fear and pain.

MaplePlank.src: Even followers of chaos must acknowledge the laws of physics. Try as they might, they cannot build structures on ego alone, and so must convert maple logs into maple planks.

UndeadBass.src: Even in death there are some fisherfolk who spend their quiet moments hooking these creatures. They wait, rictus still, in patience and draw these wretched things from beneath the waves, only to find their prey as dead and decayed as they are, and cast them back into the water.

Weeds.src:
Even the plant world has its outcasts. Weeds are unloved, unwanted and yet they always find a way to turn up in the most unexpected of places. Just like my cousin Terry.

Still, at least weeds have some uses... unlike Terry.

DowdunReach.TheCourtyard.src:
Even worshippers of the so called “god of evil”, a moniker levied on Zamorak by the Saradomin worshippers, have a need for green spaces. Nature is soothing, grounding and calming, it can do wonders for our mental health, and sometimes even those who follow the lord of chaos need somewhere to relax.

This was the courtyard once, long ago now: a place of gentle contemplation and relaxation, before the corruption took hold.

Now, it is a wild and overgrown place, infected by chickens and chincompas alike. A good place to set up camp, for those with decent survival instincts, but not somewhere you’re likely to find much of a chance to relax.

BlightwoodShortbow.src:
Every hunter reaches a crossroads in life when a choice becomes clear. They have honed their skills with a bow, surpassing the challenges posed by the Brynmoor prey. They could settle into a comfortable life in the village—hunting the same old deer, earning a regular wage, and basking in a relaxing level of respect from their peers. Or, they could dare to dream bigger, to push their skills to new heights. 

The Wild Knights journeyed into more dangerous territories, facing off against deadly monsters warped by the anima twist. Joining them would mean abandoning the comfortable life of friends and family but earning a chance to face challenges that they would never face at home. 

Most choose comfort, as one might expect. But those who choose to improve would be taught how to craft a more powerful weapon, casting aside the oak bows that carry their names. They would carve a new name and identity into the limbs of their latest weapon and join the knights.
