Power, trapped in dragonstone crystal and worn around the neck, that is the essence of this amulet. The facets of the dragonstone refract and refine the enchantments cast upon the item, somehow creating a magical lattice of surprising strength.

Many have tried to create variations of this theme, yet dragonstone proves too fragile a substance for practical use. Once someone attempted to make a dragonstone dagger, to see if they could turn it into a blade of glory, yet they could not find a sufficiently large stone that wasn’t valuable enough to bankrupt a small nation.

One wizard attempted strange alchemical practices to try and forge a staff of pure dragonstone. Alas, not only did he fail to create such a stone, but the magical explosion that resulted from his hubris removed his lab, and all his research, from this plane of reality.

It’s probably a good idea that no one attempt to duplicate his work.

Dwellberries.src: Pretty blue berries, go well in a cheesecake.

SaradominCloak.src:
Priests of Saradomin would often wear cloaks like these. Simple affairs, designed to keep them safe from the breeze whilst also venerating the god of order.

Both practical and fashionable. A good Saradominist always looks their best in any weather.

LinenApprenticeBody.src:
Prized for its lightweight and nimble nature, linen armour finds favour among apprentice wizards and those who value agility. Composed of layered cloth, it forms a rudimentary defence capable of withstanding minor assaults. 

At first, acolytes would spend time at the wizard’s tower to learn about the magic the armour would protect the wearer against. It was common for young priestly acolytes to become enamoured with the mysterious life of the apprentice wizards. They would see them hurling spells with skill and panache, making their lives of quiet contemplation seem awfully dull in response. Many young acolytes would make linen armour for themselves, practising spellcasting in secret.

The priests soon discovered their numbers dwindling, while the wizard’s guild gained more members. So, the decree was given that robes were to be crafted in silent contemplation, far away from those who would later wear them. This would keep fewer acolytes from being lured away, but the defensive prowess of the armour diminished in return.

The high priests considered this a reasonable exchange.

LinenApprenticeHead.src:
Prized for its lightweight and nimble nature, linen armour finds favour among apprentice wizards and those who value agility. Composed of layered cloth, it forms a rudimentary defence capable of withstanding minor assaults. 

In the third age, apprentice wizards wore this armour as they practised basic spells. The more senior, blue-robed wizards guided them in their practice and taught them basic enchantments that helped them resist low-level spells and curses. 

The creation of these robes was a sacred duty entrusted to the young acolytes of the faith. It was a testament to their devotion and a means of assisting others in their service to Saradomin.

LinenApprenticeLegs.src:
Prized for its lightweight and nimble nature, linen armour finds favour among apprentice wizards and those who value agility. Composed of layered cloth, it forms a rudimentary defence capable of withstanding minor assaults. 

This simple armour would remain popular with apprentice wizards long into the third age, falling out of fashion only when faced with something more dangerous than a goblin.

The beastmen further north of Brynmoor used weapons far more vicious than a goblin might wield. They tore through linen armour as if it were nothing, and the diminished enchantments of the acolytes did nothing to shield the blows.

Apprentice wizards died in droves, and the armour fell out of favour.

MapleShortbow.src:
Putrilius, the cthonian demon, will tell you that any living thing can be possessed. If needs must, a cthonian can be a cockroach or spider, for a time. 

In one desperate moment, after the Dreaming Stone shattered, Putrilius was forced to possess a maple tree. It wasn't an experience she enjoyed. Most curiously, she found herself becoming attuned to the maple's inner cadence. Everything slowed. Putrilius barely registered a thought in two years.

What woke Putrilius was a logging axe. Her maple body was toppled and then fletched into an armature. For a moment, as Putrilius' life faded from the wood, she was a shortbow. 

It was the closest she had come to dying. With a cognitive spark, she moved from the bow to a passing hound before all her lifeforce ebbed away.

WateringCan.Wooden.src:
Rain is unreliable. It is far too whimsical in when and where it falls. Relying on its good nature is a sure-fire way to court drought, famine and ruin. Because of this, the druids created rainfall you could hold, handheld containers of water that could be summoned when and where it was needed.

Fill one of these up from any water source and you can use it to keep your farming plots nice and moist.

BlackDragonLeather.src: Rangers are stealthy little blighters. They like nothing more than to crouch behind a mushroom and ping arrows at a target, preferably without being seen. That preference makes black dragon leather hugely attractive to a ranger. Not only does it bend nicely at the joints for the mushroom-crouching, it's highly durable and - best of all - it's black, which makes the whole subterfuge thing more likely to succeed. I've aways suspected that rangers like the black as it makes them look a bit edgy, but that's unproven.

DraconicStaff.src:
Rasthin was a powerful sorceress, even among the dragonkin. She had mastered all manner of spells and was even schooled in the techniques of the previous Revision.

Still, magic as an art was largely looked down upon in dragonkin society. It was considered vulgar and the obsession of children. Alchemy and science were the true path forward. In part, it’s because of the connection between magic and the hated Elder Gods, whose anger the dragonkin feared rousing.

But Rasthin knew the value of magic, as did the other members of her group. She created a staff, forged from glittering crystal and anima-infused iron, which allowed her to channel her magic into powerful spells.

Yet, even with a weapon as powerful as this, she discarded her magic when she uncovered the power of Ashenfall – preferring, instead, to enjoy her newfound connection with elemental flame.

Still, the remnants of the staff pulse with potential, and while they may never achieve their former power, they remain mighty magic tools, just waiting to be crafted.

FireIronArrows.src:
Rasthin was the master of fire. It was the gift she had stolen from the “soul of the world” as she called it. She could use the inner flame to inspire confidence or rouse people into a great fervour. The fire could reveal secrets, forcing truth from those who stood before her. But, more practical than all of that was one simple truth, that fire could burn.

There were many a dragon that tried to battle Rasthin directly, believing their dragonfire could destroy her. Their bones litter Ashenfall. It was only Queen Kuldra herself who could challenge the dragonkin, and theirs was a battle that left scars in the lands for centuries.

These arrows borrow a piece of Rasthin’s power. Able to inspire only by the fear they kindle in the wielder’s enemies. Yet, kindle they do, for those who face these flames will surely feel echoes of the fury wrought by the dragonkin lord of fire.

ScornedWilderness.ScornedWilderness.src:
Rasthin’s built a device that would harness the power of the Wellspring, attuning an individual to one of the runic elements, granting them power beyond reasoning without any of the pesky limitations of godhood. Selfishly, she hoarded this power for herself and her allies; using what gifts were granted her to manipulate, control or destroy her enemies.

When Kuldra broke free of her chains and rose up against her dragonkin masters, Rasthin refused to allow the queen to gain access to the power of the Wellspring and turned her device into a weapon. In one great act of defiance, her device exploded and tore the region apart, shattering it into floating islands in defiance of the laws of gravity. The damage is felt across all of Ashenfall, but none so intensely as here.

Now, Kuldra has made this place her palace. She sits on the remnants of Rasthin’s technology and works to transform it into a weapon that threatens all of Gielinor. If she is not stopped, she will unleash shockwaves of pure anima that will rip the mainlands into fractured islands, just like the ones she calls home.

None will survive the process.

RawBeltfish.src:
Raw beltfish is a tricky customer. It's a tough, almost sinewy meat, more like a whip than a food product. If you're a chef and want to torment your sous-chef, then crack a beltfish and watch them pay attention.

Equally, if you're a sous-chef and your chef is constantly whipping you with beltfish, then a beltfish makes for a handy garotte.

SauteedSardines.src:
Redberries are red

Sardines are grey

This is the meal 

I eat while I slay.

Reek.src: Reek doesn't reek. He just has an aroma THAT IS UNAPPRECIATED IN ITS OWN TIME.

KuldraCape.src:
Regularly, I have stood behind someone and had absolutely no idea - none at all - whether they have killed Kuldra or not. I might be in a queue for a cup of tea and the person in front of me would exist in a metaphysical state of both killing and not killing Kuldra. I wouldn't know until I asked them, and frankly that's a question I don't want to ask everyone.

Praise be for the Dragonslayer Cape! Now, when I stand behind someone in a queue, I can know - with certainty - whether they have killed Kuldra.

ReinforcedLeatherBody.src:
Reinforced leather, designed to withstand powerful attacks. Layers of stiffened leather folded together to strengthen one another, turning singular sheets into a powerful defensive force. 

There was a bountiful supply of leather in Brynmoor, much to the chagrin of cows. Young villagers would be crafted sturdy leather armour when they trained with the guard. Few villagers would ever make the cut of town guard; the demands were strict, and the discipline required was more than many could handle. Yet, those who made the cut were afforded the uttermost respect among the people. 
At least those who were not afflicted with the curse of the Amalgamated.

ReinforcedLeatherLegs.src:
Reinforced leather, designed to withstand powerful attacks. Layers of stiffened leather folded together to strengthen one another, turning singular sheets into a powerful defensive force. 

When an Amalgamated rose through the ranks of the guard, a tricky feat given the prejudice against them, it did not instil the populace with a sense of comfort. The villagers saw the marks of the elemental corruption on the guards and would turn and walk the other way. They would refuse to report a crime if they saw leaves instead of hair. 
Amalgamated guards would rarely be granted equipment of greater quality than reinforced leather. No matter what missions they were assigned. It was seen as a waste, considering the uncooperative nature of many villagers, making it hard for an Amalgamated guard to do their duty. 

It is, perhaps, no wonder that few Amalgamated guards chose to remain in the service for long.

ReinforcedLeatherHead.src:
Reinforced leather, designed to withstand powerful attacks. Layers of stiffened leather folded together to strengthen one another, turning singular sheets into a powerful defensive force. 

While metal is the preferred material for armour, leather has its charm. Its wearers boast greater agility and find it easier to hide the sounds of their movements than they can in metal gear. But its most important benefit is the relative cheapness in construction.

StuddedLeatherBody.src:
Reinforced leather, with metal plates woven throughout. The plates rest underneath leather coverings, with metal studs to hold them in place, giving the armour its name. Favoured by scouts and hunters for the mixture of agility and defence. 

Dealing with the armour’s distinctive scent soon became a training tool for more dangerous hunters. It taught them to use the wind as a weapon. They would always walk against it, the wind in their faces, meaning that the garou could not smell them coming. When the weather didn’t help them, the Wild mages would cast constant subtle air spells, changing the breeze’s direction.

One wild mage and her friend, a strange boy who wore a wolf’s skull as a mask, got the tactic down to an art. She used strange, sinister magics to enchant bones to maintain air spells, allowing her to precisely control the wind’s direction. She used this to lead the garou into traps, where her ally leapt from the shadows, taking out the unfortunate garou warriors.

StuddedLeatherHead.src:
Reinforced leather, with metal plates woven throughout. The plates rest underneath leather coverings, with metal studs to hold them in place, giving the armour its name. Favoured by scouts and hunters for the mixture of agility and defence. 

Most Wild Knights favoured studded leather armour over the more durable metal plate. Moving through the forests required as much grace as guts, and stealth is always a hunter’s friend. 

When they were brought into the war against the garou, the leather armour proved less popular at first. While durable and agile, leather has a strong and distinctive smell. The garou’s olfactory senses were much stronger than humans were prepared for, capable of tracking down the leathery smell from a disturbing range. Wind magic helped to keep the scent away from them, but it wasn’t enough to eradicate it.

StuddedLeatherLegs.src:
Reinforced leather, with metal plates woven throughout. The plates rest underneath leather coverings, with metal studs to hold them in place, giving the armour its name. Favoured by scouts and hunters for the mixture of agility and defence. 

While the design of studded leather made it excellent for hunters and invaluable in battles against the garou, it fell short against those who knew its construction. Betrayal is a constant foe, and once the garou war had come to a close, the Wild Knights found themselves at the mercy of it. 

Though there were more dangerous threats, with the dragons that appeared out of nowhere, there were always some that prioritized power and persecution over common sense. Daggers emerged from the shadows and drove between the plates sewn into the leather. The poison on the tips of these blades ended the life of more than a few Wild Knights. 

The assassins called themselves the “Glass Knives” in memory of the serial killer that took the lives of so many Amalgamated. To them, the strangeness of the knights was a greater threat than the dragons, and they were happy to pay the terrible price that their actions would cost.

UmbralSandsCape.src:
Reminisce on all the times that sand got literally everywhere. In your shoes. In your eyes. In your breakfast. This cape is a beautifully embroidered reminder of all the hot sun, scratchy grains, and annoying bugs trying to eat your face.

Wear it with pride.

UndeadCow.src: Rotted and twisted, these cows have a terrible beef with the living!

Rufus.src: Rufus is deaf, but that doesn't stop him from being the alpha of the group. If anything, it puts him in an admirable position, as he's less bothered by Gnasher's zooms, Lurch's wind, and Tiny's barking.

AirRunes.src:
Rune essence has the unique property of absorbing and transforming ambient magic into something that can be used by even races without a natural magical aptitude, like humans.

An air rune contains anima that is aligned with the wind itself. A practitioner of magic can take the rune and convert it into a gentle breeze. Or, with enough of them, a gale force wind.

Very popular in the hot summer months.

RunePoisonArrows.src: Rune poison arrows were often called 'overkill arrows' by the garou in Kuldra's Tower. If the sharp rune metal didn't kill you, then the magical resonance in the arrow would. There was almost no need for the poison on top of that. You had to truly hate someone to make a rune poison arrow.

RuneShortsword.src:
Runite is not readily available to everyone in Kuldra's army. Kuldra preferred that it - alongside magic wood - was reserved to the upper reaches of her army.

It is easy to look at her chaos of heads and think that she somehow represents disorder, but Kuldra instilled hierarchy in her troops. You needed to earn your place at the top of her troops, and she was consistent in what earned that place. You had to be inconspicuous enough to never draw her attention, and you needed to avoid anyone who might draw that attention. Suffer fools, and you suffer with them. Stand within metres of them, and you suffer even more dearly.

UmbralSandsCapeGolden.src: Running in sand is one of the hardest things in the world, so take a bow. You've not only mastered Umbral Sands, but you've run about in it, which is something that most of us would try to avoid.

HealthAndStamina.src:
Sadly, most of us aren’t immortal. We are each made from squishy bags of flesh, that don’t do well when stabbed, sliced or otherwise turned into a pincushion. In Dragonwilds, we represent the stability of our squishy fleshy bits by our Hitpoints.

When we’re injured, our Hitpoints go down. If they reach zero, why I’m afraid that’s rather it. Well, until you resurrect of course – handy thing that. You can recover Hitpoints with certain potions, or by making sure you’re well fed.

Stamina, is the measure of how tired we are. The lower your stamina, the less energy you have and you need a little bit of energy to handle most tasks. Attacking, dodging and skilling all use stamina when you engage in them. If your stamina is at zero, you won’t be able to perform the action you are attempting to do.

Fortunately, stamina recovers over time, especially if you keep yourself well hydrated.

GarouWeave.src:
Sadly, this is not a new hairstyle unlock, rather it’s a special cloth created by the Moon Garou. They say it’s woven from moon sprite silk, which can only be obtained in the light of a full moon and, even then, only by shamans. 

The truth is that it’s less complicated than that. It’s crafted by a gaggle of garou grannies, each of them weaving together special fibres that have been passed down their family line for generations. Each bolt of cloth may seem the same, but they are each a unique blending of garou family craftwork.

Saradomin.src:
Saradomin is known as the god of order. Once human himself, he is perhaps the most popular deity on Gielinor, especially among other humans. He preaches tradition, education and righteousness, and prizes human well being above almost everything else.

During the third age, he was part of the God Wars and waged a holy campaign against the usurper, Zamorak. These two deities remain in eternal conflict, both considering each other their greatest foe. This hatred has spread to their followers and has been the cause of many conflicts across Gielinor’s past.

The church of Saradomin watches over much of the mainland kingdoms, with priests and the faithful advising the leaders of entire nations.

He is depicted as a bearded man wearing a crown, often carrying a staff. His symbol is a four pointed star.

OakStaff.src:
Saradominist mages preferred the hefty swing of an oak staff over the more pliable ash. They felt that sturdier oak allowed for more powerful spells. The more durable wood was less prone to shattering itself into splinters when they cast their most devastating magic. 

While most wizards practised familiar spells, pushing their research into different practical applications for what was already known, one wizard would push the boundaries of spellcasting. Her name was Cynthia Valtis, and she would go down in local legend.

She would have liked to be remembered for her ability to transform twigs into carrots, thus preventing the famine that threatened Brynmoor. She would have wanted to be remembered for her clever application of wind and water magic to create a nice cool breeze during the summer heat. But, alas, she would be remembered for an ill-advised fire magic experiment that would see her travel across the continent faster than any wizard before. 

Her body has yet to be found.

RawSardine.src: Sardines travel in large shoals; their lives spent as part of a grand community. There’s something a little tragic seeing one here on its own. Still, with a little heat, perhaps a sprinkle of salt and some other seasonings, and you’ve got yourself a nice snack.

SqueakingSausage.src:
Sausages are proof that ignorance is bliss. When you bite into the juicy banger, you are best served not to think about its contents. Nor about the origins of the skin that contains the meat so well.

Although simple, and lacking in much needed herbs and spices, these sausages manage to curb your hunger well enough to help you avoid thinking too much about what they’re made from.

Ignore the squeak… and the whiskers.

Seeds.Magic.src: Seeds are brilliant, aren't they? Within one seed, no bigger than a fingernail, is pure potential. Given the right conditions, it will grow into something as big as an oak tree or as remarkable as a magic tree. They're little Big Bangs in a seed format, distributing mass and foliage from a dense centre.

SteelBolts.src:
Sharpened bolts of steel projected at great speed is a formula for your target to have a very bad day.

Although it was cheaper and quicker to forgo the coal and craft iron bolts, the relentless nature of the undead hordes required a more practical approach. Steel was stronger than iron, and was more likely to put the ravenous undead back in the dirt where they belonged, making it very popular in the last few years of Fellhollow’s resistance.

EnchantedSteelBolts.src:
Sharpened rods of metal, enchanted with magic. A surefire way to guarantee that your enemies have a particularly bad time.

In Fellhollow these bolts were vital against the undead, as they provided that additional firepower needed to take down the relentless tide of shambling corpses.

BowOfElidinis.src:
She is known by many names, both here and in the deserts entire oceans apart from one another, yet to all of them she is a source of life and creation. She is the river in the desert sands, from which all civilisation blooms, and she is the rain that washes away the cruel and merciless when the monsoon season comes.

To the Moon Garou she is the River Mother, the Moon Maiden and their salvation. For it was she, who helped the wandering garou to step away from their primal predatory nature, and tame the sands, cultivating crops and building cities.

She left the deserts centuries ago, to places unknown. Some say she wanders the stars in search of a place where her grief can be lessened. While others claim she prepares for war against a more insidious foe. A creature of fire, ash and hatred, the demon of the sun.

This bow was left to one of her favourite Moon Garou, a warrior called Kyter, whom she had raised as her own after he was orphaned by a cruel sandstorm. The bow was passed down his family line, parent to child, until the last of the bloodline was murdered by Fuzan.

Now, the bow is yours. Use it wisely, for she will surely be annoyed if you don’t.

TinOre.src: Shiny and metallic, combine with copper to make bronze bars.

CopperOre.src: Shiny and metallic, combine with tin to make bronze bars.

SilverOre.src: Silver is an excellent conductor of magic. It’s why it shows up in so many legends and myths about supernatural foes. As a precious metal, it is highly prized in the crafting of jewellry and strongly disliked by lycanthropes everywhere.

Bread.src:
Simple wheat, water, yeast and salt, combined together and incinerated within an oven. A staple across many cultures and species across Gielinor and beyond. The Icyene of Hallow enjoy a flatbread that they can wrap food in, for a meal on the wind. The aviansie of Abbinah, when the limited wheat is available, prefer a thick and sturdy bread, so that each bite lasts longer. Elves enjoy a sourdough, priding themselves on how long they can keep the starter alive.

For the people of Ashenfall, much like their cousins in the mainland, a simple loaf is more than enough.

WhitePlatebody.src:
Sir Percival Lateef only had a short moment of wonder, before the horror struck. The beach he had arrived on was surrounded by cliffs, meaning his only options were to climb or to swim, and since he was wearing the heavy armour of the White Knights, he decided that sinking wasn’t an option.

It took him many hours and several near falls, but he eventually made his way up and down the cliffside, only to encounter a region filled with the ravenous undead.

As a White Knight he trained to fight such evils and he fended them off as best he could, yet there were too many for him to face alone. He was forced to retreat, to a shrine, atop a rocky island, displaying the symbol of Saradomin, and there he prayed.

WhiteFullHelm.src:
Sir Percival Lateef was a proud man, assured of his own prowess, character and moral standing. On the mainland, he would train the other knights in swordsmanship, as well as host several long and laborious lectures on his supposed life as an explorer. He had travelled across the lands, to the frozen polar regions, and the jungles of Karamja, but no one ever seemed particularly interested in his stories.

Tired of being ignored and teased for his exploits, he took a boat and sailed it north of the mainland into regions unknown. His boat was destroyed. His crew left for dead, and he found himself on a unknown beach of strange, unnatural hues. The first human on Ashenfall for centuries, he was finally the explorer he dreamed himself to be.

SearedFarmSteak.src: Sizzling on the grill, there is little that has united middle-aged villagers than a steak seared to perfection. Brynmoor villagers would gather around grills to discuss hunting, village politics and anything else that came to mind, all as an excuse to silently judge the way the current chef prepared this simple meal.

MagicalMending.src:
Skilled craftspeople are worth their weight in gold. The ability to repair broken equipment, and weaponry, was a core part of any craftsperson's trade. But, in the wilds of Ashenfall, such trades lacked the excitement and adventure of more whimsical professions. Hunters, warriors and druids, were the roles that everyone wanted, and so it was that fewer and fewer apprentices took up the hammer. As such, smiths would focus on creating new equipment, and tools, leaving repairs on the backburner for sometimes weeks at a time. 

Frustrated, the druids created a solution to this problem. Using a variation on the ritual that preserved wood, timber, and stone, the druids could turn back the clock on a piece of equipment, returning it to a healthier state. 

Over time, more people began to favour less deadly professions, and the spell would be used in only the most dire situations.

FriedEgg.src:
Slimy, greasy and everything you need. There are few things as surprisingly satisfying as a fried egg sandwich. If only you had some bread!

Contrary to popular humour the aviansie have no issue with people eating eggs around them. Indeed many of them have raptor like tastes and will happily consume the eggs of livestock birds. Boiled almhas (a domesticated bat-like creature) eggs were popular snacks on Abbinah, yet those eggs could not be fried as they would combust dramatically when exposed to a naked flame.

Fortunately chicken eggs are far less flammable.

MagicTreeSapling.src:
Small yet full of magical energy, the magic tree sapling is one of the few trees in Ashenfall not taught to despise humankind.

That is, until it sees you cutting its parents down and harvesting their bodies as crafting materials…

StringyMeat.src: Smaller creatures have much less meat on their bones, making them a less fulfilling meal. Hunters would subsist on these while stalking larger prey over several days. The Wild Knight Ilom was particularly fond of drying out these little morsels, treating them as a meaty little snack for boring patrols.

AdamantiteOre.src: Smelt this, alongside coal, to create adamant bars. One of the most impressively durable metals available on Ashenfall, adamantite ore is highly prized by the desert-dwelling Moon Garou, who use it in a variety of endeavours.

HarmonisedCompound.src: Smelting discordant residue into harmonised compound is astonishingly reckless. In essence, you're 'cooking anima', which is akin to gargling fuel and then sipping on fire. You are dealing with some of the highest percentages of anima - the lifeblood of the world. We'd tell you to be careful, but this is the person who has wandered into the home of a five-headed dragon with the express intention of killing it.

SmokedHerring.src:
Smoked herring is not, as the idiom will claim, "red". It is more of an orange, coppery colour. That means the term "red herring" is something of a red herring. Which tracks.

The process of smoking a herring has changed over the years. In the Second Age, a herring would be smoked in the village elder's pipe, in the hope that some of the elder's wisdom would transfer to the fish. In the Third Age, entrepreneurial Zamorakians would line their demon portals with herring, in the hope of an infernal aftertaste. Nowadays, people use a cooking pot.

SnakeskinLeather.src: Snakes have a terrible deal in life. They must crawl along the floor, in the filth everyone else steps over. They suffer hate, fear and aggression from everyone who sees them and worst of all, if they bite their tongue, they're doomed. This snakeskin leather is gathered exclusively from the latter snakes, those who chomped down inefficiently and became their own undoing. This makes the leather both ethical and comparatively easy to gather. Waste not, want not, after all.

PanFriedDesertSole.src: So flat is a desert sole, that you could stick a handle on it and it would look something like a frying pan. Which, even as I write, is letting off fireworks in my brain and tastebuds. What if you used a desert sole frying pan to cook some chips? Or a curry? Goodness, I'm drooling.

Fellhollow.DragonsRun.src:
So named because Xikotal would delight in dashing through the valley each morning with the sunrise, snapping at the vanishing shadows as he made a game of chasing away the night. Imbued with the magic of the air, Xikotal reveled in the feeling of the wind against his scales, and he loved the laughter of the children that would run along beneath him, joining him in his fictional battle against the night.

Now the walls of this valley feel lonely and oppressive; corralling and trapping you, so that the dead might stand a better chance of adding you to their ranks.

In time, it seems, the night won the fight.

BlazingBlackKnight.src:
Some Black Knights looked upon the infernal realms with a sense of wonder. They saw how the demons wielded flames as if they were an extension of their own bodies and, lacking any magical talent of their own, these knights were filled with unbearable jealousy. They sought ways to turn these demonic flames to serve their own ends - some via alchemy, others via desperate chemical combinations - yet none were able to replicate the hellfire that they so dearly wished to wield.

So, as the foolish so often do, they turned to those with the power. The demon Adramalech was a master of fire, more so than many of her fellows, and she found a way to let the flame burn for another, using their own soul as fuel. She taught these knights to ignite their weapons, turning swords and axes into blazing infernos as extensions of their arms. The knights were grateful, foolish as they were.

InfinityCloth.src:
Some fabrics are too beautiful for mundane hands. It feels almost a crime that you, a mere mortal, should be allowed to hold such a material. To craft it into clothing is an act so sacred, that priests should be set up solely to handle this fabric.

At least that’s what some tailors believe.

Infinity cloth is so garish, so incoherently vibrant, that it induces a strange sort of psychosis into those who use it. They do not see the vulgar brightness of the colours, nor the incomprehensible combinations that would be a fashion crime in any other world. Instead, they see only shimmering colours and a sparkling iridescence that reaches somewhere inside of them and murders their sense of taste.

Infinity cloth is a beautiful blasphemy, handle with care.

FeatherBait.src: Some fish are drawn to feathers. Something about the colours and the way the water dances around them, it’s almost hypnotic to them.

LobsterBait.src: Some fish can only be attracted with a very expensive meal. Kind of like trying to date someone far out of your league. What better way to woo those with more refined palettes than a delicious lobster dinner?

PristineDesertSole.src:
Some fish were born to be hung on a plaque within somebody's house. The desert sole, flat as the wood that you're going to nail it onto, is one of those fish. Its eyes even follow you as you move around the house, like those paintings you hear about in haunted houses.

As a note, the attractive form of the pristine desert sole, and its flatness of course, means that it could have other uses. It makes for a fine doily, for example. You're free to use it as you please.

MediumWardstone.src: Some materials are better at resonating with souls than others. This is why a home made of better quality stones feels more comfortable than one made from pebbles. When used in wardstones, they allow for more powerful effects at no greater cost to the soul itself. Drawing out more of the ambient anima within a person, whilst minimizing the damage done.

SteakAndEggs.src: Some meals require silence. As you chew each mouthful, you reminisce on times past. On loved ones lost. On friends remembered. On moments that bring a smile to your face – simple and uncomplicated, without the weight of the world’s burdens crushing down on you. This is one of those meals.

IronPickaxe.src:
Some metals tower over others, laughing at the weakness of their lesser cousins. Iron is sturdy, strong and the foundation of many a civilisation. The metal makes strong bridges to cross dangerous waters. It can be smithed into tools, and weapons, stronger than any before.

An iron pickaxe is one such tool. The blade of the axe is hard and precise, delivering massive force at the point of impact. Few ores and stones can resist this power, which is why dwarves have long since favoured the iron pickaxe.

SteelFireArrows.src: Some people just want to watch the world burn! Some people want to watch the world burn, but have thought through the logistics of fire and so decide to set the world aflame from a distance. These arrows are popular among the latter category.

WeakEnergyPotion.src: Some times you just need an early morning pick me up. While many rely on the power of bitter brown beans, herblore masters have mastered the superior elixir. A shot of this fills the body with a sudden burst of adrenaline, banishing tiredness and filling their drinker with pep.

FerociusFurnace.src:
Some wizards study the stars. Some wizards investigate the ways in which an enchantment can be used to make beautiful art. Jillian Varden was only interested in fire. She would study it relentlessly, she created spells to warm the hearth and light candles from a distance.  But in her heart she wanted only one thing, to create a flame hotter than anyone else. 

The furnace was her answer and she spent weeks studying how one might push the flames harder and higher, so that metal might melt faster beneath their rage. She created a spell that would revolutionize smithing, yet she dreamed still of hotter flames. 

Soot was all that remained of her lab. Her body was never recovered.

GrilledTomatoes.src: Somehow still juicy, even after a judicious application of fire.

FeatheredLure.src: Sometimes a feather alone isn’t enough, there must be flavour as well. Delicious, sticky, berry juice is pressed into this lure, so that the taste of it might spread through the water and attract the attention of fish with fruitier palettes.

BluriteOre.src:
Sometimes colours just want to manifest themselves. There is the sweetness of orange. The cowardice of yellow, and the peaceful serenity of a summery green. Blue, tired with only being linked to sorrow and sadness, sought a physical existence. One that could be shaped into new and wonderous things, and so blurite was born.

A metal that is so very, very, blue.

It’s in the name. After all, it’s blue, right?

ArmouredCatfish.src:
Sometimes evolution is inspired by the wrong things. The catfish of Ashenfall have long been the victim of any creature that chooses to make them lunch. They are caught, cooked and consumed more often than is reasonable, and their suffering seemed too great as a result. So it was that a god took pity on them and armed them with a defence.

It is uncertain which god, for none have claimed responsibility, but the divine whimsy could have come from any of them. All we know is that the fish now have a chance against their assailants: an armoured hide to ward off some of the worst of their misery.

Sadly, they are no match for you.

Watermelon.src:
Sometimes it’s not enough to drink water, you desire the urge to chomp on it instead. These melons are delicious and refreshing in ways that few other fruits seem able to match.

Smashing one with a hammer is not recommended, but still manages to be weirdly satisfying.

SteelBarbedArrows.src: Sometimes it’s not enough to just kill your enemy. There are times when you really want them to suffer as well. Steel arrows are nasty enough, but covering them in deadly barbs that will rend the flesh and empty the liquid lifeforce of a person onto the forest floor? That’s just overkill.

OakSeed.src: Sometimes naming conventions are piffle. Yes, yes, we know the argument: it should be called 'oak seeds' so that players know it turns into an oak. But we all know that an oak seed is an acorn. Grow a spine, naming convention people!

WoodenSpade.src: Sometimes the very earth itself must be punished for its cruelty! These wooden tools, simple and elegant, can break through the planet’s crust, letting you show Gielinor exactly who’s boss.

Seeds.SwampWeed.src: Sometimes you don't want to grow pretty little flowers, you want to grow something you found in the murkiest corners of the world. Swamp weed, as it's name suggests, is normally found in the deadly swamps of Ashenfall, but with these seeds you can grow them from the comfort of your garden.

RawUndeadEel.src:
Sometimes, you have to ask yourself why you cook everything you find. Is this really going to make a succulent meal? Even dead it twitches occasionally, animated by some remnant of necromantic energy. Its flesh is partially decayed and the smell… oh the smell…

I recommend cooking it very, very thoroughly.

Seeds.Onion.src:
Sometimes you just want a way to make everyone around you cry. Onions have always served this purpose, and I often bring one with me to slice into at social gatherings when I feel everyone is being just a little too happy.

With these seeds, you can avoid scavenging for onions across the dangerous plains and instead produce a steady supply with them to torment your friends and family. Or you could eat them, I guess, if you’re weird.

Seeds.Cadavarberries.src:
Sometimes you just want to fill your garden with deadly berries. This was certainly true of Agnes DeWithlington-Smithe, a self-proclaimed “witch” with zero magical talent. She delighted in filling her garden with strange and dangerous herbs and flowers. The more poisonous, the better.

Locals would claim that she was a retired assassin, trying to hone her craft. In truth she just found something about the plants that she admired, and, ultimately, she thought they were pretty.

GroundSandstone.src: Sometimes you just want to prove how much better you are than a lump of rock, by grinding it down into a fine powder. Yeah, take that sandstone, you’re not all that tough as dust, are you?

BronzeMedHelm.src:
Sometimes you just want to wear a cube on your head and call it fashion. There's no shame in that, we all have our quirks. Why, I like to strut around my house with a raven-shaped walking cane and top hat on and no one's calling me weird - true, it's because anyone that does so is kneecapped and thrown into my basement oubliette, but they learn from their mistakes over time. 

Haha, did I say basement oubliette? I meant something entirely sane and normal, you don't need to worry. 

Now, these bronze helms are the very peak of rectangular fashion and, for just a few bronze bars, they're very cost-effective.

SuperFuelPellet.src: Sometimes, natural processes need a bit of a leg-up, a catalyst to get them firing. The super fuel pellet, though, is less of a leg-up and more several legs all the way up. It's an inverted centipede of a leg-up. So powerful is the super fuel pellet, it is believed that a bag of pellets could turn a runite mine into a reasonably decent blacksmith's shop with a single explosion.

CurseFragment.Vault.src: Sorrow can be a strength, misery can be might, despair can drive you to acts you would never have attempted before. This piece of a curse isn’t enough to push you into the darkness, but the chains of grief it forges give you a reason to fight, a purpose to push forward, if anything just to rid yourself of this burden.

BoneBolts.src: Special bolts whittled from bones, whilst only of use for a very specific crossbow, these bolts pack a surprising amount of punch.

Tomato.src: Squishy red little things, these fruits are a staple in sauces, salads or hurled at people in the stocks when you want to laugh at their misfortune.

ShimmeringScalePowder.src: Stare into the shimmer scale powder and it's like looking up into the night sky. Constellations form in the dust. Often, you'll see Moon Garou merchants idly stirring their stocks of shimmer scale powder, fascinated. It's not difficult to see how infinity cloth gets its many shimmering colours.

SteakSandwich.src:
Steak, if you ask me, is infinitely diminished by putting it between two slices of bread. Steak should stand proud on its own, garnished with salt and barely introduced to a flame.

As a journal-writer, I can't stop you. My powers are limited to shaming you from the dark recesses of your interfaces.

SteelCrossbowLimbs.src:
Steel crossbow limbs are sturdier than their counterparts, with a greater durability that allows them to create stronger and more dangerous crossbows.

Indeed, this durability seems to have put a nominal end to the unfortunate curse between cats and crossbow limb-related catastrophes.

As a result, in Fellhollow, cats still had a place in the home, even after they had been systematically outcast from Bramblemead. It was said that Xikotal, in particular, enjoyed the gentle purring noises that they made and would surround his lair with hundreds of the creatures so that he might be lulled into a gentle sleep.

WoodenClub.src: Sticks and stones may break your bones and this club is proof of the first bit. A large stuck that can be swung with impressive heft, capable of crushing bone with surprising ease. Popular by every warrior ever, when they're abandoned in the woods and need to defend themselves.

Stone.src: Sticks and stones may break your bones, which makes them greatly desired in warfare. Stone can be found everywhere. In the grass, behind bushes, hiding in an uncomfortable part of your shoe just waiting for the right time to strike.

TokTz-Mej-Tal.src:
Stone is not traditionally great at channelling magical energies. Stone is hard, solid and unchanging. Its shape can be carved away, but it will not bend, nor yield, only snap and crumble. Magic requires a more pliable medium to be used effectively.

Yet, the KotHaar are older creatures, to whom magic itself must bend. Creatures who were forged at the very birth of magic on Gielinor. The magic of the Elder Gods, to which all of creation must kneel.

This staff, the TokTz-Mej-Tal is older than the civilisations of Gielinor, and it still carries some of that old-world magic within it.

Try not to break it.

EnchantedIronBolts.src:
Stone remembers, wood forgets, iron holds a grudge. So goes the Imcamdo saying. A reference to how much stronger metal weapons were than wood and stone. Still, with magic, this adage can become painfully true.

The first enchanted iron bolts on Ashenfall were crafted by Lina Hesperian, one of the Amalgamated. She had hair that flowered like a waterfall down her spine. Her eyes were crystalline lakes, sparkling in the light, and her smile was as refreshing as any spring. She enchanted the bolts so that they might carry the gift of water, washing away infection for a clean and gentle kill. She made them for the hunters, so that they might claim their quarries with as little suffering as possible.

She met the end that far too many Amalgamated suffered. Alone, frightened, in the cold and the dark of an alley, her blood seeping from the knife wound in her chest. As she gave her last breath, she cursed the world for it’s cruelty, and the iron listened.

Now, each enchanted iron bolt taps into that grudge, inflicting a reminder of her suffering on any that feel the bolt’s sting.

PoisonDragonfireShield.src:
Strange magics have transformed the head of a tyrant, into a mystical adornment to this powerful shield. It is still strong, still durable and resists the fury of dragons, but now the shield seethes with Velgar’s wrath.

The magic of the shield is twisted into a bitter poison. One that yearns to strike and rage against any in its path. In battle, it’s possible to turn this poison on one’s enemies, afflicting them with a dragon’s hate.

Sometimes, in the dark, when the night is silent, it’s as if the shield whispers angry curses into the darkness. As if the last vestiges of Velgar’s fury are carried on the wind as hateful poison.

OakLogs.src: Stronger than ash, the oak tree strands proud against its lesser cousin. Oak logs are more durable, sturdier and more desirable for more advanced construction. Though the trees are harder to find in Brynmoor, it is said that Ghornfell offers more of them, if one is willing to face the dangers of exploring it.

AdamantCrossbowBolts.src:
Sturdy bolts of one of the most durable metals. Capable of piercing most armours with relative ease.

Have you considered what else those metal bars could be used for? You could create tools that would grow plants in these desolate lands. You could craft beautiful sculptures to bring joy to all who see them.

But, no, you went with murder spikes instead.

Though there are ruddy great dragons around the place, so I suppose it’s a fair plan.

OakPlanks.src: Sturdy lengths of oak, refined for use in construction projects. A popular material for any skilled architect.

SummonerFlament.src:
Summoner Flament's experiments were sanctioned by Alric but given a wide berth by everyone else. He was less interested in the comings and goings of demons – how to bring them into this world, how to shuffle them out – and more concerned with demonic behaviours. He wanted to see what the average avernic demon would do in any myriad of situations. What do they do when starved? How do they behave when in the company of other, non-avernic demons? Could they drown? Could they be dropped from a great height?

Summoner Flament had a pit. It was in that pit that he would keep his testing demons. He would get an allocation from the magi (who would shuffle away before they had to interact with Flament). Alric knew that Flament's works were unorthodox, but they did produce results that could be leveraged against the demons.

And it was from the top of the pit that Flament scratched notes, watched, and sang.

"Ten red demons, sitting in a pit. Ten red demons, sitting in a pit. And if one Black Knight should accidentally slip...

There'll be ten red demons, chewing on human bits."

There was madness in Summoner Flament before the Dreaming Stone shattered.

Anchovies.src: Surprisingly good on pizza, these salty little fish are a popular delicacy across Gielinor.

BraisedUndeadEel.src:
Sweet Saradomin on High, why on earth are you braising an undead eel? Are you a mind rune short of a rune pouch?

Perhaps it's a dare, and you're going to get a hefty payout after making it? I can't think of any other reason, sane or otherwise, why you would fish for the horrible, wriggly thing, pick it up afterwards and then braise it, which – we may add – is a process to DRAW OUT FLAVOURS. 

What next? Bury it in the ground for days and eat it afterwards? I would not put it past you.

Adhesive.src: Tacky like your great aunt’s wardrobe, this sticky substance has a wide range of uses when it comes to crafting.

BrokenTitansSword.src: Take Lord Rasmodel's broken sword. It's a suitable testament to him: robust and true, but shattered into pieces. You may even find the means to remake it.

DowdunReach.TheLake.src: Take a moment here to enjoy this quiet moment of beauty in a fortress of horrors. There is no deep lore, no hidden secrets, just a quiet calmness where it doesn’t belong. The world is full of spots like these, and they should always be protected.

Leather.src: Tanned animal hide has a distinctive smell and was surprisingly popular among some of the quieter villagers of Bramblemead. This versatile material can be used to craft a wide range of items, including armour and weapons.

DraconicLeather.src:
Tanned hide infused with a dragon’s vigor, draconic leather was a gamechanging discovery to the people of Fellhollow. It was as flexible as normal leather, but more resilient than even hardened leather, and it could be fashioned into a variety of shapes useful in a variety of armoured styles.

For a short while, the fashionistas of Emberwood village would use this leather to create garments that evoked the majesty of their draconic protectors, without bearing the scales that might cause undue offence.

TeaLeaves.src: Tea leaves have three uses, at least at the time of writing. The top survey answer is of course 'for making tea' - congratulations if you got that one. Then there's augury, using the tea leaves to divine the future. Finally - and this one's the pointless answer - if they are stuffed into someone's nostrils while they sleep, it will often induce the voiding of one's urine. It's true, go look it up. Information to hold back from your children, if you have any.

GameMeat.src: Tender meat, straight from the hunt. Traditionally you would hang the meat to dry out a little before consumption, marinating it in wines, spices and preservatives. However, you can lob it in a fire if you want a more immediate meal. We don’t judge.

Thammarith.src:
Thammarith has been to this festering plane before. He fought in the God Wars on the side of a chaotician called Zamorak.

He was no Tsutsaroth, so he could not command a position as a lieutenant or general. He never saw this Zamorak, whom he fought for. Rank and file was very much his place.

What he did see, though, was a sight that lingered. In a cave that glittered with ice, a winged woman flew. She cut through his fellow demons with speed, slicing before they could throw up claws in defence. He caught glimpses of her: stern looks and flashes of red; he carried those glimpses with him for centuries.

When he found himself back in Gielinor, summoned through an infernal gate, he was surprised by himself. His first thought was of that woman, and whether he might see her again. No matter what he did in the Reach, the thought could not be shaken. What had she done to him?

DoubleMeatSandwich.src: The 'twist' in the meat twist is a delightful redberry jus. The 'twist' in the Anima Twist is not, unfortunately, a delightful redberry jus.

BloodblightCape.src:
The Bloodblight swamp was once a pleasant place. Golden fields of wheat, rustling in the breeze. Life here was simple yet fulfilling.

Until Velgar took it all away.

He fought the mighty god of war, Bandos, and he should have lost. Dragons are powerful, and Velgar is stronger than most, but even in his most arrogant days he was no match for a god.

Yet, arrogance is not a mortal taint and the war god reeked of it. Bandos cast aside his wards. He refused to don his armour. The god pressed into the lair of the great dragon, and tried to wrestle him to the grave.

He nearly succeeded. Bandos wrapped his arms around the dragon’s serpentine neck and dug his fingernails beneath the scales. Velgar, in his writhing fury, called down a poison-filled rock from the heavens and cast it at Bandos, striking him in the temple. As the god reeled, he released Velgar, allowing the dragon to breathe a jet of anima-infused poison, at the unsteady god. Still wavering from the blow, Bandos breathed in the toxins and felt weakness for the first time in centuries.

A smart tactician, Bandos retreated. Better to face the shame of retreat, than risk the oblivion of death.

In his jubilant rage, Velgar spilled his blood on the once fertile plains, corrupting them with his hate-filled poison. The fields wilted. The crops blackened and then collapsed into venom.

This cloak, is reminder of that blighted day.

MapleWand.src:
The Brynmoor School of Magic fell to fire, and it didn't rally in another location. The school, it was said, had been losing money, and the wizards saw the fire as an opportunity to count their insurance money and cut any further losses. The students were left to apprentice elsewhere, if they could find the work, or practice their magic in other, ill-thought-out manners.

Upon the death of a foremost wizard, an old dean of the School of Magic, a chest was wheeled out. Inside were hundreds of sticks, wrapped in cloth. The wizard's family believed them to be incense sticks or diffusers - scented with holly berries, as per a decoration on the stick's base. The family sold them for a single gold piece each. A poster was attached to the front of the chest with the words 'Fire Sale - Incense Sticks' .

It is hard to describe the carnage that followed. The sticks were not incense but splitbark and maple wands, and those wands were intensely powerful. They were infused not with the smell of holly berries, but with the elements of fire, water, air and earth. When lit, they reacted explosively, and when held, they fired chaotically. Brynmoor was alight that night, and everyone had a different story of what happened to them, from stoves encased in rock to clothes blown clean off by air magic.

Most of the wands were discarded or destroyed. But a few found their way into the hands of commoners - those who were not allowed, or could not afford, to practice magic. Street urchins, scullery maids, chimney sweeps. Each of them had the beginnings of magic in their hands.

PoisonedFangArrows.src:
The Children of Shadows loved using these. The very notion of bone and poison combined as a weapon; it touched some deep dark part of themselves and filled them with a malicious sort of glee.

Alas such weapons proved relatively useless in any secret campaigns against the Saradominists of Bramblemead. Certainly, they could assassinate a baker if they needed to, but against a knight it would just ping harmlessly off their armour.

Still, they made for good talking points at the secretive meetings, making enjoyably sinister table-decorations that paired well with the wine and cheeses.

MapleStaff.src:
The Children of Shadows were never a grateful sort, but they would acknowledge that the groves of maple trees in Dowdun Reach were a boon. Almost everything wooden in the keep – from the library bookcases to the bannisters – was made from maple. 

Alric relished walking among the maple trees. For so much of his life, he had been encased in stone and surrounded by essence: working long hours in the keep. But the maples were for thinking. 

In his twilight years, Alric carried a maple staff with him: the Subjugation Staff. It was a crutch for an old man, yes, but it was also a way to bring the grove with him. When he couldn't muster the energy to visit his favoured trees, he carried a remnant with him.

DowdunReachCape.src:
The Dowdun Reach Cape is an emblem of your complete and utter mastery of Dowdun Reach. Congratulations.

You've seen things people wouldn't believe. You've attacked lesser blue dragons while on fire on the battlements. You've watched the Dreaming Stone glitter in the darkness near Dowdun Reach gate. All of these moments will be washed out in time, like a wet cape in rain.

BlackKnightTitan.src:
The Dreaming Stone had been shattered. 

Lord Rasmodel, on his knees, heard no voices. For the first time in too, too long, he could hear his own breath. His heart played a welcome beat. For decades, he had felt like he floated above the world. Now he was part of it again.

Footsteps. Lord Rasmodel lifted his head wearily. Who would interrupt this moment?

Ringing around him was his family. The Rasmodels. They were all there – all the ones he knew, loved and had met. They were dressed as the finest nobility, the Rasmodels at their height. They had regained their standing – the name meant something again. 

His father knelt down and lifted Lord Rasmodel's bloody chin. Their eyes met. "Rest," his father said. "We will take it from here."

Milliburn Rasmodel, twenty-fifth Lord of Rasmodel, took his retirement.

Kebab.src: The Drunken Dwarf delights in the humble Kebab, offering it to any who might catch his attention. The delicious combination of spices and subtle flavourings makes it a marvellous meal. For those afflicted, or self-inflicted, by particular poisonings, the Kebab is a time-honoured remedy.

Tok-Xil.src:
The Elder Gods are not subtle in their creations, and this is best exemplified in the Tok-Xil. Not considered part of the KotHaar caste, as such, this creature is more like living artillery, built purely for destruction.

In aeons past, these creatures would blast apart mountains, decimate forests and banish creatures back to nightmares. The world was a darker, scarier place, and needed deadlier and deadlier defences to push the evil back.

Recently - and by recently I mean in the last few thousand years - there has been much less need for the Tok-Xil in Ashenfall. They still stood as the guardians of the Lens, but it has been a long time since they last saw combat.

Fuzan, of course, changed all that.

Now, the Tok-Xil roam the desert sands, obliterating everything in their path. They are uncaring engines of destruction, slaying any living creature in their path.

FireMithrilArrows.src:
The Fogger's Gala was one of the few dates that a Black Knight could look forward to. An annual tradition, it would take place on the mistiest day of the year. As soon as low clouds started rolling in, word spread among the knights that it was Gala day.

It was an informal event on the battlements of the keep. There were quivers that represented each of the night's events, and the knights would name their arrows and place them in the quivers of those they wanted to participate in. Arrows were drawn randomly to determine the order. 

Sergeant Blister was on hand to take bets. He brought his blackboard, which he seemed to have on-hand when needed, and a week's wages were placed on friends and adversaries. 

The events all revolved around bows and crossbows. The fog made it almost impossible to see anything, so the Gala was a test of both memory and accuracy. One event required the archer to hit hay bales with fire arrows. The hay bales were invisible, so they had only location names to go by: the hut by the waterfall, Skrexis's bed. This meant firing Hail Mary's in the vague direction of their quarry, hoping that it would ignite in the night.

Other events included Pin the Arrow on the Goblin (as you can probably imagine, a noisy goblin ran about in the fog), Farthest Arrow and Alric's Curtains.

TzHaar-Ket-Om.src:
The KotHaar are practical creatures, not known for flights of fancy nor leaps of imagination. So, it makes sense that they would create a weapon like this.

The TzHaar-Ket-Om is  a large cylinder of obsidian, whose purpose is to be whacked against something with as much force as one can muster. The impact delivers enough kinetic energy to split rock, shatter bone and do tremendous damage to ones internal organs.

Elegant this weapon is not, but you cannot argue with its efficiency.

ObsidianLegs.src:
The KotHaar do not die as we do. There is no afterlife for them, just silence. They are reduced to fragments of obsidian, crushed down and down with the weight of their souls. Once returned to the Elder Kiln the KotHaar will live again, it just may take some time. Fortunately, time is irrelevant to the KotHaar and they are content to simply wait out the aeons until their time comes again. So, in a way, you do them a favour by wearing this obsidian armour, as it gives them a chance to see the world as they wait.

The joints and pivot points in this leg armour takes a little time to adjust to. They were originally moved by pneumatic systems of magma and rock, rather than the fleshy nonsense that comprises the human form.

Sturdy, strong and durable, these legs feel like they could wade through lava, and many have attempted to do so. Whether it worked well, none can say, because none who tried have managed to record their findings. Perhaps give it a try? What could go wrong?

ObsidianChest.src:
The KotHaar do not die as we do. There is no afterlife for them, just silence. They are reduced to fragments of obsidian, crushed down and down with the weight of their souls. Once returned to the Elder Kiln the KotHaar will live again, it just may take some time. Fortunately, time is irrelevant to the KotHaar and they are content to simply wait out the aeons until their time comes again. So, in a way, you do them a favour by wearing this obsidian armour, as it gives them a chance to see the world as they wait.

There is a common misconception that the KotHaar are a hive mind. Certainly many of them work as if they are one, but they are bound by a shared purpose, not a shared consciousness. This is a distinction that other races struggle with regularly, but it is easily understood when, as inevitably happens once in a while, one of the KotHaar turns away from their intended purpose and dares to wonder what else could be.

There are a few stories, hidden in the deserts, of KotHaar explorers found doing various things. They might spend days staring at a cactus, or they might dig through a mountainside to see what’s inside.

Perhaps this chest armour, that you now wear, might once have dreamed of being something other than its purpose. Now, perhaps, that dream has come true.

ObsidianHelm.src:
The KotHaar do not die as we do. There is no afterlife for them, just silence. They are reduced to fragments of obsidian, crushed down and down with the weight of their souls. Once returned to the Elder Kiln the KotHaar will live again, it just may take some time. Fortunately, time is irrelevant to the KotHaar and they are content to simply wait out the aeons until their time comes again. So, in a way, you do them a favour by wearing this obsidian armour, as it gives them a chance to see the world as they wait.

This helmet is durable, powerful and undeniably shiny. The obsidian glass reflects light in strange ways, glinting in a way that seems strange for such a dark material.

Moon Garou that prevail against the KotHaar do not wear the obsidian as armour, despite the obvious advantages. They worry that should they don the black glass, then they will find themselves possessed by whatever fire spirit animates the KotHaar, and the Moon Garou legends of fiery beings are not their happiest stories.

PieSwabbie.src:
The Moon Garou aren't particularly hot on pies. They like their dishes open and aromatic, engulfing all of the senses. A pie is the anti-garou dish: it disguises itself until its pastry is broken, and only then do you get that delicious waft of smells. It's a culinary jack-in-the-box.

Which is a shame, as I think the Moon Garou are really missing a trick. The ripe smell of a desert sole is particularly suited to pies, as it ambushes the eater when they break the seal. That's where the 'swabby' comes in, as eaters will often have to wipe their eyes from the olfactory assault.

Keris.src:
The Moon Garou believe this weapon was given to them by a goddess of the river, who took the desperate garou and raised them up to become masters of the desert sands. The weapon was created as a  tool against one of the deadliest denizens of the dunes – the kalphites.

The blade tip can find its way through the chinks in the Kalphite exoskeleton, piercing through the chitinous armour and damaging the much squishier flesh beneath. It was turned many a battle against the Kalphites from a garou bloodbath, to a garou victory banquet – though they  tend to find the Kalphite meat a little less appetising then they’d like.

Moon Garou champions are gifted the Keris dagger after achieving a great victory. It is a symbol of their bravery and marks them as skilled warriors to all the other tribes. In olden times, a bearer of the Keris would be treated with great respect. They would be given food, lodging and anything else they needed to further their victories.

Nowadays, however, the Keris is seen more as a tool of survival against the insectoid foe.

BeltfishBroth.src:
The Moon Garou don't like to waste a kill. Every last organ and morsel of flesh is eaten or used in some capacity, in honour of the creature that surrendered its life.

In that spirit, beltfish broth is the final stop for a beltfish's innards. Eyeballs, teeth, fins, organs and even the odd parasite ("tapeworm, tapeworm, you make my belly squirm", as the garou song goes) are boiled and served in this delightful dish.

CookedMonkfish.src:
The Moon Garou don't recognise the term 'monk'. It's very much a Saradominist or Zamorakian term (strange how the customs of the two gods are so similar, don't you think?). The Moon Garou are more shamanistic, and do not understand or care for things like 'denying yourself worldly pleasures'. It is their belief that when there are so few fruits and treasures in the desert, why would someone possibly deny themselves a moment of enjoyment?

Which raises the question of why the Moon Garou call these fish 'monkfish' at all. Well, the answer is a little on the boring, perhaps even obvious side. The River Goddess, who many Moon Garou worship, came to Ashenfall from mainland Gielinor, where the monkfish are more prevalent. So she pointed at the fish, said its name, and Bob's your monkfish.

AdamantMedHelm.src:
The Moon Garou have crafted impressive suits of armour. Stylish, elegant, and sturdy. One of their blacksmiths experimented with the medium helm, and earned much mockery from his tribe. 

True, the helm was sturdy and turned aside arrow and blade alike, but it lacked the grace and style of the traditional adamant armour, given that it was so very, very square. 

Still, he would be most glad to have crafted it, for on one sandstorm-heavy evening, it was the only thing that saved him when the kalphites attacked. They were brutal, they were cruel, they tore apart the rest of his caravan in moments, yet his helm stood strong against the maw of one of their number, and they abandoned him when they realised how much effort eating him would be.

PharaohsSceptre.src:
The Moon Garou tried the whole Pharaoh concept exactly once. Unused to non-violent systems of government, they gathered together as a people and pulled stones from a bag to decide who was the luckiest of all of them, and therefore who deserved to rule.

It was, as you can imagine, not a smart system of governance.

The winner was a garou called Hakanaten, and he did not want the job. He had always been an outsider, far more interested with the goings on of the nearby Kalphite hives then he was with the goings on of the city. Still, he had been chosen by an assumption of destiny and was set upon a throne with crown and sceptre in hand.

He hated it. He made decisions as best he could, but could never please everyone. If he tried to help one person, it angered another. If he cast judgement on a lawbreaker, he was deemed cruel by some and weak by others. No matter what he tried, he only found himself more and more isolated from his kin.

In the end a revolt saw him deposed and the throne destroyed. He was cast into the hive he so adored, where he was expected not to live for long. Yet, he had studied the hive and he could mimic their behaviours better than some of his own people’s. He helped them dig tunnels. He joined them on hunts. He lived a life far happier among the hive then he ever did at home.

The sceptre, that had been cast down with him, carries with it a measure of his fondness for the insects. It is said that anyone who wields it, can call on the hive for aid, in memory of an unlucky monarch.

RangerTunic.src:
The Nightingale was the bane of the nobility, and they became obsessed with her destruction. Not just her capture, they needed her obliterated – gone from the memories of the population forever. But this was a tricky task indeed, because the wealth the Nightingale harvested, was given back to the people of Bramblemead, rather than lining her own coffers, making her a local hero.

So they hired Moragrin the hunter to track her down. Moragrin was a cruel and merciless assassin, trained in multiple weapon techniques. She delighted in little more than seeing the look in her victims eyes the moment they transition from living to dead.

For days she followed stories of Nightingale, wandering through the village, adopting multiple disguises that she might uncover Nightingale’s real name. In all that time she learned only one thing, that the villagers loved Nightingale and would never knowingly give her up.

PoisonedMithrilArrows.src:
The Rasmodels were notorious for their use of poison. When they lived to the south, in Temple Woods and Bramblemead, it was often said that you should cover your cup, mouth and ears around a Rasmodel. One of the family was finally caught red-handed (or green-handed, considering the poison used), and the rumour became fact. They were banished to Dowdun. 

Their reputation followed them, but became more gift than curse. No one in Dowdun Reach wanted to cross the Rasmodels, for fear of waking up in spasms. 

We say that it was mostly a gift because of an event between a young Lord Rasmodel and his cousin. Lord Rasmodel claimed that he could shoot an apple from the top of his cousin's head, and promptly did so. He handed one of the resulting apple-halves to his cousin, who ate it and promptly keeled over and died.

It turned out that the arrow used to the cleave the apple was poisoned. Lord Rasmodel claimed that he had been using his father's hunting arrows, and one of them must have been tainted. It seemed entirely plausible.

But there was still doubt. And that doubt grew into a reputation: a reputation that outmatched his own family's. Even at the age of eight, the inhabitants of Dowdun Reach gave Lord Rasmodel a wide berth.

RotswornMarauder.src:
The Scalesworn were heroes. Only the strongest, most skilled and powerful marauders would be chosen by Xikotal to act as guardians of the dragons. They would guard the great beasts as they slept, standing strong against any force that might try to do them harm.

They were blessed with the mark of the dragon, granting them some of the power of their draconic masters.

These marks would be their undoing, when Imaru refused to stay dead. They became the first of the infected, inflicted with a terrible withering curse that would drag the souls of any they touched into Imaru’s hungry maw.

BlackKnightBody.src:
The Shadow Knights, or Black Knights, as they would come to be known, were mostly melee and ranged fighters. When magic was needed, they would enlist Alric's magi, but that secondment was always short. The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate.

Archmage Alric came to Lord Rasmodel with a sheet of paper. It was morning, when the Master of Dowdun was most impatient. 

Alric had been monitoring the Black Knights. He had suspected something for years now, but today he had proof. The sheet was from a ledger, and it accounted for the number of magi casualties since Alric had become Archmage. There had been one hundred and seventeen deaths from one hundred and seventeen incidents. There was no single incident ion which more than one mage died. 

Alric was in a fury, tossing papers and spitting curses. It was proof that the Shadow Knights were deliberately negligent, that they saw the magi as disposable. Lord Rasmodel kept silent, and let the mage rampage.

The orders went out from Lord Rasmodel the next day. All Shadow Knights were to allow two magi to die with each incident.

BlackKnightCowl.src:
The Shadow Knights, or Black Knights, as they would come to be known, were mostly melee and ranged fighters. When magic was needed, they would enlist Alric's magi, but that secondment was always short. The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate.

Lord Rasmodel gave his Black Knights two sets of orders. The first they were free to discuss, and were encouraged to do so. They were there to protect the magi from the demons. Should one break from its bindings, it was to be put down. In an outbreak situation, the Shadow Knights had full jurisdiction and freedom to kill with impunity.

The second set of orders was not to be discussed, not even in the company of another. There were two salient instructions. 

Instruction 1: The Shadow Knights would allow for the "Demon's Share". Should a demon become unruly, a single mage fatality was encouraged before the demon was to be put down. It was like the culling of rabbits. The mage numbers needed to be managed. 

Instruction 2: Should the flow of demons be too much for the magi to control, the Shadow Knights were to collapse the infernal portal. This was the primary directive: the demons and magi were secondary.

BlackKnightChaps.src:
The Shadow Knights, or Black Knights, as they would come to be known, were mostly melee and ranged fighters. When magic was needed, they would enlist Alric's magi, but that secondment was always short. The melee knights were mostly posted in the grounds, but the ranged knights had a different role: they were stationed around the demon gate.

Lord Rasmodel's greatest challenge came from within. It did not carry a sword or crossbow. 

The Shadow Knight numbers were dropping. It was impossible to resign from the order – that was written in the charter – but more and more of the knights were falling into madness. If it were physical wounds, Lord Rasmodel could have done something about the epidemic. He could amputate the problem with a single swing of his sword. But his enemy was intangible. 

He decided to visit those on the precipice of madness. Most were unintelligible, but some talked of food not satisfying them anymore. Others called out to the Dreaming Stone, like it was their mother, as if it would save them. In many cases, it sounded like the afflicted were arguing with themselves: two enemies unleashing an enmity. 

One of the mindless disquieted Lord Rasmodel more than the others. She was an afflicted soldier that he knew from long ago. She rambled in a voice that mimicked the droning of a bored aristocrat. Lord Rasmodel knew that voice well. He stumbled from the bedside of the soldier and took no other visitors that day.

BronzeGreatsword.src:
The Wild Knight Kessel was unusual in her choice of weaponry. Where most of the order chose to wield bows, daggers, or swift blades, Kessel favoured a bronze greatsword. On the battlefield, she hefted it across her shoulders, never letting the hilt leave her grip.  

As one of the Amalgamated, Kessel’s skin glowed like burning coals, her battle scars resembling faint reddish embers. She harnessed this heat, channelling it through her sword. Her magic set the blade ablaze, a sight that struck terror into the hearts of her enemies. With great arcs of red flame, she cleaved through enemy forces, incinerating them as she severed their limbs from their bodies. 

On one fateful day, she would use this technique against a force of garou hunters. The battle was long, hard, and brutal, and both sides faced great casualties. But it was when she sliced her blade across the young garou prince that war was inevitable.

AmuletOfAccuracy.src:
The Wild Knights knew the dangers of missing their target. If an arrow did not slay its target quickly, then too soon would the quarry either escape, or, worse, gather friends. Wolf packs could easily tear a small group of Knights to pieces if not dealt with fast.

The Amulet of Accuracy made sure that hunts went smoothly. When a shot landed, it landed hard. Alpha wolves would be slain in a single well-placed shot, and sturdier threats might go down in a small flurry of arrows.

When Silverthorn Keep stood against the rising horde of zombies, these amulets were worn by the keep defenders who unleashed a torrent of arrows into the hungry dead.

Treequipment.src:
The Wild Knights often spent weeks at a time alone in the wilderness, surviving on nothing but what they can forage and hunt. But tools and weapons, are subject to the curse of entropy and more than a few times a Wild Knight would find themselves alone and miles from civilisation, with a broken axe-shaft in hand. Death would often follow swiftly after. 

The druids among them, created this spell to save their brethren. It would transform a tree into supplies enough to let the knight return home, where they could repair their equipment properly. 

Although not as flashy as a fire-blast, this spell has saved more lives than most and it's creator is still toasted by the Wild Knights on their nights of celebration.

InspiringAmuletOfRanged.ArchersAmulet.src:
The Wild Knights used many tools and tricks in their hunts. Looking for any edge they might have against the untamed wilds of Ashenfall. One jeweller, a water-Amalgamated by the name of Lochlan, created an amulet imbued with the communal spirit of the hunters. He would leave the gemstone, that would serve as its base, in the gathering hall and soon it became a tradition for each hunter to touch the gemstone if their hunt was successful.

Over the years this gemstone took on their pride, prowess and skill and that became a magical enchantment that lay within the heart of the stone. Crafting an amulet from the crystal, Lochlan found a way of sharing that enchantment with everyone who wore it.

Now, millennia later, the echoes of that enchantment linger within the crystals, just waiting for someone to remember them.

WildArchersBody.src:
The Wild Knights were known for their ability to scout the wild areas of Ashenfall. They could walk where no one else dared to tread, and they were masters of the hunt – putting even the garou to shame.
