Their archers wore sturdy leathers, using carefully laid folds to shield them against harm. These would break easily, but the archers made it part of their ritual to maintain them regularly. Each day, they would wake and tend to the leather, making their armour seem brand new with each morning.

Archers of the Wild Knights were quick, silent and deadly. A joke their more melee-focused companions used to raise on those rare occasions when the knights would gather. Drink and company lead to banter and poor jokes, which created much missed laughter that the Wild Knights always enjoyed.

Archer, warrior or mage, the Wild Knights would hurl jibes at one another, without a moment’s thought. Yet, when needed, there was no stronger camaraderie and they would all die for one another.

WildArchersLegs.src:
The Wild Knights were known for their ability to scout the wild areas of Ashenfall. They could walk where no one else dared to tread, and they were masters of the hunt – putting even the garou to shame.

Their archers wore sturdy leathers, using carefully laid folds to shield them against harm. These would break easily, but the archers made it part of their ritual to maintain them regularly. Each day, they would wake and tend to the leather, making their armour seem brand new with each morning.

Archers worked alone, it was easier that way. They could stalk their prey, silently and slowly, sometimes taking days between kills, as they followed their quarry through the lands. They would hunt monsters and people with equal focus, as dictated by the order’s commands.

To harm the wilds was to make yourself a target of the Wild Knights. To sully the green lands of Guthix, an unforgivable crime. Yet, there were always those who would risk their ire, wannabe despots and greedy fools yearning to plunder the realm.

They all met the fate they deserved, in the end.

WildArchersHelm.src:
The Wild Knights were known for their ability to scout the wild areas of Ashenfall. They could walk where no one else dared to tread, and they were masters of the hunt – putting even the garou to shame.

Their archers wore sturdy leathers, using carefully laid folds to shield them against harm. These would break easily, but the archers made it part of their ritual to maintain them regularly. Each day, they would wake and tend to the leather, making their armour seem brand new with each morning.

The helm is designed to focus the wearer’s vision, so that their target receives all their attention. Distractions are cut from the picture. Everything exterior to their quarry is removed from view. The archer’s sight is trained on their victim and, so the rumours claimed, they never missed their mark.

PoisonedBronzeArrows.src:
The Wild Knights were not above poison, any edge in a battle was worth having. Poison meant that you could take down a dangerous beast, even if your initial shot wasn’t a mortal one.

The druids among the order felt little concern over its use either, after all nature is filled with wielders of poison and so the Wild Knight archers were simply emulating nature’s tools.

FortifyingHeartySoup.src: The Wild Knights would prepare this soup before heading into the poisonous Bloodblight Swamp, or when facing venomous monsters. The mushrooms would absorb some of the toxins they encountered, and the soup would be filling enough to last them through the long journeys.

GoldCape.src:
The Wise Old Man has a saying that feels applicable here: 'modesty is overrated'. His argument is that we celebrate modesty and assume that there's some kind of value to it, but it rarely, if ever, has any value at all. No one has cashed in their modesty for a great benefit. Modesty isn't the cornerstone of any great achievement in the world. Some people may like you a little more, but - and this is the Wise Old Man we're quoting, mind you - 'being liked is overrated for all the same reasons'. 

What the WOM is saying is that you shouldn't feel guilty wearing your gold cape. Modesty is overrated. Enjoy yourself!

RawSalmon.src: The Wushanko islanders are masters of turning this into a delicious and satisfying meal. Alas, you never did take the time to study their culinary ways and must apply heat to this meal, lest you eject your internalised failures upon Ashenfall’s soil.

AbyssalWhip.src:
The abyssal demon is a foul beast. A single one can massacre a village before the warning bell can even sound. Crafting a weapon from their remains symbolizes triumph against adversity or perhaps just hubris in its purest form. 

Infused with the hate of the demon, each whip crack generates unbearable pain. Victims find themselves overcome with suffering as the agony seeps into the wounds the whips leave behind. 

It is said that the whip even feeds on that misery, growing stronger with each strike, each life taken. The hate imbues the weapon with a desire to inflict more pain, and it grows stronger each time such a wish is granted. Or, so the legends say. 

Only one Wild Knight has ever chosen to wield the whip in vengeance against the demon for a fallen sibling. Her name is dust in the wind of history, but there are still creatures that hide in the shadows, afraid of the crack of her whip.

Windstep.src:
The air can be wrapped as a cloak around you, making heights much less scary to face. Once, long ago, young druids would use windstep to hurl themselves from atop the highest mountains, descending to the ground below. Higher and higher they would climb, each trying to outdo the other. Until the inevitable finally intervened. 

Since that tragic day, it has been well known that there is a limit to the height at which Windstep might protect someone. They call it the splat-limit, because druids are very bad with names.

InspiringRingOfFarming.FarmersRing.src:
The ancient Potteringtons, a lineage of strange old women that dates back as far as recorded history, consider farming to be a sacred art. It is said that under a full moon they consume a tea brewed from the first leaves to grow on Gielinor, and in doing so are imparted inscrutable farming wisdom.

Nonsense, perhaps, yet this ring contains a single bead of that mystical tea and those who wear it find themselves agriculturally inspired.

AnglersHat.src:
The angler's hat has two very important uses. The first is there's a chance to not reduce the number of fish in the pool when catching. 

The second is perhaps more important. When passing a fellow angler, you can participate in the age-old gesture of doffing. No words, just a silent acknowledgment of each other's presence as you partake in a doffing custom that has spanned centuries.

GhornfellPlains.src:
The anima of Ghornfell is less table than that of Brynmoor, and the anima twist’s effects are more pronounced. Plants take on the hues of dragonfire, making the entire region dance like an inferno when the summer wind blows.

Towering in the distance is a great tower, shattered now yet still imbued with ancient dragonkin magic. A terrible roaring can be heard from this structure and a shadow passes over it when General Velgar returns. The dragon makes his lair in the remains of a dragonkin’s hubris, a monument to an architect long since dead.

Garou make their homes across this region, sending out hunting parties to slaughter anything that crosses their path.

Atop the mesa, something glistens in the moonlight and a mournful sound carries on the wind. A sorrow that resonates in shimmering crystal.

FireSpirit.src:
The aviansie believe in five types of spirit, those of the water, earth, light, storm and fire. The spirits of fire governed inspiration and creativity and were known among the aviansie people as the Gal'Son – the passionate. While perhaps not replicating the dancing spirits of legend, the fire spirit that this spell calls is no less passionate about being helpful. It loves little more than lighting your way and shielding you, as best it can, from the cold. 

In truth, this spell does not create a fire spirit, rather the runes attract nearby motes of elemental fire, bringing them together into a single entity. Each spirit is more like a colony of tiny lights, ready to banish the shadows in the darkest places.

Armadyl.src:
The aviansie deity, Armadyl, is know as the god of justice. Though young, by god standards, and naïve by many others, Armadyl has a devoted following due to his care for his people.

In the god wars, he perhaps most of all, suffered at the hands of Zamorak, for when Zamorak destroyed Forinthry, it took Armadyl’s people with it. Whole settlements were wiped out in a single sweeping motion, thousands of the aviansie reduced to ash. Including Armadyl’s own husband.

Since the edicts, Armadyl has had a change of heart. While he will fight if he has to, he prefers a more peaceful path. He returned to Gielinor to put a stop to Bandos’ warmongering, preventing him from turning the planet into a war-torn wreck. Though Armadyl holds peace as the highest virtue, he was not afraid to kill the god of war.

On Ashenfall, Armadyl and his people did not take part in the dragon conflict. They disappeared deeper into the mainland and have not been heard of for centuries. Though Armadyl has left Gielinor and returned to the world of his people, there are rumours of winged beings living further into the continent.

BarbedBronzeArrows.src:
The barbed bronze arrow was the ammunition of choice for the hunting party of Lord Gawurin, the regent of Ashenfall. He and his hunting party would head out into the woods alongside a small contingent of White Knight bodyguards. The lord would hunt deer, boars and other game there, but he wasn’t the most accurate shot. 

This arrow was designed for bloodletting, meaning he only needed any hit to begin the prey’s downfall. A single strike would start them bleeding, slowing them down and making them easier to hunt. The hunt outcome was all but inevitable. Poor sport, some would whisper, but the lord cared only for the end result. 

It’s perhaps fitting, then, that Lord Gawurin would be hunted with his own arrows on the night of Falling Embers.

Beltfish.src:
The beltfish, or 'largehead hairtail' if you want to get fancy, is no replacement for a real belt. Anglers have been known to break their belts mid-fishing session and will look into their buckets, wondering if the beltfish 'might do'. Yes, I know - there's no helping some people. 

But if you are tempted, here are the reasons why a beltfish is a sub-par belt. 

1. The beltfish is actually a bit of a chonker. It doesn't fit through the loops in your trousers.
2. The smell of a beltfish is riper than your average fish. That ripeness only escalates as the hours go on.
3. Nobody is going to be impressed with your fish-eye belt buckle.
4. An eel is actually a more functional belt.

Infusion.CoolingRelentless.src: The best archers in the world are often said to have ice in their veins. It's an odd idiom - you would imagine that would be both uncomfortable and give an archer the shivers, precisely what they wouldn't want - but it's meant to indicate a steeliness, a cold efficiency. Well, imagine applying a tap (or faucet, if that's your orientation) to an archer and draining them for a drink. That would be the cooling relentless infusion.

Secateurs.src:
The best way to get leaves to stay healthy, is to instil within them a healthy sense of fear. By pruning away the leaves that have allowed themselves to fall to weakness, frailty and disease, you show the other leaves what happens if they don’t behave.

I find that whispering their failures to the plant, as I slice away parts of their extremities, emboldens the plant with a desire to thrive.

Whetstone.src:
The blade is not just a weapon in the wilds of Ashenfall, it’s a tool. Sometimes it’s the difference between seeing tomorrow and having a very bad today. 

Dwarves have always understood the importance of properly maintaining one’s equipment. They turned the care for their weapons into a ritual of almost religious significance. Blades would be cleaned, serviced and sharpened so that they might cut through deadlier dangers and challenge greater threats. 

The whetstone is a simple device, but one that served as a backbone of this ritual. A smith would learn to gently sharpen the blade to the thinnest edge possible, treating it almost like a competition. They would boast and brag with each other about the sharpness of their blades. 

A popular dwarven myth speaks of the Prime Whetstone, capable of sharpening a blade to the point that no armour or metal could withstand it. Sadly, or perhaps thankfully, no evidence exists to provide any truth to the myth.

DragonBlood.src: The blood of a dragon is a strange thing. It is infused with magic in a way that most other creatures can’t match, a side effect of the alchemical processes that created their kind. Dragonkin scientists needed blood that could adapt to a wide range of chimeric additions to the body. As such dragon blood, unlike human blood, doesn’t possess any particular type and each could act as donor to the other.

BronzeArrowBroadhead.src:
The broad-headed bronze arrow was the ammunition of choice for the hunting party of Lord Gawurin, the regent of Ashenfall. He and his hunting party would head out into the woods alongside a small contingent of White Knight bodyguards. The lord would hunt deer, boars and other game there, but he wasn’t the most accurate shot. 

The broadhead of the arrow was designed for bloodletting, meaning he only needed any hit to begin the prey’s downfall. A single strike would start them bleeding, slowing them down and making them easier to hunt. The hunt outcome was all but inevitable. Poor sport, some would whisper, but the lore cared only for the end result. 

It’s perhaps fitting, then, that Lord Gawurin would be hunted with his own arrows on the night of Falling Embers.

BronzeMace.src:
The bronze guard defended the alliance between the followers of Guthix and the followers of Saradomin. The metal symbolized the unity of two different materials and created something stronger. While most of the guards preferred the noble sword, a few preferred the physicality of the bronze mace. 

Each swing delivered powerful momentum straight into their enemy. The force broke bone, obliterated muscle, and often sent their victims reeling, allowing a second strike before the foe could recover. 

There was a mountain of a man known as The Cairn, for his skill at delivering people to one, who favoured the mace over more noble weapons. He crushed anyone who defied the alliance, providing the force of justice with each swing of the mace. 

When he was asked to turn his fury on the priests of Guthix, it was the one time he stayed his hand.

BunnyCactusSeed.src:
The bunny cactus isn't only named that way because of its rabbit-ear-like limbs. It's also a prolific reproducer. A single plant can produce dozens of seeds, and in turn it can create dozens of bunny cacti. 

Now I think of it, the bunny cactus also develops little tufts of fur on its spikes, reminiscent of a rabbit's cotton tail. Damn, they really nailed the naming of this cactus.

DorgeshuunCrossbow.src:
The cave goblins are a practical sort, using materials more readily available underground than any that might require potential damage to their subterranean dwellings, such as mining. This crossbow is made from bones, traditionally of creatures found beneath the surface.

Zanik once used this crossbow to defeat a deadly spectre in the underworld. A being infused with some dread malign power, that threatened the denizens of Um. Normal weapons had no effect on the creature, yet for some reason the bone bolts fired by this crossbow were enough to unravel its material form, banishing it back to the darkness.

WoodenShield.src:
The children of Bramblemead loved nothing more than to craft themselves wooden shields and swords and then challenge one another to single combat. They would play the roles of brave heroes against dastardly villains, whacking one another with their wooden toys. It gave the local healers constant work. 

Yey, a wooden shield is no toy and has saved the lives of countless warriors. As a beast’s claws slice against you, having a hunk of wood between you and the creature is much appreciated. Wood splinters, but flesh bleeds, and blood is less easily replaced than timber.

SteelDagger.src:
The children of darkness were very fond of steel daggers. They were powerful, dangerous and very expensive at the time, making them the perfect ritual tool to demonstrate their adoration of the god of chaos.

Mostly the offspring of wealthy families, the rituals of the Children were performed out of boredom more than religious fervour. They would gather at secret meetings and proudly display their elaborately carved daggers, trying to prove to each other who was the most devoted to the lord of darkness by way of expensive kitchenware.

If you asked any of them to use such a blade in battle, they would be more inclined to slit their own throats in fear, rather than mutilate their opponents.

WeakAntifreezePotion.src:
The cold is a terrible force, responsible for countless deaths each year. The chill of winter seeps into a home and snuffs the life out of those who haven’t made adequate provisions. It was the herblore expert Valius Malone who created the first antifreeze potion, that held back the claws of winter’s grasp.

It was only years after his death, that it was discovered he only created the potion because the ingredients were cheaper than the lumber needed to keep his fire burning.

BronzeCrossbowLimbs.src:
The complicated mechanisms of the crossbow sparked a small technological revolution in Bramblemead. Such devices had once been the domain of the dwarves, who guarded their advanced techniques to maintain their smithing dominion. However, soon human smiths found themselves creating these complex trigger mechanisms.

There were casualties, certainly. Some mechanisms tightened strings too greatly, snapping back with a force that could cause serious harm.

One notable example involved the pet belonging to the village priest, a curious feline with absolutely no sense of self-preservation. The cat entered the workshop, as she so often did, and took it upon herself to knock everything she could to the floor. Unfortunately, in doing so, she triggered the release mechanism being worked on and quickly learned that cats are not meant to fly.

CorpseCotton.src:
The corpse flower is a strange creature. Strange, almost flesh-like sacks, filled with a noxious gas that explodes upon contact with the air. The resulting mass of fibres looks disturbingly like thin strips of a cadaver’s skin, earning it the name “corpse cotton” by the more macabre Emberwood villagers.

In truth it’s little more than thick plant fibres that can be woven together into a smooth, durable and, frankly, fashionable fabric.

BlackKnightCrossbow.src:
The crossbow is the ranged preference of the Black Knight, mainly thanks to its stopping power. An avernic demon will rush a target at distance and then slash at close quarters. Having a crossbow stops a demon from getting to that troublesome second stage.

Our assumption is that you are not a demon, but the sentiment still applies. You will want to avoid a crossbow-wielding Black Knight at distance and, instead, move in for a spot of slashing. You need to search for the demon inside yourself.

CrystalSeed.src:
The crystal tree is a magical thing, a native to the elven world Tarddiad and brought to Gielinor when the elves migrated. Unlike most seeds it is nourished not by soil, nor sunlight, but by music. Elf song reaches into the crystal, creating a harmonious resonance that causes the crystal to thrive.

As well as growing trees, this seed can also be sung into specific shapes and forms, becoming a tool or weapon of great power.

This seed is a little different to those found in Tirannwn, infused both with the magic of Ashenfall, but also the essence of cherished memories.

RotswornReanimator.src:
The curse of Fellhollow is crueller than it might seem on the surface. Those who pass on within proximity of Imaru's hunger find their souls face to face with the ravening maw of a dread beast that wants nothing more than to consume their souls. This, unsurprisingly, is upsetting and frightening to just about anyone that sees it, and most flee from the river Noumenon, rather than face that nightmare. Yet, a soul must travel the river to reach the afterlife, lest they lose themselves, their focus and their memories, becoming little more than an animating force that refuses death. 

Most of Fellhollow now suffers this affliction, but some suffer more than others. The reanimator refuses to die: it will do everything in its power to avoid Imaru's maw. With each death, it clings to new flesh, dragging new corpses into the conflict, and desperately tries to claw out even a few extra moments of unlife. Each time it's slain, the soul is damaged further and further, until eventually there's barely anything left for Imaru to consume.

CookedBeltfish.src: The custom with a steamed beltfish is to eat it all in one, like a sword-eater swallowing their blade whole. The Moon Garou chomp it down like they were raised by pythons. The human gullet isn't quite built for this method of eating, so be careful if you're invited over for a Moon Garou celebration. Aim for the smaller ones at the banquet table. Chew subtly.

Zombie.src:
The dead should not move like this, yet these creatures don’t seem to have gotten that message. Undead are normally animated by magic, though some are motivated by stranger things.

These undead are animated by hunger, and the desperate final moments of what is left of their soul. Regrets, need and pain drive muscle, sinew and bone into motion, creating this most pitiable of creatures.

MonstrousFangs.src: The deadly canines of a large creature. Much more fun when they’re not still in the snapping maw of the creature chasing you.

FleetfootedInfusion.src: The deer of Ashenfall are quick and nimble, able to dash across entire regions at the drop of a hat. Boiling the tainted water of Ashenfall with a deer’s antlers, draws some of this swiftness essence into the clean water, granting the drinker a measure of that fleet-footed nature.

DwellberryInfusion.src: Delicious dwellberry infuses water with a delightful flavour. It’s easier and far more refreshing and hydrating than normal water.

DesertRobes.src:
The desert is a cruel and unforgiving place, and that was before Fuzan corrupted the sun against it. Dry air, filled with sand particles, leech all moisture from the body, leaving you dehydrated, exhausted and with no respite in view. Oases can be mirages, tricks played by the dunes to lure you deeper into your own destruction. These robes help to limit some of the desert’s power, through ancient tricks learned by those who have dwelled within the dunes for generations.

Robes are freeing, allowing the body to breathe and allowing moisture to evaporate, cooling you down. They’re also easy to brush down, expelling sand that has crept its way into all the most uncomfortable parts.

This desert outfit was apparently passed down to the Moon Garou by the River Mother, who brought the lessons she had learned from her own deserts with her. She taught them how to craft them, how to fold the patterns for best effect and she taught the Moon Garou how to dance in them.

On rare festivals, the Moon Garou will attach ribbons, bells and obsidian glass shards to their robes. When they dance it creates a glorious swirling medley of colour, sound and glittering sparkles.

DesertHood.src:
The desert is a cruel and unforgiving place, and that was before Fuzan corrupted the sun against it. Dry air, filled with sand particles, leech all moisture from the body, leaving you dehydrated, exhausted and with no respite in view. Oases can be mirages, tricks played by the dunes to lure you deeper into your own destruction. These robes help to limit some of the desert’s power, through ancient tricks learned by those who have dwelled within the dunes for generations.

The hood is the most basic necessity of the desert. It shields the top of one’s head from the sun’s cruel ministrations, acting as a barrier between sunstroke and you. The hood also helps protect against particulates of sand that have been stirred up by meagre breezes.

The overhanging fabric shields the eyes from the light, just a little. A tiny point of shade in a glaring light that’s almost crushing in its brightness.

Finally, they’re surprisingly fashionable, everyone should try one.

DesertLegs.src:
The desert is a cruel and unforgiving place, and that was before Fuzan corrupted the sun against it. Dry air, filled with sand particles, leech all moisture from the body, leaving you dehydrated, exhausted and with no respite in view. Oases can be mirages, tricks played by the dunes to lure you deeper into your own destruction. These robes help to limit some of the desert’s power, through ancient tricks learned by those who have dwelled within the dunes for generations.

These simple leggings are all that stands between you and obliteration by a sandstorm. Sand can be sharp, it can be abrasive and, given time, it can wear a person down to nothing but the memory of them in another person’s mind.

Cloth won’t stop that, not really, but it will delay the obliteration long enough for you to get to shelter when the worst of the storm hits. You’ll still want to run, though.

MapleInfusion.src: The distilled strength of a maple tree, pumped straight to your dietary tract. You might fell a rising fury whenever you stare at a logging axe, however.

NightmareCrucible.Key.Helplessness.src:
The dragonkin Avisk was obsessed with dreams. He believed they were the key to unlocking the true power of the mind. Nightmares, especially, fascinated him. In the folds of a dream he placed powerful creatures in the hope that the dream would infect them, somehow, making them easier for him to possess.

He forged each of the crucibles after an archetype of nightmares, strengthening them with the power of the collective unconscious from a variety of species. A rare dragonkin that considered the minds of others races, not just his own.

A common nightmare is that feeling of helplessness. That no matter what you do, no matter how hard you try, you are destined to failure. A nightmare so powerful that it seeps into the waking world, inflicting people with imposter syndromes, paranoia and jealousy.

This key is that feeling crystallised and used to shape the Nightmare Crucible. Alas the creatures within are not quite as helpless as Avisk hoped.

Lifeward.src:
The dragonkin discovered a unique and powerful resource in their time on Ashenfall, the blood of a goddess – Lougrim. She was a moon deity, in-tune with the natural world, the forests and a source of great vitality. Her blood carries some of those properties. 

If imbibed, even small amounts of the blood, centuries old, can enhance one’s vital spark, making you hardier and healthier. You can take more damage, survive greater threats, overcome the most dangerous challenges. 

The blood was kept in a number of urns, which were separated and hidden across Ashenfall, in the hope that the resource wouldn’t easily be destroyed. It was to be a linchpin in their great endeavours, until Kuldra laid those lofty dreams to rest. Once they were buried, deep within the earth, but time, and other, more mysterious sources, have brought them to the surface just in time for your arrival. 

Anyone, and by that, I mean you, dear reader, can use the power of these urns for yourself. Explore Ashenfall and seek out these hidden locations; take the power of a goddess for your own. 

Whilst the blood may be weaker than before, it will still make you healthier, increasing your ability to stand against the great treats of Ashenfall.

DragonkinDarkMageRobes.src:
The dragonkin of Ashenfall revelled in power, gaining elemental mastery from the land's strange anima. Although their kind tended to ignore magic in favour of alchemy and science, the dragonkin of Ashenfall enjoyed a time as sorcerer kings.

They wore robes that empowered their magic, using alchemical techniques to create cloth that resisted their elemental powers. Fire would not burn so easily. Cold would not damage the threads. Lightning could be turned aside with a flick of a cloak. Though these techniques are lost to time, the echoes of their powerful resistance remain.

Although dragonkin tend to favour form over fashion, they stitched these robes with undeniable regal zeal. They were more elaborate than necessary, more stylish than required, feeding into the ego of the wearer.

Rasthin, it is said, was particularly fond of stitching elaborate filigree into her robes. Made from threads woven with precious metals and gemstones, her robes would sparkle and glitter as she flew across the realm. When she brought forward her flames, everyone marvelled.

Glittering against the sky, she inspired as much devotion as fear in her subjects.

DragonkinDarkMageLegs.src:
The dragonkin of Ashenfall revelled in power, gaining elemental mastery from the land's strange anima. Although their kind tended to ignore magic in favour of alchemy and science, the dragonkin of Ashenfall enjoyed a time as sorcerer kings.

They wore robes that empowered their magic, using alchemical techniques to create cloth that resisted their elemental powers. Fire would not burn so easily. Cold would not damage the threads. Lightning could be turned aside with a flick of a cloak. Though these techniques are lost to time, the echoes of their powerful resistance remain.

Lacrussa was the only dragonkin to resist the allure of magic. She insisted that science was the greater power. That with time and study, it capable of almost anything. Lacrussa wore the robes as a small act of rebellion, claiming that magic would always be overcome in the end.

Unlike her companions, Lacrussa refused to decorate her robes. She took no joy in precious stones or shiny metals. She refused to embroider designs across the cloak. She did, however, use alchemical techniques to enhance her robes' defensive power. Something the other dragonkin soon came to copy, proving, in her mind, the superiority of science.

DragonkinDarkMageHood.src:
The dragonkin of Ashenfall revelled in power, gaining elemental mastery from the land's strange anima. Although their kind tended to ignore magic in favour of alchemy and science, the dragonkin of Ashenfall enjoyed a time as sorcerer kings.

They wore robes that empowered their magic, using alchemical techniques to create cloth that resisted their elemental powers. Fire would not burn so easily. Cold would not damage the threads. Lightning could be turned aside with a flick of a cloak. Though these techniques are lost to time, the echoes of their powerful resistance remain.

The hood was designed for two purposes. The shadow it cast upon the features of the dragonkin made their visage scarier and more intimidating. Goblins, humans and garou would cower before the reptilian grin, which was all they could see in the shadow. The second was to hide their frustration at the foolishness of others, including their fellow dragonkin. It is much easier to roll one's eyes when no one can see it.

NightmareCrucibles.src:
The dragonkin, Avisk, was obsessed with the power of the mind and he crafted various experiments to help hone and strengthen his own. As well as expanding his strength of conscious will, he knew that he needed to empower his subconscious as well.

Using techniques stolen from other dragonkin creeds, he created small contained realities made from fragments of dreams he captured across the world. Dreams, like thoughts, run wild and free, but unlike thoughts dreams can escape their boundaries and flee to other hosts, other vessels, like psychic parasites.

A man can dream of success, but it be his son that continues his legacy. Another can dream of power, yet it isn’t until decades later that someone awakens the slumbering dream and perfects it, becoming king, emperor or worse. Avisk caught many of these dreams, sifted through them and claimed the worst of the worst and used them to craft these realities.

The crucibles would be places where  creatures could be honed, tested and improved. Through trial and torment, they would emerge stronger and more powerful, making them ideal subjects for the experiments that would come.

Perhaps it is a mercy that Kuldra put a stop to his schemes, for what fresh nightmares could he have birthed, should his work have continued?

InternalAlchemy.src:
The druid Gastritix often struggled with Bramblemead dishes. Something about the rustic cooking troubled her stomach and she would find herself in constant distress. Even bread, simple as it was, would leave her doubled over in agony and there were many times where she regretted that day's meal. So it was that she created a spell, which would speed up her digestion to near instant speed, granting her the energy needed to survive, but somehow preventing her normal stomach issues. 

Thereafter, with this spell in her repertoire, she became a noted local chef, finally able to enjoy a good meal.

InspiringRingOfMining.ProspectorsRing.src:
The dwarves know that the earth has a memory, gemstones especially so. What they don’t tell you, is that the earth holds a grudge. Each time a pick pierces the stone or smashes a piece of ore from its home, the earth remembers.

A skilled enchanter can use that grudge, that earthen memory, and turn it back against the grudge-filled earth. Traditionally this is done via jewellery, with dwarven goldsmiths making most of their living from miners purchasing these trinkets.

ImarusTalon.src:
The essence of an undead dragon, distilled down into a blade. What could go wrong?

This weapon is cold to the touch in ways far beyond chilling. Holding it feels as if you’re out in the cold, with no shelter to protect you. Exposure in the palm of your hand.

Worse than the cold, is the hunger. This scimitar wants to cut, to stab, to slice and to maim. It wants to see your enemies bleed so that it can feast on their suffering. Imaru may be dead, but her hunger is eternal and you feel it infecting you with each swing of the blade.

Still, the power of this blade makes it almost worth it. What’s a little hunger when faced with the destruction of your foes? Lament later, surely, and revel now in the carnage. Perhaps there’s a little dragon in you too?

BonesToPeaches.src:
The essence of magic is change, this the druids believed. Elemental magics were assumed to balance one element with another. Mending spells transformed the present into past. When one druid found himself trapped in a wolf's den, he was forced to rely on this concept.

The wolf had him cornered, trapped behind a crack in the wall, too small for the wolf to attack him, but leaving him no room for escape. Around the druid, were the bones of the wolf's victims, which had been hurled through the crack like some burial ritual. Starving and thirsty, the druid worked out a spell, using the runes in his pocket to turn the bones into the sweet, sticky fruit that would keep him alive. Fed, on this strange discovery, the druid outlasted the wolf's hunger for his flesh and when the wolf went to seek his own food, the druid took his chance to escape. 

Eating the transmuted bones of others is considered a little odd in civilised society, yet when one is in the wilderness, one takes what they can get.

AdventurersLongbow.src:
The expedition to Ashenfall included skilled adventurers. If fate had been kinder, they could have gone down in legend as mighty heroes, rather than in slow, quiet, death, where their names might be forgotten.

This bow was a design brought to Ashenfall by the hunter, Finn: a simple longbow crafted from easily obtained materials. Finn was a scout and a ranger who enjoyed exploring all the nooks and crannies of White Wolf mountain, in search of treasure. He joined the expedition in the hope of discovering new wonders and new stories to share with his people back home.

Instead, he found a dragon and the end to his story.

AdamantMace.src:
The first adamant mace was not, as you might expect, used for battle. Rather it was a rolling pin used by the ancient matriarch known only as The Crone – a name she chose for herself, thinking it quite funny.

Her baking skills were so dire, that whatever she produced had the consistency of iron and was more durable than steel. So, she required a tool strong enough to fight back against her sturdy pastries. She commissioned a rolling pin of adamant metal, and she used it with great zeal to beat her baked goods into submission.

Though teeth would still shatter against her scones, there was an artistry there that none could deny. So it was that more people would create adamant rolling pins, until an angry chef beat her rude husband to death with it, and the first true adamant mace was born.

After that, Moon Garou would still favour an adamant rolling pin, but many a warrior would bring a mace into battle, just in case they were forced to face up against the crone’s pastries. Which happened more often than is reasonably explainable.

CompostBucket.src:
The first bucket on Gielinor was created by Ms Hyacinth, to help her around the farm. They had buckets back in the human homeworld of Teragard, of course, but she hadn’t brought anything with her from the village Guthix had recruited her from.

The problem was that Ms Hyacinth had a cow, named the traditional Bessie, that produced an unreasonable amount of manure, and Ms Hyacinth needed something to help with the clean-up.

She used local twigs at first, weaving together more of a basket than a bucket, and the results were not as watertight as she had hoped. In the end, she meticulously combined strips of wood, tied together with cord, and they were able to withstand even the worst of Bessie’s endeavours.

Now, you too can fill one of these marvellous contraptions with horrifically pungent compost. Spread the smelly stuff across your farming plots and marvel at the health and happiness of your leafy little friends.

EnchantCampfire.src:
The first campfires changed the path of human destiny. Shivering cave dwellers lasted longer against the winter, and in time they learned to use this flame to dominate the land. Ever since, campfires have warmed a primal part of our spirit, and many yearn for the simple pleasure of sitting around one with their companions, on a summer night. So it comes as no surprise that the first druids found a way to make such fires even more appealing. 

The runes drew out some essential nature of the campfire, letting it burn hotter, brighter and better than before. Food cooks faster, cold quickly burns away and even the campfire ghost stories feel better against a backdrop of this flame.

IronArrowBrutal.src:
The first of these weapons was not commissioned for war. Nor was it commissioned for hunting. Instead, this most deadly arrow was created for nothing more than vengeance.

Against a pigeon.

Lord Gawurin was the ruler of Brynmoor, as appointed by the priests of Saradomin. He wore expensive garments of the finest materials, adorned with glittering jewels and gold chain. So, he was most affronted when a single pigeon determined that such a garment was the perfect restroom choice.

The pigeon's audacity was unforgivable. Day after day, Lord Gawurin's garments were defiled by this feathered fiend. His anger grew, fueling a desire for revenge that consumed him. He commissioned an arrow, a weapon of brutal design, with a single purpose- to make the pigeon suffer.

With a sinister smile, he summoned the most skilled hunter, a woman who had brought down countless foes, and ordered her to end the pigeon's reign of terror.

She stood at the top of the castle, her bow steady, her aim true. The tension in the air was palpable as she prepared to unleash the arrow of vengeance upon the pigeon. The world seemed to hold its breath in anticipation.

She missed.

BarbedIronArrow.src:
The first of these weapons was not commissioned for war. Nor was it commissioned for hunting. Instead, this most deadly arrow was created for nothing more than vengeance.

Against a pigeon.

Lord Gawurin was the ruler of Brynmoor, as appointed by the priests of Saradomin. He wore expensive garments of the finest materials, adorned with glittering jewels and gold chain. So, he was most affronted when a single pigeon determined that such a garment was the perfect restroom choice.

The pigeon's audacity was unforgivable. Day after day, Lord Gawurin's garments were defiled by this feathered fiend. His anger grew, fuelling a desire for revenge that consumed him. He commissioned an arrow, a weapon of brutal design, with a single purpose- to make the pigeon suffer.

With a sinister smile, he summoned the most skilled hunter, a woman who had brought down countless foes, and ordered her to end the pigeon's reign of terror.

She stood at the top of the castle, her bow steady, her aim true. The tension in the air was palpable as she prepared to unleash the arrow of vengeance upon the pigeon. The world seemed to hold its breath in anticipation.

She missed.

RuneMedHelm.src:
The first suit of rune armour was worn by the god Guthix, after many months of failed blacksmithing attempts. For all his might, skill and wisdom, Guthix, it seemed, was remarkably poor at anything practical and that delighted him in ways he couldn't share. For Guthix had never really wanted to be a god. Though he took his responsibilities seriously, he had ascended in an act of vengeance, not by deliberate intent. In his transcendence, he had lost much of what made him happier in his mortal life. Failures, it seems, could spark as much joy as success, for one learns and grows from the experience and such growth defines who we are. 

The rune medium helm is one of the first pieces he crafted. You can tell because it looks like a brick with delusions of grandeur.

WoolThread.src:
The fluffy coats from the fluffiest creatures, refined and wound down into a single thread. Useful for crafting various garments and highly prized by grandmothers everywhere.

On the mainland, the most impressive collection of wool belongs to Great-Aunt Potterington, in Kandarin. Her sister, Granny Potterington, is constantly trying to claim this title for herself and has accelerated her sheep breeding program in an attempt to mass produce as much wool as possible.

StaminaPotion.src:
The frustrating thing about agility courses is that you can't keep doing them forever. Agility's final boss is lactic acid, and it likes to stick spears into your muscles and joints.

Well, the humble stamina potion is +1 against lactic acid. If you're planning on physical activity and want to flick the bird to exhaustion, then we would recommend making one or two.

MagicLongbow.src:
The garou spoke in hushed tones about a hunter in the eastern reaches of the Fractured Plains. They knew well enough not to approach her: she would keep to hunting game, unless the garou posed a threat. If a young garou was unwise enough to rush her, she would punch an arrow through their throat. 

The hunter wouldn't hide herself particularly. While she was hooded, her weapon of choice was a magic longbow, and it would surge with energy like a lightning bolt in the Highlands. The hunter knew that she could not be touched; that the garou could watch her all they wanted.

All the garou could do was share stories about her. Trackers said that she moved without leaving a trail - something that meant she was neither human or goblin. Others claimed that they heard soft music in her territory and promptly forgot why they were there. One garou even claimed to see a shadow of the hunter - a version completely in black.

SpookyBait.src: The ghostly remnants of ectoplasm can be strangely appealing to certain fish. Perhaps it is the siren call of the rivers of the underworld, calling all life to its ultimate destination. Perhaps it’s some sort of ancestral grief urging the fish to reconnect with those they have lost. Perhaps it’s simply that they find the thing pretty. Who can really say?

GlassVessel.src:
The glass vessel. The emblem of potential. It could find itself filled with anything. Water, demonic oil, maple syrup. It could smash before it ever sees use. It could languish in someone's inventory, forgotten for months. In many ways, we are all glass vessels. 

Check back in your journal for other delightful moments of poignancy and philosophy. You may find your life inalterably changed by the wisdom there.

Zamorak.src:
The god of chaos, Zamorak, is often associated with evil. In truth, it is more complicated than this, as Zamorak promotes freedom and self-improvement, rather than relying on tradition. Needless to say, he and Saradomin have been in conflict across the ages.

Zamorak is one of the Mahjarrat, the mysterious creatures from the world of Freneskae. He was recruited to serve under the Empty Lord, Zaros, but he found Zaros’ methods too hands-off for his tastes. Using two of the Elder Artefacts, Zamorak betrayed Zaros and drained him of enough of his power to allow Zamorak to ascend. Zaros, presumed defeated, disappeared into the void where he might rebuild his strength.

News of his usurpation of Zaros is what began the God Wars, the greatest and bloodiest battle in Gielinor’s history. An alliance of Saradomin, Bandos and Armadyl, pushed Zamorak to the brink and caused him to destroy the entire region of Forinthry in a last desperate ploy. This act awoke Guthix from his slumber, and caused him to enact the Edicts that would banish the gods.

Zamorak has tried repeatedly to reclaim Gielinor, using the legions of demons at his beck and call. He has been pushed back by alliances of heroes, yet is always scheming to return and finish what he started.

CheekyFryUp.src:
The grease. The sizzling scents. The feeling of your arteries withering just from a single glance at the dish. Is there anything in life as close to the divine as a nice, cheeky fry up?

Popular among those who have consumed a few too many gnomish cocktails the night before, a cheeky fry up is hailed as a great cure for the pounding headache that follows such indulgences.

GraniteMaulHandle.src: The handle for a powerful weapon. Wrapped in sturdy leather and imbued with ritual magic. A dwarf capable of crafting such a piece is acknowledged to have completed one of the trials required to be a master smith.

WitheredHeart.src:
The heart is a pump, nothing more, designed to push precious blood around the circulatory system, so that our weak and feeble frames can function. Yet, metaphysically, it is the most important organ, for it houses our emotional centre, the very essence of what makes us human.

A withered heart isn’t just a heart that has languished. Nor is it just a heart that is drained of blood. No, a withered heart has had all the humanity leeched from it, emptied of emotion, or connection, of self.

This process is imperfect, of course, and tiny fragments of soul-matter remains, that can be refined and extracted from the heart. Withdrawing the last remnants of what made the owner “them”.

BramblemeadCape.src:
The heart of Bramblemead village was never really the castle, which came much later to the party. It wasn’t the town hall. It wasn’t the druid huts. It was the windmill. Grain heaped by the village was brought here and milled down into flour. The flour became bread, pastry and batter, turning village meals into something that helped people to live, rather than simply survive.

Food, becomes a banner around which everyone can gather. To break bread with one’s enemy was a way to settle old scores, and forge new connections. More good has been done over the dinner table, than on any throne. Flour, turned Bramblemead from a settlement, into a thriving village.

Now, the windmill lies dormant and still. The foundations warped by the centuries, despite the magic holding the rot at bay in the ancient timber, and the stone cracking from time. When humanity fell, it was rats and goblins that claimed the heart of the village, though they had no use for the swirling sails.

To the goblins it was a place where food could be hidden. Supplies sealed up from rival tribes. For the rats, it was a restaurant full of goblin supplies that were never well sealed.

The sail no longer turns. But, perhaps, in the fullness of time, this village heart might beat again.

DriedCadavaberries.src: The heat makes them edible, but only just. A once popular snack among the people of Fellhollow, who seemed overly cavalier about the consumption of deadly poisons.

FallenHopliteApsis.src:
The hoplites of Emberwood named themselves after Saradomin’s forces in the holy scripture. The legendary hoplites were warriors on the world of Hallow, who were trained from farmers and artisans, rather than military families or nobility, and the Emberwood hoplites came from similar stock.

They were best known for their fighting style using spears and shields, with the shield being the defining feature. These shields were designed to be worn for longer periods of time, resting against the shoulder for more comfortable carrying.

The hoplites may have been raised from peasant stock, but their camaraderie made them a force to be reckoned with on the battlefield.

As the withering took them, the hoplites retained the rote memory of their training and remained a deadly threat to all who faced them.

YewLongbow.src:
The hunter is the lifeblood of the Moon Garou. The Umbral Sands are not as hospitable to agriculture as many would like, so diets must be supplemented with fresh meat. This is particularly true for the Moon Garou, who remain primarily carnivorous in nature.

One hunter, Flytr, was the first to craft a longbow from the yew trees in the oases. Legend had it that the trees were sacred, special, a gift of the River Mother, designed to keep the Moon Garou safe. It was the greatest of blasphemies to use the wood for anything, but Flytr had never been particularly concerned with matters of faith.

She found a tree that had been struck by lightning, to lessen the guilt of repurposing the wood. She whittled down branch and bough, to create the longbow and, when she was done, she could have sworn the weapon was excited to be used.

It felled foes at great range, making her one of the best hunters the tribe had ever seen. Soon after, yew trees were no longer protected, as it came to be believed that the strength of the bow was proof that the River Mother wanted the wood to be used.

Heartwraith.Hookworm.src: The insides of Kuldra are filled with more than just flesh. She has gorged herself on anima and her blood contains the last remnants of a fallen goddess. Kuldra herself is close to divinity, held back by dragonkin safeguards that prevent her from achieving her full potential. Yet, that power must flow somewhere and within her flesh crawl the vile heartworms: warped parasites empowered by this excess of magic. These strange creatures are filled with Kuldra’s rage and hatred, and will happily obliterate anything they encounter that isn’t the queen’s anima-infused flesh.

IronGreatsword.src:
The iron greatsword is a devastating weapon favoured by the most powerful warriors. The strongest garou warriors wielded them in battle against goblin invaders, turning armies of green-skinned soldiers into nothing but viscera.

When the dragons turned on their allies, these blades would be turned against armoured scales. Several dragons underestimated the power of these weapons in the hands of a skilled wielder. Garou thanes tore young dragons to pieces, wearing their bones as symbols of their success.

It made them an excellent target for the older dragons. Velgar, a mighty general, marked those wearing dragon bone adornments for death. He crushed them first, brutally and swiftly. Their strength shattered beneath his claws or swallowed in an instant.

The practice quickly fell out of favour.

RedberryInfusion.src: The juice of the berries infuses the water with a pleasant flavour. It’s easier and more refreshing to drink, offering greater hydrating properties than normal water.

DesertDevil.src:
The kebbit of the sands have a strange name, one that implies a connection to the fiery realm of Infernus. This is, weirdly, not actually that far from the truth, because the desert devil is not native to the Umbral Sands, but rather the result of poor security at Dowdun Reach.

Originally, they were brought to the Reach as a rapidly reproducing source of meat. Sadly, the once peaceful and vegetarian chinchompas of the region discovered that their meat was delicious and consumed them voraciously, becoming the carnivorous chinchompas the region is currently overrun with.

A few of the kebbits escaped to the desert, where they survived by feeding on cacti and small insects that lived within the sands. Now, while their meat is no longer as delicious, they’ve adapted to survive in the desert and can be found running round the sands without a care in the world.

ZamorakMagePack.src: The knapsack of a mage in Dowdun Reach. It contains all the materials that the mage would have needed for a day's work. Now they are yours.

PaladinBody.src:
The knights of Saradomin had many names over the years. White Knights. Temple Knights. In Ashenfall, they were called Paladins. Brave and faithful, members of noble families who took up the sword.

They were the second, third and fourth children of Brynmoor’s “nobility” – a title given to those families that were most loyal to the priesthood, and the most obedient were raised the highest.

This chest piece was especially well made. Blacksmiths would take extra special care to make sure that the process went smoothly, as nothing but perfection would withstand inspection. It made forgery practically impossible, or at the very least, far too expensive to be feasible.

It is said that the paladins were capable of working miracles in battle. Rumour held that the power of Saradomin flowed through them, and helped them to smite all who stood against the church.

PaladinLegs.src:
The knights of Saradomin had many names over the years. White Knights. Temple Knights. In Ashenfall, they were called Paladins. Brave and faithful, members of noble families who took up the sword.

They were the second, third and fourth children of Brynmoor’s “nobility” – a title given to those families that were most loyal to the priesthood, and the most obedient were raised the highest.

These platelegs were exceptionally well made. Sturdier and stronger than the armour worn by Brynmoor guards and other Ashenfall human soldiers. It was certainly stronger than the helms of the Guthixian-aligned knights or the druids they guarded.

Paladins were a righteous force, noble and true to the priests' teachings. They brought order from chaos and discipline to indolence, remaking Bramblemead according to the church’s designs.

PaladinHelm.src:
The knights of Saradomin had many names over the years. White Knights. Temple Knights. In Ashenfall, they were called Paladins. Brave and faithful, members of noble families who took up the sword.

They were the second, third and fourth children of Brynmoor’s “nobility” – a title given to those families that were most loyal to the priesthood, and the most obedient were raised the highest.

This helm was a symbol of pride among the respectable families of Brynmoor. A sign for all of Brynmoor to see that the bearer had been chosen to stand as guardian of the Saradominist faith. It earned the wearer favour. It earned status. It earned the ire of those who followed a different faith.

UndeadRangerHood.src:
The last hunter in Fellhollow hid in the trees for as long as he could. Beneath him the dead shambled and stumbled and clawed at the bark, yet he remained in the trees safely out of reach.

He fed himself on nuts and berries, stealing form the treasure troves of squirrels and birds, occasionally risking a trip to the ground to hunt a passing animal. He gave up on cooking the meat he hunted, as he could not stay on the ground long enough before the dead rose up to face him, so he tore into the carcasses of deer, sheep and rats, trying his best not to vomit.

He barely noticed when his appetite changed, since he was so used raw flesh and the sickly cold taste of blood pooling in his mouth. So, when the withering began to take him, he hardly noticed.

Sometimes, if you’re quick enough, you may catch a glimpse of a skeleton in the tree branches. Even in death he fears the monsters on the ground.

LawRune.src: The law rune is an odd sort of power, it embodies not some elemental force, but instead it represents the rigidity of reality. The rules in which all of creation operates, are conceptually encapsulated within this small stone. Gravity, movement, location, all these things are bound within, and when the rune is used in magic, these rules may be altered for a time. Teleportation relies heavily on these runes, overwriting the concept of distance for the casting.

DiscordantResidue.src:
The life of a creature within Kuldra's Tower is not a pleasant one. Every beast or warrior (even the undead ones) are at constant threat from any of Kuldra's five heads, and the tower itself is a font of anima. Any kind of life expectancy is a luxury.

Evolution has handed the creatures of Kuldra's Tower something of a lifeline. Anima attaches itself to the creatures in a kind of symbiosis. The anima seeps into the creature, feeding on its softer tissue and leaving something like a crystal residue behind. This discordant symbiosis makes the creature hardier, at the cost of a humming, constant pain.

Salmon.src: The life of a salmon is one of great journey and strife. They swim back over great distances, leaping upstream to cement their legacy. It is tragic then, perhaps, that such journeys become the happy lunchtimes of bears and other animals.

WeakCoolingPotion.src: The liquid in this potion is always cold to the touch. It tastes like an iced glass of lemonade on a hot summer's day, or a chilled glass of water when you've been working out in the sun. Drinking this potion makes the body cooler than before, shielding one against fire's fury.

OakLongbow.src:
The longbow is every hunter’s friend. Capable of taking down prey over a greater range than the shortbow, it has been the end of many a deer trying to flee through the woods. 

Bramblemead would host a thrilling archery tournament. The villagers would proudly bring their own longbows, meticulously crafted by hand, and compete to take down cleverly hidden targets scattered across the village. It was a spectacle of skill and precision, with the only rule being that the target must be shootable from the open street. 

With the introduction of magic, the competition took on a whole new level of silliness. Participants conjured magical air currents that sent arrows astray – often into unsuspecting washing lines or pies cooling on windowsills – or they would playfully blast arrows out of the air with fire spells. 

However, this stopped after the Amalgamated archer, Derien, joined the game. Gifted with the element of air, his arrows curved gracefully with each shot, missing traps, tricks and deceptions. His victory earned the Amalgamated more jealousy, which led to the competition ending out of envious spite.

AnimaInfusedBark.src: The magic of Ashenfall permeates the very trees of the region, imbuing their bark with mystical properties. This bark can be refined into wild anima, a magical crafting component that is popular with spellcasters of all kinds.

SmallAshes.src: The magnificent bounty of a demonic kill. Want to know what an infernal creature carries around with them in their everyday life? Look no further!

BronzeCrowssbow.src:
The members of the Wild Knights who trained with melee weapons, generally found themselves the victors in friendly sparring matches against their companions. The reasoning was simple – shields. A shield could turn aside blade, arrow and spell, with equal skill and it left their enemy vulnerable to counterattack. This sense of superiority began to change from friendly competition, into a sense of smugness capable of souring many friendships.

Roliker Hallister was particularly obnoxious. His skill with sword and shield was admittedly impressive. At the age of twenty he could best even some of the commanders of the Wild Knights in single combat. Healthy pride twisted into smug egoism, which then rotted down into unpleasant superiority. He was rude. He was dismissive. He was pretty much an obnoxious nightmare to be around.

Which is why he was very surprised by the bolt in his shoulder, and why no one else seemed too inclined to help him out. Vanida Mox was a skilled archer and inventor. She was quick to learn, quick to study and she had the enviable ability to see when something was wrong and work to find a solution. Popular with the other knights, because she would work with them, share accolades, and stand for what the order truly meant – a barrier between the world and the wild.

As Roliker’s ego grew and grew, she realised that the archers in the order were at a significant disadvantage in close combat. At range, they were obviously superior, but as all the sparring matches were held in the courtyard, there was precious little distance available. So she began working on a device that would deliver the power of an arrow but allowing one hand free to hold a shield.

It was very effective.

She named it a “cross-bow”, because she was very very angry when she unloaded it into the cloud of smugness known as Roliker. Later that name would be attributes to the mechanical structure of the device, but now you know better.

NightmareCrucible.Key.Betrayal.src:
The mind is a powerful thing. Thought can shape reality; intention turns to impulse, which moves muscle and bone, which in turn can shatter stone. The Aughra were fascinated by such power and sought more and more ways to harness it.

For Avisk, who was determined to force his will on all living beings, it was a myriad collection of tools in one, squishy, vessel. Dreams and nightmares were an especially fascinating study. Dreams, like thoughts, can shape reality. A child dreams of the stars and goes in search of the tallest trees, the highest mountains, anything to help him get closer to those twinkling baubles.

The elderly dream of their youth and regret decisions made decades in the past. Entire lifespans can exist in moments. Avisk yearned to harness that power.

When he crafted the crucibles, he distilled nightmares down to their purest forms. Each one forged from archetypes shared across countless species. Yet what nightmare is stronger then when friends become foes, when trust turns to betrayal. When we look into the eyes of our loved ones, what if it’s hatred that shines back?

This key is the concept of betrayal crystallised down and used to unlock the Nightmare Crucible. The beasts inside offer no loyalty, for in a world forged by betrayal they know that trust is nothing but a pleasant fiction.

MithrilWarhammer.src:
The mithril warhammer was once the weapon most associated with Lord Rasmodel of Dowdun Reach. He was rarely seen without it. In the mornings, when he was in most pain, it would be a prop, something to lean on while the night's watch recounted the events of the early hours. In the afternoons, it was a beautiful warning, a threat of what might happen if you disobeyed him.

Lord Rasmodel wasn't one for naming his weapons. He found the custom a little juvenile. But when his thoughts were elsewhere, you might see him pat the head of his warhammer. There was kinship there, even if he wouldn't admit it.

Jade.src:
The more green the colour of jade, the higher the concentration of iron in its makeup. Popular among many cultures for both its beauty and it’s use as a crafting material.

In the eastern lands of Wushanko, jade is highly prized. Some islands have elaborate rituals about its usage. There are rumours of rare jades with magical properties, each a different colour of the rainbow.

FortifyingCrunchies.src: The mushrooms of Ashenfall have absorbed enough magic over the years to give them special properties. A well-cooked mushroom will absorb certain toxins from whoever ingests them, making them invaluable for scouting into poison-filled areas.

VannakaDefault.src:
The mysterious warrior, Vannaka, is regarded as one of the premier slayer masters in the world. He trained under the legendary Duradel, and the two even duelled one another once. Duradel won. Something Vannaka has never entirely managed to get over. 

Vannaka’s origins are mysterious. He claims no nation as his homeland, nor does he speak of family or friends. Conversations lead only to talk of combat and the slaying of dangerous creatures. Yet there is something about Ashenfall that creates a silence in him. He stares out across the continent as if searching for something.

SalveAmulet.src:
The name is a bit of a misnomer, since this amulet has very little to do with the river Salve. Instead its name refers to the crystal that traditionally sits at the heart. This crystal was first brought to the region by Saradominist priests, some time in the third age. They had harvested it from a cave near the river Salve and found ways to cultivate on Ashenfall’s soil, by utilising the natural magic infusing everything.

Sanctified by faith and magic, this amulet was deadly to the undead, and the dragonkin Lacrussa was fascinated with the properties. She stole the recipe for its creation and hid it within her vault, long before the withering curse spread over Fellhollow. Instead she had delved too deeply in her own experiments and discovered something buried within the earth that would twist and reanimate the dead.

This amulet allowed her to hold the forces back and keep them from overrunning her lab. That was, until, she met her end at Kuldra’s fangs.

MysticFibre.src:
The origin of mystic fibres, thread and cloth are wreathed in mystery. There's little to no mention in any written histories, which – on its own – seems unlikely. It is not a subtle material. There should be log after log of merchants trading it, or actively avoiding trading it. 

This leads me to believe that the mystic material is an elaborate troll. It's a plant – and I don't mean that in the floral definition. I think someone has introduced it as a joke, and I have a list of potential culprits. Brassica Prime: you are number one on that list.

PipeCactusSeed.src:
The pipe cactus is like an iceberg, if you replace the ice with cactus and the sea with sand. A pipe cactus runs deep, deep into the sands, its roots grasping for any moisture it can find. That moisture often can be found at the bottom of quicksand, or on the bedrock, many metres below the surface. A pipe cactus is one of the few that can 'pipe' that moisture up. 

Many a moon garou has tried to suck that moisture up through the 'pipe' of the cactus, like a natural well. The pipe cactus has evolved counter-measures to that particular ploy, including valve-like structures up its stem, and, you know, spikes.

Vulture.src:
The poor vulture gets a bad rap. We see them as omens of death; scavengers circling around us, waiting for us to die. This image is fair, but ask yourself why they do this and what good it brings the world.

Would you rather the desert was filled with the rotting corpses of those who have succumbed to the Scorch? Or, is it not better to find picked-clean skeletons, in which disease and corruption cannot thrive?

Countless lives may be saved by a vulture’s feeding habits, but you never think about that, do you?

SteelMace.src:
The priests of Emberwood village were not as militant as their fellows back in Brynmoor. They saw little need for weapons, when a dragon watched over their flock. Still, they carried steel maces by their side as a symbol of office, each one ornately engraved with the symbol of their chosen deity.

Although the Saradominist priests had first insisted that different faiths could only turn on one another, they found an odd sort of kinship in their fellows and would regularly enjoy debates of the merits and flaws of each other’s faiths.

KalphiteGuardian.src:
The queen is all that matters. Protect the queen at all costs.

Those are the only thoughts within the guardian - the only drive, the only reason for living. All their energies, every cell in their bodies, fixated on that singular command.

Perhaps this is why they fight with such fervour. When your entire existence is reduced to a single focus, a single command, everything must get a little frustrating. The kalphite do not aspire, they do not dream. They have their place in the hive and they accept it completely.

Avisk was fascinated by this. As one of the Aughra, he was always obsessed with the mind and the potential within it. Whereas the other Aughra sought to escape the curse by transferring their consciousness to a single new body, Avisk dreamed of becoming the swarm. The kalphite fascinated him. He saw them as a single entity comprised of multiple individual moving parts and the potential of that structure became his new obsession.

When he stole some of the royal eggs from the Kharidian Desert’s hive, he was forced to battle several guardians who were protecting the nest. While they were no match for the power of a dragonkin, they nonetheless earned what passes for Avisk’s respect and he made sure to encourage his new queen to create as many guardians as possible so he could study them further.

Raven.src: The raven wakes early and perches on the battlements of Dowdun Reach. There it can watch for adventurers. It longs for them to suffer a grisly end, not because a raven feels malice, but because a grisly corpse is easier to feast on. The food has been taken out of its wrapper.

AbyssalAshes.src: The remnants of an abyssal demon. Fine ashes, infused with malice. Not great for the skin, despite what Doric will tell you.

Fellhollow.SilverthornKeep.src:
The ruined bastion of the Wild Knights, after they abandoned Bramblemead in search of greener pastures. For a while it was a powerful stronghold, with a growing legion of knights that would seek out the imbalances across Ashenfall and lay them all to rest.

When the dead began to rise and the Withering took hold, the keep closed its doors and focused entirely on defence. It was, ultimately, a losing battle. The problem with fighting the dead is that each of your force that falls becomes a new soldier in theirs. Defeat was the only outcome possible, but the knights held on as long as they could.

RuneFireArrows.src:
The rune fire arrow is central to a story about the knight commander, Sir Leigh. In his will, Sir Leigh requested a full-boat burning. He wanted to be pushed out to sea, towards the mainland where he was born, and an archer was to set the pyre alight with a rune fire arrow. Sat at his desk, writing the will, it would have sounded like a fantastic idea to Sir Leigh. But in reality it was very different.

Rune, you see, has repulsive properties. It is diamagnetic. So when Sir Leigh was laid to rest in his gold armour atop a raft, and the archer tried to aim for the pyre-wood beneath him, the rune arrows would not hit. Dozens upon dozens of arrows were fired, and they all deviated from their path thanks to the runic properties. By the time a boat was sent out with a man holding a lit torch, two seagulls and one shark had been set alight.

BlackDragonhideLegs.src:
The scales of a black dragon are sturdy things, capable of deflecting all but the strongest attacks. It’s not so much that they’re harder than other scales, but that the creature that bore them is so determined to survive that that tenacity passes on to one who wears it.

Scathach wore armour forged from the scales of her victims, and necklaces of their teeth dangled around her neck. She walked bravely among the dragons, because she knew that none would dare challenge her as she wore the skin of their kin.

Her confidence won the attention of Kuldra. Impressed with the garou’s skill, strength and sheer audacity, Kuldra granted her a drop of her blood, elevating Scathach above both her kin and the dragons she challenged.

It was this blood that would cause Scathach’s betrayal, because the remnants of the moon goddess, Lougrim, whispered within Kuldra’s blood and urged Scathach to turn on her mistress.

Sadly, her betrayal was short-lived, and stands as a warning to all other garou not to attempt the same foolish plan.

BlackDragonhideCoif.src:
The scales of a black dragon are sturdy things, capable of deflecting all but the strongest attacks. It’s not so much that they’re harder than other scales, but that the creature that bore them is so determined to survive that that tenacity passes on to one who wears it.

There are no stories about people making bonds of friendship with the black dragons of Ashenfall, because the dragons do not allow anyone to think of them as their equals. They are the masters, the superior species and the garou and goblins of the Scorned Wilderness have long been taught to know their place.

There are certainly plenty who would challenge them, true, but over the centuries the list of successful challengers has yet to pass into double digits.

BlackDragonhideBody.src:
The scales of a black dragon are sturdy things, capable of deflecting all but the strongest attacks. It’s not so much that they’re harder than other scales, but that the creature that bore them is so determined to survive that that tenacity passes on to one who wears it.

There were a few garou hunters that were skilled enough to challenge a black dragon, but only one was ever strong enough to skin an entire one and wear its scales as armour. Her name was Scathach, and she was the very model of garou savagery.

She wielded a great spear and, where other garou would sneak, she would leap, proudly, into battle against the dragons, to prove that the garou were just as deadly as the dragons, if not more so.

When her spear pierced the heart of a mighty dragon, she would let out a howl that would terrify even the bravest of souls.

MithrilScimitar.src:
The scimitar form is not commonplace on Ashenfall. Unlike the mainland (where you can't walk five metres in the Kharidian Desert without getting slashed by one), the scimitar is a rarity. Only an offshoot of the garou, found in some of the harshest deserts of Ashenfall, are known to wield it. 

That is likely to change, of course, as more adventurers make landfall. It makes you wonder what the island will look like in five, ten years' time as the cultures intertwine.

Feathers.src:
The simple feather is the greatest invention of the avian species. The aviansie race is particularly proud of their plumage and hold lengthy conversations about the best maintenance methods. For the average bird, such as magpies and similar, feathers grant them the ability to soar through the skies, defying the whims of gravity.

They are a vital part of crafting arrows, as the feathers are used for the flights that cause the arrow to fly true.

BakedPotato.src: The simplicity. The elegance. Few things in life are quite as dependable as a good old baked potato. Crispy exterior, fluffy interior, and it goes well with just about anything.

EvasiveInfusion.src: Smaller creatures can be annoyingly good at getting out of harm's way. When boiling water is infused with a small fang belonging to one of these critters, the evasive essence is pulled into the clean water, allowing the drinker to benefit from it.

DubiousMeatPie.src:
The smell from this pie is strange. Undertones of gamey meats, the tantalising touch of subtle herbs and spices. The pastry is crip, inviting…and yet, beneath the crust, hidden behind the pleasantries, is the scent of something otherworldly.

Death has touched this pie.

DowdunReach.TheGarrison.src:
The soldiers needed a place to gather and talk about things without the stigma of brutishness that the mages placed upon them. The garrison served such a purpose. Once it was a place where warriors would gather and discuss things other than battle. They would hold long conversations about their passion for gardening, their love of art, or they would lament their frustrations with management, while the magi assumed they were just getting ready to fight.

There were cells here for prisoners, chains all along the walls. Yet, if you listened closely to the occupants, you would know that this was a place of healing conversations - until everything went to hell.

Now, the knights that roam here have no room in their hearts for idle conversation. Their entire being is overrun by a wild need to destroy. It has become the exact sort of place that the magi had assumed it always had been.

AbyssalSpine.src: The spinal column of an abyssal demon. A monstrous creature from between the gaps in reality. It pulses with hatred, and you’re convinced it wriggles occasionally.

MithrilMace.src:
The standard term is mace, but Vannaka prefers bludgeon. "It's one of those sound words, like stomp and grunt, right? When I hit someone with it, it bludges. Bludge, bludge, bludge."

"You're thinking of onomatopoeia," Dionysius said, helpfully. 

"Nah, but good try. I'm thinking of breakfast," said Vannaka.

Infusion.CoolingArcane.src: The stereotype is that wizards are the lazy corner of the combat triangle. They don't have to swing an axe like a melee warrior, or dodge behind mushrooms like a ranger. They stand stock-still, tossing fireballs: a glass cannon who crosses their non-spellcasting fingers, hoping that they don't get impaled on an arrow. But let me tell you: the wizard has to wear the heaviest, most uncomfortable robes, even in the heat of places like the Umbral Sands, and that is hard work. For those wizards, there is nothing like the cool, soothing taste of a cooling arcane infusion.

StoneArrow.src:
The stone arrow's weight and durability make it a more popular choice among hunters. The hardness of the tip makes it better at piercing tough animal hides or less durable forms of armour. In the second age, druids considered it a form of cheating, citing that it required a human's ingenuity to create rather than being a gift of nature. 

They seldom complained when the evening meal was served, celebrating the success of the hunt alongside everyone else. 

Even with somewhere as remote as Ashenfall, some humans turned to banditry, and they were very fond of stone arrows. Cheap and easy to produce, they help to kill and threaten anyone who makes the mistake of travelling through bandit-controlled woodland. 

One such bandit, the self-described "bandit king, Otho", would choose only "interesting" stones to turn into arrows. Glittering pebbles that swished through the air. He was nicknamed the "Magpie King" because of his love for shiny pebbles. A moniker he was very unhappy with.

BlightwoodStaff.src:
The stranger the wood, the more powerful the magic. It’s unsure why this is, but it’s been true since magic was first discovered. When used as a tool for destructive magic, Garou druids learned the power of blightwood. 

Ashien, a legendary druid among the garou, was among the first to wield such a weapon. As the story goes, they were wandering the swamps when the goddess Lougrim came to her in a vision and gave her a quest.
