Ashien was to journey deep into the swamps and do battle with a demon that dwelled within. 

They found the demon; it emerged out of the fog with a chilling screech and destroyed their staff with a single swing of its blade-like claw. In panic, Ashien blindly reached for the nearest weapon, the root of a swamp tree that had fallen in the mud. Through it, they channeled their will to survive, and it burst free of the branch as a flash of lightning. 

The creature burned beneath Ashien’s gaze, vanishing back into the mists as if it never were. 

Since then, garou druids would favour blightwood when crafting a staff.

StrongSweetTea.src: The strong sweet tea is like being punched and kissed at the same time, which makes it something of an acquired taste. The Wise Old Man swears by it, and mumbles something about "liking my tea like I like my women", which we won't dig into for fear of getting the Wise Old Man cancelled.

StuntedKalphiteWing.src:
The stunted kalphite wing comes from, perhaps unsurprisingly, a stunted kalphite, which is one of the saddest beings in all of Ashenfall. Imagine sharing thoughts with everyone around you, as the kalphite do, and knowing that they think you are a good-for-nothing runt. The other kalphite don't get to hide behind social niceties: their opinions are immediately accessible. 

Of course, all of that is moot now that you have killed the stunted kalphite. Bet you have mixed feelings now.

DireWolfLeather.src:
The tanned hide of a powerful dire wolf. It's sturdy, thick, ready for enchantment and more resilient than normal leather. 

A legend speaks of a warrior that wore the tanned hide of a dire wolf. He wore it proudly as he walked the streets and used it to strike fear into the hearts of bandits and criminals alike. After all, a warrior that could best such a beast, was no one to be trifled with. 

The story goes that one day he met another warrior, proud, skillful and handsome, and the two of them became the best of friends. They would fight together, spar together and rescued helpless villagers as an unstoppable pair. Until the night of the full moon, where the truth was revealed. Where once his new friend had stood, there was now a dread wolf of midnight-black fur and eyes of burning coal. They fought again, but gone was the jovial sparring of friends. Now they fought as man and beast, tooth and claw versus blade and shield, until all that was left of the two of them was this story.

CliffWoods.src:
The temple of Saradomin oversees all of Brynmoor, the stained glass windows once glistened in the sunlight as a beacon to the villagers of Bramblemead, below.

In the Third Age, when the rest of the world was at war, followers of Saradomin arrived on the continent and created a small settlement at the peak of the cliff. Here, the expedition could gaze out over the water, looking back toward the homes they had left, and gazing down towards Bramblemead, the home they would create.

Overtime the expedition mixed with the villagers, leaving their tents and their huts, and finding homes in the village. As the camps were brought down, stones were placed as the foundation of the temple, as the word of Saradomin spread throughout the streets.

Now, millennia later, the temple stands proud, but silent. The walls and windows remain steadfast against the onslaught of time. A faint trace of priestly magic keeps the more monstrous elements from creeping inside. It is a sanctuary against the wild frontiers of Ashenfall, and therefore the home base of the current expedition team.

It is said that the windmill, northwest of the temple, is haunted. The timber creeks ominously even though the sails no longer turn. At night, sinister creatures patrol its exterior, waiting for any opportunity to strike.

RingOfTheWoodcutter.src:
The trees of Ashenfall are infused with magic, which makes them a little more cunning than a normal tree. While lacking sapience, nor sentience, these trees possess on characteristic in abundance – they possess spite.

A tree’s spite resonates back across the axe that cuts it, leaving splinters in the handle and cracks in the blade. Over time this shatters the tool, forcing repairs, which can infuriate lumberjacks when they’re in the middle of a swing.

This ring makes the wearer’s anima feel more in tune with nature, reducing the spite of the tree’s retaliation. While unable to negate it completely, it makes axes last longer and logs feel lighter to carry.

UnusualTrout.src:
The trout is unusual in a few different ways. It's still breathing even out of water, which you could probably classify as more than just 'unusual'. But we like to stay away from hyperbole, so we'll stick with 'unusual' for now.

It also seems to be eyeballing you. Little sideways glances that could be interpreted as judgements. And when you do fail at something - burn a fish, perhaps - it tuts, loudly, like a librarian.

Dragonwolf.src:
The unholy fusion of dragon and beast, creations of twisted dragonkin science. These creatures seem somehow resistant to the cursed nature of the region, but they refuse to sit still long enough for anyone to ask them why.

Not that they would answer, they have a wolf’s mind, not a dragons.

KrillBait.src: The vile ashes embedded in these strange fishing lures whisper to the most sinful part of the fish, drawing them to their demise. At least that’s what the Zamorakian mages claimed. In truth, they were simply tastier and more desirable to the fish, who have little concept of morality.

OakShortbow.src:
The villagers who proved their skills with an ash shortbow were brought into the forest by a Wild Knight instructor in search of more durable wood. The oak stood proud and tall in the forest, standing firm against the ebb of time. Villagers would gather the sturdiest branches that they could and be brought to a quiet place in the wood to begin carving their new bows. 

The Wild Knight would tell them that a good bow is more than just a weapon, but an extension of oneself. They encouraged each villager to put a piece of themselves into the bow, a decoration on the handle, or a poem carved into the wood. Whatever made the bow personal to them. 

This connection in the crafting process would help the villagers feel comfortable with their new weapon, and many young hunters would use the same bow throughout their lives. It even became a tradition for young hunters to gift a bow to their beloved as a marriage proposal. A tradition that survived into the third age.

NecroticBonemeal.src:
The walking dead are strange things, animated by hunger, need, rage and a touch of magic. In Ashenfall it is the hunger of Imaru that drives them, as her great maw draws in the souls of both the living and the dead, the afflicted try to cling to life with everything that they have.

They fail, but the drive remains. Fear, desperation, and simple need keeps the body moving, if not alive. This changes the body, that hunger and rot seeping into the very bones and changing them to be something other than they were.

When ground down, these bones become a powder containing hints of that animating magic. A necromantic resonance with a wide range of uses.

MithrilMedHelm.src:
The warriors of Dowdun Reach were skilled in the manipulation of mithril metal. They made swords, axes, and great hammers that could crush their enemies flat. They crafted impressive suits of armour, though they favoured the more sinister-looking black armour than the mystical-looking mithril. 

One Zamorakian blacksmith, a man called Bob, like so many people on Gielinor, crafted the first mithril medium helm to very little fanfare. He would wear it at every meeting, he would show it off at all the big events, all to impress the women of the keep. You can imagine how well that went. 

Not very well, for clarity's sake.

Fellhollow.LakeOfLostSouls.src:
The water here is filled with the torn fragments of souls, the victims of the Withering and Imaru’s boundless hunger. The waters of Noumenon have seeped in through cracks in the world and infected the great lake that once lay here.

In a forgotten time, great dragons would bathe in the lake alongside villagers and the populace would gather round to relax in the warm springs that fed the lake bed.

Grief and rage had poisoned the waters, turning it into a danger best avoided.

LargeAnimalHorn.src:
The weapons of the animal kingdom can make for useful crafting components. Unfortunately, you generally have to battle against said weapons in order to use them. Many a hunter has underestimated how damaging an animal horn can be.

It is not a mistake they repeat.

WillowRod.src:
The weeping willow is a sallow tree, known for its love of water. Find a brook or ford and a willow will be there, lost in its reflection. 

That familiarity with water makes willow a strong wood for fishing rods. There's the merest wisp of magic running through it, an affinity for water. The fish recognise that affinity and relax. They circle until they're caught, which is pretty handy for an angler.

BirdMeat.src: The white meat of a bird is surprisingly versatile. While delicious on its own, it can be combined with various dishes, seasoned or marinated to create surprisingly varied flavours. The meat is often softer to consume, making it an easier meal for the on-the-go hunter.

BlightwoodLongbow.src:
The wild creatures of Ashenfall have always been elusive. Bramblemead villagers would tell wild stories about the deer that got away or the sheep that shrugged off an arrow. Still, those who could wield a bow rarely left their family hungry. 

One Wild Knight, Frode, was so skilled with the bow that he never returned from a hunt empty-handed. His siblings among the Wild Knights would send him out hunting before every great gathering so that they might feast heartily upon his return. For years, this was their happiest tradition. 

Until the day he did not return. 

It is said that his body was found in five separate places, spread out across the forests of Brynmoor like some gruesome compass. His quiver was empty, yet none of his arrows – marked as they were, with his symbol, an owl – would ever be found.

WillowPlank.src: The willow trees of Fellhollow are some of the only non-haunted things in the area. Therefore, the best plan is clearly to cut them down and slice them into thin little strips so you can make pretty furniture from them.

MagicFocus.src:
The wizard Mallory was never as good as he had hoped to be. He was proficient in spellcasting and his rote memory was excellent, but the power of his spells always fell a little short. He advanced through the ranks mostly through technicality, but he never quite earned the respect of his peers. 

That was until the day he created the focus. Mallory had always been good at making things. He enjoyed the simpler magic of crafting, and he found you could weave small threads of magic into the construction of something, breathing just a little bit more life and wonder into it than before. True craftsmanship, he believed, carried a little bit of the creator’s soul in it. 

The focus proved this theory and elevated it further. By creating a focus and subconsciously imbuing it with a bit of his essence, it would create a smoother, more fluid, channel of magic through the body, which created spells of greater potency. 

Tragically, after sharing his knowledge with the other wizards, he was murdered by his mentor. Who then took his knowledge and claimed it as his own. Karma is a stern judge, however, and the offending wizard later found himself being swallowed whole and digested by a dragon. 

Just punishment, I’m sure Mallory would agree.

DraconicVisWax.src:
The wizards of the Wizards' Tower have managed to artificially generate vis wax, through the Rune Goldberg Machine. It takes piles upon piles of runes and distills them to a thin, waxy substance. It's possibly the least efficient process in the world - the equivalent of sieving a mountain to get a couple of nuggets of gold.

The alternative is to find vis wax in its natural, unfiltered state, but that has its own mountain-sized problems. You need to siphon it from the most dangerous of dragons, and those dragons need to have been in a state of intense rage when they died. It's enough to make a wizard sigh and approach the mountain with a newly bought sieve.

KotHaar-Hur.src:
There are few beings on all of Gielinor as strange as the KotHaar. They, like their distant cousins the TzHaar, were once members of the TokHaar race, but long ago split from the hive mind to serve a different function: protecting the Lens.

Each of the KotHaar is an individual, yet they do not see themselves as a separate organism from one another. They function something like an insect hive, each of the KotHaar fulfilling a specific function, so that the greater community can exist.

They have no leaders. No politics. No selfish desires. They exist for one another: a perfect, cohesive whole.

Or they did. Fuzan put an end to that.

The KotHaar-Hur are workers. Once, they served as the backbone of KotHaar society. They lifted the rocks, they carved out underground tunnels. They are the glue that kept a secret society of obsidian creatures together. Now, the magma that animates them has been turned against them by Fuzan’s Mark, and the KotHaar-Hur turn from labourers to cannon fodder in Fuzan’s twisted games.

Guthix.src:
There are few gods with a heart so heavy as that of Guthix. Born to the world of Naragun, which was destroyed by warring gods, he achieved ascension in an act of grief-ridden vengeance and has regretted that decision ever since.

He was the first god to discover Gielinor and the powerful anima flow within it, and he used this power to grow stronger. Yet, it was when he discovered the Stone of Jas, a powerful artefact and tool of the Elder Gods, that Guthix would become the legendary figure that he is.

The god of balance slept through the God Wars, only waking to be reminded of the danger that gods represent. He created a powerful barrier to banish the gods, keeping them from returning to this world.

For a time Gielinor was safe and Guthix slept beneath the ground, drawing power from the anima.

Ancient and full of a deep grief, Guthix had come to believe that a world could only be safe if there were no gods left to rule it, and he laid out the path for his own end. He was slain by the Mahjarrat Sliske, which brought an end to the Fifth Age and ushered in the return of the gods.

For a time the world fell into chaos, until powerful heroes forged an alliance and created Edicts of their own, banishing the gods and leaving Gielinor, once more, in the hands of mortals.

SteelShield.src:
There are few things as good at shielding you from harm, as a great slab of metal between you and your foe. The steel shield is more durable than its iron kin, capable of resisting greater and more deadly blows.

It was popular among Fellhollow locals, who would play a game that indicated an intelligence shortage among the population. The game consisted of one player being equipped with a crossbow and other players would hide around the area carrying steel shields. The crossbow wielder would then hunt the other players and try and fire a bolt into their shields, marking them as out of the game.

Unsurprisingly the injuries caused by this game were large and common place. Even the death of some of the players wouldn’t cause the activity to be banned. “It’s tradition”, “it’s just good fun”, “hardly anyone gets hurt”, these were the arguments made even as parents grieved the loss of their child from the game.

KalphiteSoldier.src:
There are many people who argue that the military is “in their blood”, and aside from those who were part of secret, medical conspiracy theories, this is not a biological truth. While you can dedicate your life to the military machine, it is a choice, not a certainty.

For the kalphite soldier it is a literal reality. They have the military in their blood. Their very genetic structure is designed with the singular purpose – battle. They are pure warriors, with minds that think of nothing else other than the defence of the hive.

The queen creates the soldier with intent. When she lays her eggs, she releases certain chemicals harvested from ingested metal ore, in this case adamantite, and it bonds with the growing larvae, becoming something stronger. That is why the soldiers' shells are harder and their mandibles more dangerous, because they are forged in the embryonic sac to be killers.

Fun fact, friend: soldier eggs are revolting. This is true of all fried eggs, but the soldier ones taste particularly bad.

MysticThread.src:
There are many steps to making mystic robes – fibres to thread, thread to cloth, cloth to robes – but you would be wise not to skip any of them. Habberdash the Impatient, a magician who lived in Temple Woods, attempted to make his robes solely from thread. He would wrap himself, round and round, with spool after spool of mystic thread, and then attempt battle.

You can imagine how it went. He got snagged on a goblin's helmet and quickly unwound, mid-battle. We're not sure who would have been more shocked: Habberdash, who promptly got stabbed in the gut, or the goblin, who was confronted with a wizard in his undergarments.

Ectoplasm.src:
There are many theories on what ectoplasm is, each as disturbing as the last. Some say that it’s emotion, condensed over years of existence. Others think that it’s some sort of infection of the soul, as only the undead seem to produce it.

In truth, ectoplasm is none of these. It’s the outer shell of a soul, the skin more or less, and acts as a sort of lubrication between the flesh and the spirit. Tiny bits of reality combine with the immaterial otherness of the underworld and congeal into a sort of spiritual mixture that ghosts and other undead find incredible useful.

Necromancers prize the stuff, finding a myriad of uses for it. Most people find it weird and decidedly “icky”.

RawShrimp.src: There are many ways to cook shrimp. Countless recipes that promise wonderful taste sensations. Right now, though, I would suggest you don’t really want to eat them. They’re all wriggly.

AdamantBarbedArrows.src:
There are moments in life where you just decide that something must be forced to suffer. These arrows are designed just for that. When your enemy aggrieves you so much that you want to rip and tear and bleed them to death, this is the arrow for you.

The Moon Garou do not use these arrows, even though they are aware of their construction. They consider it an unnecessary amount of suffering to inflict, when a well-placed shot is quicker and less dangerous for everyone else. 

Bandits that take up these arrows soon find themselves mistrusted even by their fellow thieves.

GypsumRock.src: There are more glamorous rocks to mine than gypsum. If you want to get an amorous wink from a dwarf then you should probably aim for diamond or adamantite. But gypsum is an honest, hard-working rock that is exceptionally practical. Gypsum just needs a better PR agent.

ZamorakSword.src:
There are myths and anecdotes about Zamorak appearing to the inhabitants of Dowdun Reach. Few truly believe them. Zamorak is not one for hiding his presence: he's more theatrical than that.

But while the Children of Shadows do not believe that Zamorak has been to Dowdun, they still cling to a hope that he will come. That hope is the only explanation for why the Zamorak Sword exists.

The Zamorak Sword, made of finest dragon-vulcanised black metal, was reserved for Zamorak. It was never used, not once. When the chaos god arrived in the keep, he was to be handed the sword. It was made for him, a token of his glory.

It is yours now. How it is used is entirely down to you. Perhaps you will reserve it for Zamorak too, leaving it in a storage chest until the time of his return. Or perhaps you'll immediately sully it with kebbit blood. The choice is yours.

ZamorakStaff.src:
There are myths and anecdotes about Zamorak appearing to the inhabitants of Dowdun Reach. Few truly believe them. Zamorak is not one for hiding his presence: he's more theatrical than that.

It may be hard to believe, but some have tried to summon Zamorak to Dowdun Reach. Call it the hubris of a demon summoner: a student feels they have mastered the art of summoning demons, so believes the next rung on the ladder is a god. Never mind that Zamorak has no ounce of demon in him.

Zamorak can be accused of many things, but he does have a sense of humour. These attempts have been greeted with a gift. He has been known to kick a bloodveld through the portal, or another creature he has to hand. It gives the demon summoner a little spot-test.

GoblinPlagueshot.src:
There are some goblin archers that have decided that they genuinely hate everything else in the world. Years of honing their craft, and gaining little to no recognition from their peers, has turned them into cruel and vindictive creatures who want to see everyone else suffering around them. They do this, primarily, through a horrible congealed substance that they dip their arrows in. They call it Plagueshot, and you really don't want to know what's in it. 

No, really, you don't. Suffice to say that wounds inflicted by arrows coated in this noxious substance tend to infect the target with a nasty poison, as well as a whole host of unpleasant maladies. 

If you're hit by one of these arrows, I strongly recommend a bath. Several of them. Preferably in bleach.

PoisonshotArcher.src:
There are some goblin archers that have decided that they genuinely hate everything else in the world. Years of honing their craft, and gaining little to no recognition from their peers, has turned them into cruel and vindictive creatures who want to see everyone else suffering around them. They do this, primarily, through a horrible congealed substance that they dip their arrows in. They call it Poisonshot, and you really don't want to know what's in it. 

No, really, you don't. Suffice to say that wounds inflicted by arrows coated in this noxious substance tend to infect the target with a nasty poison, as well as a whole host of unpleasant maladies. 

If you're hit by one of these arrows, I strongly recommend a bath. Several of them. Preferably in bleach.

LightningBerserker.src:
There are those among the garou who were born in the Stormtouched Highlands and inherited some of its scorn. Their blood boiled and their movements crackled with lightning, emulating the great storm that afflicted their homes. This created a constant itching sensation, that occasionally bloomed into pain. Suffice to say it was enough to drive them quite mad. 

Most of these garou would not live to see adulthood, as the pain distracted them at dangerous moments, cutting their lives short. Those that do survive become berserkers, finding ways to turn their constant storm-filled rage into a power to wield against their prey.

FarmersHat.src:
There are those who spend years studying the magic of druids, to try and find a way to bend nature to their will. They go on long pilgrimages, solve complicated riddles and have arduous conversations with nature spirits about the fundamentals of reality. 

They needn't have bothered. For, you see, there are already those who understand how to reshape the land to serve them. People who cultivate rows of plants, each of them focused on providing food, medicine or some other benefit to their agricultural master. The farmer may be the greatest nature wizard in all of Gielinor, though they need never utter a single spell. 

This hat was once worn by the farmers of Bramblemead as a sign of their status. It was created by one Abigail Potterington, age 6, who had been taught the basics of embroidery by her mother, who had been taught it by her mother, and she by her mother and so on. The flower was said to represent a great towering oak – Abigail was not good at art.

Monkfish.src:
There are, in fact, two variants of the monkfish. One is the Piscatoris monkfish, known for its gamey taste and slightly depressed countenance. The other is the Ashenfall monkfish, which has a more trout-like flavour and a happier, almost smirking countenance. Anglers, who like to simplify things, distinguish them by calling them 'sad boy' and 'happy boy'.

Both monkfish are 'sad boys' when they're caught, of course.

AdamantArrows.src:
There is a constant battle between fletchers and armour smiths to one up each other. The armour smiths craft armour from stronger, sturdier and harder materials, meaning arrows must be made of equally, or greater, sturdiness of materials to pierce through them.

The adamant arrow is a shining example of this eternal conflict. The metal is durable, powerful and deadly in the right hands, and pierces mithril, steel and lesser metals with almost mocking ease. Only adamant and greater quality armour stands a chance against them.

BlueDragonScale.src:
There is a curious trend in Gielinor, whereby the most fragile fighters – archers and magic users – are the easiest to spot. From blue dragonhide to mystic robes, the fashion is to wear garish colours, as if the rules of the animal kingdom apply. But no, archers and magic users aren't poisonous, venomous or hoping to be mistaken for a bee.

We wonder why that lack of subtlety might be. In the case of blue dragons and their scales, perhaps it's a cruel joke played by the dragonkin. They have seen that humans keep killing their creations, wearing their hides as trophies. They've got their revenge by way of a generous use of the rainbow.

GarouRunt.src:
There is a humility to the garou exile. These lowborn garou are not cast out of society: they choose to leave it themselves. They accept that they have been dealt a poor physiological hand and take leave of the camp. They know that the only way to return is to become stronger, and that requires exposure to Ashenfall's threats. 

The exiles live outside of the main encampments, sometimes in packs, hoping to harden themselves on any brigand that might pass their way. If you see runts approaching, you might even note glee on their faces. You are a rung on an imagined ladder: a step towards acceptance. Take pride in the fact that they have seen you as a threat, and deem you as someone who might make them stronger.

DowdunReach.ThePastures.src:
There is a phrase “to put them out to pasture” which is used to describe someone being discarded, or perhaps even left to die. In Dowdun Reach, this was depressingly literal. There’s a reason that the rats are everywhere in the Pastures - a reason why the grass is so alive, despite the dilapidation of the rest of the region. 

It is because the soil is nurtured by the bodies of those cultists that were not able to keep up with the rest of the fortress.

Sardine.src:
There is a popular game among children, where they hide themselves around the house and then other children join them once their hiding place has been discovered. It was a game clearly invented by very tired parents, who wanted to make sure their kids were well behaved and contained in a well-known location. After all, where else can you fit seventeen children, if not in a wardrobe?

Sadly for Gielinor’s fisherfolk, the namesake creature of said children’s game does not possess the same desire to make its captor’s life easier. Fortunately, however, they are numerous enough that one need not worry too much about the difficulty of catching them.

Fellhollow.WitchwillowRange.src:
There is a story in Emberwood about the witch of the forest. She lived, so the stories claim, in the great willow groves, working spells and brewing potions that would bring the forest to life. She turned princes into frogs, spindles into deathtraps and little girls were warned to never accept crimson cloaks from strangers at night.

Of course, none of this was true. There was a witch who lived in the willow groves, a kindly old thing called Beatrice. She spent most of her time growing a little garden, and feeding the animals that came to wander by. Never once did she curse any princes, and the only cloaks she offered were when the rains were heavy and the wind far too cold.

Trout.src:
There is little exciting one can say about trout, they have few advocates and fewer fans. Yet, they do taste delicious with a little lemon and a few herbs, so perhaps we should thank them for not being awful.

One trout was awful. A villain. A monster who rose from the depths to bring terror to us all.

Nah, just kidding – they’re trout… I got nothing.

RatMasterSkrexis.src:
There is no "Rat Master" position in the Black Knights or Zamorakian Magi. Rat Master is very much self-appointed.

Rats would come and go through the banquet hall, the dorms and the library, and Skrexis would watch them. There was one rat – fat as a carnivorous chinchompa – that led them. One eye was scarred and its claws were long, made for gouging. Skrexis monitored the rats' movements, noting when they would be in each room. The rats had a timetable; they were predictable.

Skrexis waited for the fat, leader rat in the kitchens. He sat, cross-legged, with a saucepan in his lap. A wave of rats poured into the kitchen, saw Skrexis and flooded back out. But the fat rat, it approached, one eye locked on the seated man.

Skrexis wished there was someone, a bard perhaps, to have seen that fight. It was for the ages. The two combatants scratched, lurched, swung and skittered, but Skrexis emerged victorious. Bloodied, he approached the rats who had been watching from the doorframe.

Skrexis had earned the title of Rat Master by way of combat.

RedDragonLeather.src: There is no better advert for red dragon leather than Fuzan. The tyrant of Umbral Sands has seen his fair share of upstarts. Moon Garou of all shapes and sizes have confronted him over the years, and none have managed to break his red leather hide. The only blades to have cut him were the claws of his mother, and the glaive of one mutinous KotHaar. Fuzan has met very little resistance over his long life, which might go some way to explaining why he is the way he is.

AxtralProjection.src:
There is nothing trees fear more than this spell. Crafted by their ancient enemy, the lumberjack, this spell has wiped out whole legions of arboreal sentinels. Guthix taught this spell to the people of Brynmoor, hoping that it would help them expand their settlement. It worked perhaps too well, and soon entire forests would find themselves reduced to stumps. Guthix was forced to implement restrictions to the spell, preventing any but the most senior druids from using it. 

Since his death this restriction has been lifted, and the trees tremble in the terror that is to come.

Blightwood.src:
There is something about the swamps of Ashenfall that encourage strange trees to grow. The result is blightwood, durable, powerful and somehow capable of channeling more potent magic than other trees.

The wild knights joked that blightwood houses the souls of the victims of the swamp, and that they are imbued with their regrets and hatred.

It’s probably not true. Probably.

UndeadEel.src: There is something deeply disturbing about a fish that refuses to die. More disturbing still are the eels that slither and writhe and wriggle beneath the waters, their hearts no longer beating and their eyes filled with the milky-white film of rot and decay.

OakWand.src:
There was a room in the Brynmoor School of Magic that every new student visited at least once. The students' purposes differed, of course: some students wanted to see if it was merely myth; others wanted to simply observe it; a few wanted to go a little further...

The room was Arnuld's Sanctum. In the centre of the circular room was a single pedestal with an oak wand. From a distance, it looked like it floated, but step closer and it would be clear that it was supported with a stand of glass. There were no inscriptions on the pedestal, no decorations on the walls. The room lacked any detailing, outside of a single sprig of holly, etched onto the lower-half of the wand.

No one had been able to grasp the oak wand to take it. Any fool who tried would be overcome by the sensation that they were on fire. They would drop to the floor, contorting in an effort to remove flames that were not there. Only the stupid and self-worthy would attempt it, and there was always a crowd of third- and fourth-years to watch and laugh at them.

When the School of Magic fell to fire (which had nothing to do with the wand), no one had the presence of mind to visit the Sanctum. Fire surged up the pedestal, and the wand's magical protection dropped. Embracing the fire, the wand was consumed, as if it were finally with its own kind. Then the pedestal dropped and something opened.

SuperFocusedMining.src: There was a time when certain Moon Garou miners would down vial after vial of super focused mining potions. The hope was that they could find a mine, away from the Scorch, and work away at gypsum deposits without having to stop for hours. After the super focused potion wore off, they would step out of their trance state and survey the material for moonstones. It's likely a good explanation for why moonstones are so rare - perhaps even mythical - to the modern garou.

UndeadRangersBow.src:
There was a villager in Emberwood called Holtz, who was a master with the bow. He could shoot rats from across a field and never scored less than a bullseye whenever he aimed for an archery target. Yet he had no desire for warfare, and no matter the words of encouragement from the captain, he would never join the guard.

For him, archery was a passion, an art, never to be used against another person. A stance quickly forgotten by his shambling corpse.

WildScoutsShortbow.src:
There was magic once, in this bow, though it has mostly faded now. Runes were ground down and mixed with plant oils to create a special resin that allowed the Wild Knights to work their magic through the bow, as if they were carrying runes. That magic has faded and the recipe for the mixture is lost to the ages, but these bows are still formidable in their own right.

Wild Knights told tales of creatures that lived within the wilds of Ashenfall and that could not be felled by normal bows. Deer with hides that glistened with starlight, sheep with silver fleeces that repelled all arrows. They claimed that these magically infused bows were the only ones capable of harming such creatures, though none ever returned with trophies to share.

IronArrowBroadhead.src:
There was once a battle between two archers, the human soldier, Eileena, and a garou archer called Krayth. The two were pitted in battle together across the King’s Pass. They camouflaged themselves and hid on opposite sides of the pass, picking off each other’s soldiers as they tried to pass.

As the battle raged on, the tension between Eileena and Krayth grew. Their stealth skills were unmatched, making it impossible for either to spot the other. Both were disciplined and ruthless, their focus solely on the kill. They were a perfect match, each move calculated, each shot deadly.

For months, their battle continued, neither side gaining a foothold over the other as these two archers stayed hidden. Until a single arrow changed the stalemate. It was an arrow from neither archer, a single broad-headed bolt that struck a garou child. Eileen refused to take another shot; children had never been acceptable targets under her watch.  

The pass fell to garou control shortly after.

DowdunReach.TheNexus.src:
There were geniuses who joined the ranks of the Zamorakian wizards. People who pushed the very limits of the magical sciences to achieve fantastical heights. The nodestones were one such experiment.

Nodestones were short range teleporters, connected together through the Dreamingstone Network, and they made life much easier for the residents of the keep. Nowadays, walks that would have taken entire minutes, could take seconds, and the Black Knights rejoiced in their exceedingly heavy armour.

Of course, some side effects did occur, mostly in the waistline. As armour became harder and harder to put on each day, the leadership were forced to create rigorous training programs that forced knights to run around the walls of the keep.

SteelCrossbow.src:
There were no garou in Fellhollow for the people to deal with, so in the early days of the settlement people created steel crossbows primarily for hunting game. The dragons that guarded the people were gentle creatures, but possessed of an enormity so vast that they required a great deal of food to keep going. Hunting, therefore, became a very popular activity, with many competitions and events crafted to provide meals for the draconic caretakers. 

When the withering began to spread and the dead began to rise, steel bolts proved just as effective at piercing a zombie’s skull as it would catching the quarry from a hunt. 

Though the dead would come in droves, the crossbow would let them be taken out at great distance, keeping the last remaining settlements safer for just a few days longer. Every moment counted in those final days.

SkeletalMarauder.src:
There were once warriors in Fellhollow that wielded great weapons with tremendous force. They were boastful, proud and dangerous people – yet they were beloved.

A tradition among these great hulking figures, was to seek out a far smaller person and act as their shield. They became the guardian angels of the bullied and the protectors of the abused. Wielding their great blades to fight against cruelty or unkindness, making the world happier by force.

Now that instinct is gone.

These skeletal creatures remember only that a sword must be swung, and that a blade needs to cut into flesh. They remember only that bone must be cleaved and that the living must be turned into the dead, swelling their armies with each swing of the blade.

StatusEffects.src:
There’s more than just bruising that awaits the unprepared adventurer, Ashenfall’s also home to a number of different conditions we in the biz like to refer to as status effects.

These effects, once inflicted, cause a continuing problem for a while. You could spend too much time in the Bloodblight Swamp and become poisoned, slowly losing health as time drags on.

Certain creatures and weapons may inflict you with nasty cuts that cause bleeding, leading to a large amount of damage if not dealt with quickly.

Each Status Effect is its own special little problem, and it’s a good idea to make sure you pay close attention to any that you run across.

WizardRobeLegs.src:
These blue robes are the signature clothing worn by every respectable mage. Apprentices look forward to the day they first wear these, as it shows they have graduated to full wizard status. The wizard's tower, in particular, uses these robes as a uniform, signifying their magical power and fealty to the god of order, Saradomin.

All documents have been expunged of the events that came to be known as the Day of Purple Feathers. No wizard or knight will speak of what occurred. However, villagers soon learned that squawking like a chicken would send both knight and wizard into unexplained panic.

For some reason, the egg deliveries to the Wizard's guild were cancelled around the same time.

WizardRobeBody.src:
These blue robes are the signature clothing worn by every respectable mage. Apprentices look forward to the day they first wear these, as it shows they have graduated to full wizard status. The wizard's tower, in particular, uses these robes as a uniform, signifying their magical power and fealty to the god of order, Saradomin.

Despite the antagonistic intentions of the White Knights' arrival in the Wizard’s Guild, the two factions got along well. Apprentices would often prank low-ranked knights, using small spells to make them appear foolish. The knights would respond with more practical reprisals, which led to an escalation of shenanigans until the highest-ranking members of both orders got involved. Then things got really out of hand.

WizardRobeHead.src:
These blue robes are the signature clothing worn by every respectable mage. Apprentices look forward to the day they first wear these, as it shows they have graduated to full wizard status. The wizard's tower, in particular, uses these robes as a uniform, signifying their magical power and fealty to the god of order, Saradomin.

On Ashenfall, it was rare for those wearing these robes to be seen outside the wizard's guild. The structure on the hillside was home to strange practices and even stranger experiments. Powerful spells were studied and unleashed across an already magically problematic countryside.

The White Knights, often summoned to address the perils that the wizard's guild inadvertently unleashed, were a frequent presence. Their duties ranged from quelling peculiar weather phenomena to managing the 'accidental' summoning of demons. To maintain control, a contingent of knights established a permanent residence within the guild, their vigilant eyes ever watchful.

SalveCrystal.src:
These crystals only grow in a cave beneath the river Salve, back in Misthalin. They are imbued with the holy energies of that river, making them a powerful ward against the undead.

Doric has been using one as a paperweight, ever since he found one on sightseeing holiday.

It’s probably blasphemous, but no one’s complained so far.

BirdFillet.src: These fillets go surprisingly well with most side dishes. The texture is pleasant, the flavour is subtle and not too overpowering. They go particularly well with garlic.

Seeds.Pumpkin.src:
These gourds are most popular around the autumn, where they are hollowed out by local children and used to ward away spirits – poorly, as it seems they attract more than they repel.

Indeed one strange fellow found himself so delighted by the strange gourds that he took an aspect of them into himself, feeling that they best embodied his favourite time of the year. So the strange individual known as “Pumpkin Pete”, part of the Pete family, came to be.

GraniteDeposit.src: These great lumps of rock are sturdier than normal stone and are excellent materials for construction.

Wheat.src: These humble grains are the staple of many a burgeoning society. Breads, cakes, pastries and all manner of delicious foodstuffs can be forged from these marvellous stalks.

GarouPack.src: These leathery packs are carried around by garou warriors. They store rations, herbs and the spoils of battle inside. Crafted by elderly garou in the villages, or parents sending their child off to battle.

MapleSapling.src: These little trees are raised by their parents to follow the doctrines of Zamorak. If they were capable of movement, or any action at all, they’d be very problematic to the rest of the world.

RotriddenRat.src: These nasty little creatures embody all the viciousness of their living kin, but with the added hatred of an undead dragon. Their bites will wither your soul, threatening to drag you into Imaru's gaze.

Seeds.Kwuarm.src: These plants are greedily hoarded by goblins and garou, their poisonous capabilities highly desired by their scouts. With these seeds, you no longer need to slaughter goblins in droves to acquire these herbs, instead you are now able to grow them yourself in your own back yard.

PipeCactus.src:
These prickly customers thrive in the desert, wanting nothing more than the warm sun on their sharp, nasty little thorns.

Cut these down to collect useful fibres that can be woven into desert cloth.

Dragonstone.src:
These purple stones are a wonder to behold. The way the light catches them and sparkles - it can delight even the smallest of children for many hours.

It was for this reason that it’s been sought after by artisans everywhere. Or possibly because of its inherent magical properties?

Nah, must be the distracting kids things. I’ve spoken to parents, a little quiet time seems like it’s worth its weight in gold.

LesserRedDragon.src:
These red dragons are only lesser when compared to Fuzan, the strongest red dragon currently active in the region.  Despite their weaker stature to their draconic overlord, the lesser red dragons are still some of the deadliest creatures in the region.

Like Fuzan, the red dragons here are fuelled by a desire to destroy. The fire that rages in their bellies yearns to be unleashed upon anything that moves - or doesn’t move (as some poor cacti have discovered). They torment the locals, and delight in their suffering.

A few red dragons give themselves grandiose names, in an attempt to claim their own legacy. One dragon, known as The Radiant, torments the Manafem Moon Garou. For years now, The Radiant has destroyed caravans, eaten travellers and brought suffering to the camp, for no reason other than their capacity to do so.

Cruelty is a deeply embedded trait in the red dragons of Ashenfall, and they view mercy as a weakness to be exploited.

BlightwoodRoot.src: These roots have absorbed more of the anima than other roots around them. It has made them stronger and more durable than the rest of the flora around them.

RedBerries.src: These simple berries might be the gap between life and death, if eaten at the right time. A favourite treat for the villagers of Bramblemead, who would mix the berries into various desserts to enjoy. The red berry pie was particularly popular with visiting Wild Knights.

PrimordialHeart.src:
These strange hearts contain the lingering essence of a nature spirit. A gentle heartbeat, waiting to be reborn to a world free of Imaru’s corruption.

Ashenfall’s nature spirits are creatures of the land, possessing myriad forms and shapes as dictated by the wild anima flowing around them. In Fellhollow their favoured form is that of the terrorbird, a beast favoured by gnome riders on the mainland.

As Imaru’s hunger infected the land, it began to leech away the vitality that kept these creatures healthy and strong. Their forests waned, from great acres of willow trees, down to a handful of groves, the last places their power would reach.

As the land dies, so too do the spirits that protect it. As creatures of the endless cycle, they must be hunted, die and be reborn to return to strength. Yet, there are no hunters in Fellhollow any more. No great beasts roaming the land to slay these gentle spirits.

So, you must be that hunter. You must kill the spirit, so that it may be reborn when Fellhollow thrives once more. How ever many years from now that may be.

Seeds.Watermelon.src: These tiny seeds can grow into a delightful patch of scrumptious watermelons. Use them to grow plants that can create delicious fruit salads, add garnish to garish cocktails, or you could paint faces on them if you’re very lonely.

KingsToken.src:
These tokens are a unique creation, crafted hundreds of years ago by high priests of Lougrim. They are passed down from monarch to monarch, a sign of their overwhelming power and strength. The power of a king has waned over the centuries, no longer sovereigns of nations, but now masters of the clan. Servants of the High Queen, Kuldra, the god-eater.

Inside each token rests a single pebble taken from Antumnos, the Garou homeworld.

PurifiedKingsToken.src:
These tokens are a unique creation, crafted hundreds of years ago by high priests of Lougrim. They are passed down from monarch to monarch, a sign of their overwhelming power and strength. This token has been blessed as part of an ancient Garou ritual, symbolically wiping away Gielinor's "corruption". Although it looks no different to before it was purified, it feels strangely lighter and is a little cold to the touch. 

Inside each token rests a single pebble taken from Antumnos, the Garou homeworld, and if you focus your senses you're sure you can feel the faintest pulse from within.

GraniteMaulWrap.src: These wrappings are made from the leather of a powerful and dangerous beast. The ambient anima of Ashenfall infuses it with a sturdiness that most leather wrapping can’t equal.

SilverRock.src: They say that silver is touched by the moon, explaining why the lycanthropes are so affected by it. Silver makes for an exceptionally good magical conductor, making it highly prized by enchanters everywhere.

MagicLogs.src: They say that you can tell how old a tree is by cutting it down and counting the rings. That's true of most trees, but not the magic tree. A magic tree is coy about its age and prefers to hide its rings. All that's left is to guess a magic tree's age, and - as per the adage - a gentleman should never try to guess a magic tree's age. At least guess a few decades younger: they're sensitive to that sort of thing.

Pumpkin.src:
They seem strange without faces, don’t they?

Heralds of the spookiest of seasons, the humble pumpkin exists in two worlds, the world of the living and the world of the dead. When carved it acts as a ward against dangerous spirits and when mixed with spices and added to warm drinks, it acts as a lure for ex-girlfriends, distracting them as it gives you time to escape.

FlankSteak.src: Thick and juicy, the Flank Steak is more filling than you might first expect. The dense meat means each mouthful makes you fuller for longer.

BestialMeat.src: Thick and tough to chew, this meat makes for a filling meal, but an exercise to bite through.

HardenedLeather.src: Thicker and more resilient than normal leather. Still smells though.

Perks.src:
Think of perks a little like status effects that don’t want to kill you. They’re friendly, helpful even. Certain foods, drinks, potions and other things, may give you temporary benefits. These benefits, called perks, might be resistances to certain effects, or perhaps they’ll give you an edge in combat.

There are several perks to discover and mastering them will make your adventures much easier.

PoisonPlantBulb.src: This bulb is infused with deadly toxins. Prized by herblore enthusiasts and hated by chefs in equal measure.

CapeOfTheUndead.src: This cape is all that remains of the once proud archers of Fellhollow. Hunters and scouts who would stalk the forests and woodland hunting game to feed the other villagers. As the time dragged on their flesh and clothes have rotted away, leaving only this cape as a reminder of their existence.

UnfiredClayDecoration.src: This clay nicknack will look really nice on a shelf, once you’ve cooked it in the kiln. Otherwise it’ll just leave red stains everywhere.

AbyssalDemonCape.src: This cloak is infused with the dark power of the Abyss. It's probably fine, definitely not cursed at all. Honest.

FarmMeat.src: This dense meat is a sturdy meal when prepared properly. It comes from larger animals who are far less willing to give it up than their smaller kin, making it a well deserved delicacy.

GoblinPack.src: This foul smelling container is made from animal hide and filled with whatever trinkets its owner collected. Occasionally a goblin will keep a pet beetle, worm or spider in these, so be careful when opening.

RedTopaz.src: This glittering gemstone really catches the light, sparkling like a tiny little star that’s dying. Count Valingard, one of Brynmoor’s nobility in the third age, was very fond of these stones and was said to have an entire chandelier made from them. Sadly, dragon fire appears to be particularly good at melting them, so the chandelier is no longer with us.

Kwuarm.src:
This herb has travelled far to deliver its malicious benefits to the people of Ashenfall. Its name, in Dwarvish, means “warm death” since it causes a terrible burning fever if the sap is consumed.

Crushed down, so that it’s sap and oils can be easily accessed, this herb is a requirement in some of the deadliest and most dangerous poisonous mixtures.

MapleRod.src:
This is it. You've made it now. The pinnacle of Dowdun Reach fishing: ownership of a maple rod. Don't let it go to your head. The hook will get stuck in your nostril. 

The humble angler doesn't draw attention to the maple rod. They don't wax it or buy it a nice kebbit-fur sheath. They don't name it something like Deborah or kiss it before they go to bed.

No, the humble angler strides into the middle of other anglers and says "levels?". They hear the fishing levels of others and nod in appreciation. 

Be the humble angler.

Delrom.src:
This is not Delrom's first summoning rodeo. He was summoned once before into ScapeRune – a twisted, upside-down version of RuneScape. 

To his dismay, he was the subject of a quest called Demon Lover. Let's just say that the only demon rings there were the ones that adventurers wanted to put on his finger.

In the end, he managed to unsummon himself by wielding Darklight and saying the magical phrase Reba Melrac Muhtniremac Odnibag Iahcrup. It was a close call.

ClayMold.src: This mould can be used in crafting.

RubyVine.src:
This offshoot of the wild jade vine has been mutated by the power of the Lens and the terrible Scorching sun. Whereas most vines require water, the ruby vine requires heat. Their chlorophyl has been replaced with embers and their stalks and stems burn internally, creating an incinerator that they use to ignite their prey.

Fuzan thinks they’re pretty, and makes sure to cultivate them all over the desert.

Liverwort.src:
This plant is not fun to encounter, and many gardeners scream in horror when they see their telltale bulbs. They contain a strange gas that reacts violently to the air, which is problematic at the best of times.

Bizarrely they were much beloved by certain dragonkin seers, the mystical oracles without any clan. They would cultivate the bulbs and use the gasses for certain ritual practices that make little sense to anyone else.

SuperFocusedWoodcutting.src: This potion gives you lumber tunnel vision, where the tunnel is made of tasteful wood rather than bricks. All there is - aside from the tunnel - is you and the tree, mano et arboro. One of the greatest, most heated rivalries of all time.

SuperFocusedCookin.src:
This potion imbues you with the desire to bake. Cakes, pies, biscuits, battas, all things culinary become your obsession. While under its effects, you will grow to understand more about nutrition and flavour profiles. You will transcend the limits of your taste buds into realms of deliciousness that only Brassica Prime can comprehend.

Use this potion wisely.

FocusedConstructionPotion.src:
This potion is sweet, yet strong. The ingredients have steeped within the mixture for some time and allowed it to increase in potency. While it’s perfectly fine to drink it directly from the bottle, you find yourself wishing you had a nice mug to use instead.

Still, this potion makes you acutely (haha, see what I did there?) aware of angles. You can measure a plank of wood with just a few well placed glances. The inner architect in you revels at the new possibilities before you, and you find yourself planning much further ahead.

FocusedMiningPotion.src:
This potion makes it easier to swing a pickaxe. Your muscles are more relaxed and able to handle greater strain, making it easier to strike at the ore, learning its weak points.

Druids used to whip up huge batches of this for visiting dwarves, who would mix it with beer for dubious results.

WeakWarmingPotion.src: This potion never chills, always tasting warm on the tongue. It's sweet, like hot chocolate round a warming fire and that feeling spreads throughout the drinker's body, shielding them from the chill of night.

FocusedAttackPotion.src:
This potion streamlines your vision and hones your reflexes. Your synapses surge with clarity and you find it easier to understand the nuance of the blade.

The Wild Knights relied heavily on these potions to train their new fighters during the decline of the Guthixian faith. With fewer numbers, it became more important to teach people quickly.

SuperAntifire.src:
This potion was created by a Moon Garou chef with ambitious far greater than their common sense. They yearned to create the greatest grilled steak ever made and required rather more fire than their kitchen was equipped to handle.

The resulting conflagration was so impressive, that it inspired a local alchemist to create this magnificent countermeasure.

LumberjackPotion.src: This potion helps you sleep all night and work all day. It gives you the feeling of well oiled elbow and shoulder joints, and it numbs the pain in your muscles from swinging an axe for long stretches at a time.

RingOfTheMoon.src:
This ring glints in the moonlight with an unnatural sparkle belying the magic within. The ring’s power causes the wearer’s anima circulation to strengthen in the darkness, but struggling to resist the light of the day.

Very popular with teenage villagers going about their black-tunic phase.

InspiringRingOfConstruction.BuildersRing.src:
This ring is infused with tiny elements of the dragonkin Brakka, a powerful creature and an architect of some skill. His hubris remains, even after his death at Kuldra’s hands, and motes of his knowledge can be preserved within crystalline structures.

Although you cannot glean the secrets of the dragonkin from these motes of memory, his instinct and innate talent for construction and be harnessed to create a ring that makes it easier to understand the art of architecture.

RingOfTheHerd.src:
This ring was often used as an engagement ring. The magic weaves souls together and makes their anima resonate in harmony. The resulting change allows for the body to regenerate more readily, enhancing their time together and forging bonds of companionship.

Naturally it only requires the bonds of camaraderie, rather than romance, and was very popular among bands of hunters, farmers or anyone else. Longtime comrades would often gift each other with these rings as a sign of their bond of friendship.

Sketchbook.src:
This sketchbook has been damaged beyond repair, the pictures long-since faded. As far as you can tell, that’s for the best. Seemingly filled with people of unnatural proportions – muscles the size of watermelons, torsos easily five sizes larger than the waistlines, and the ears… so fluffy.

Hands so unnaturally large it creates some sort of primal fear within you.

It’s probably for the best that this book was buried beneath the stone.

Clay.src: This sticky brown substance is rarely considered the right answer to the classic joke, however it has many more uses outside the realm of low-tier comedy.

Granite.src:
This stone is stubbornly resistant to magic. Whereas other stones absorb the nascent anima, granite refuses. It exists on its own terms, not the whims of magic. As such it is highly prized in construction projects, as it resists most magic and what enchantments do affect it, last much longer.

Legend speaks of a weapon forged from this stone. A great hammer, said to be able to crush almost any armour.

DragonAltar.src:
This strange altar is a creation of dragonkin alchemy, more than it is a place of religious observance. It hums with a faint power, imbued as it is with the energies of Ashenfall. Atop the altar sits a resting place for a challenge horn, a device used to summon a dragon and force them into battle. 

This altar is attuned to General Velgar, a warrior dragon infused with the power of the earth.

RuneEssenceGeyser.src:
This strange material absorbs magical energy, causing it to defy gravity, among other things. It is best known for the creation of runes, powerful little stones that can be used to cast spells. A pickaxe is needed to harvest the essence. 

The floating essence rocks can be knocked out of orbit, with a little effort, making them easier to mine.

ClayVessel.src: This vessel can be sealed to allow for the storage of potions.

Fellhollow.BleakfieldsValley.src: This was the first settlement in Fellhollow. The humans that fled Bramblemead and its cruelty set up the first tents, cabins and early homes here. They would farm, forage and do their best to survive, until gentle Imaru and Xikotal took them in and brought them to Emberwood, where they might found a stronger settlement.

PurifyingWater.src: This water is drawn from a rejuvenation pool and contains within it the spark to fight off the Wither-rot. Although Death keeps these pools active in modern times, a long time ago these pools would have been blessed by Imaru and her magic. She created the water as a way to stave off illness and corruption, in the population she protected.

DirtyWater.src: This water will quench your thirst a little, but it contains a faint residue of a cataclysmic event that afflicted Ashenfall. As a result, there are traces of a tainted substance in the water. Drinking it will damage the soul of anyone who is not native to the area and adapted to it.

Seeds.Irit.src: Thorny irit is a pain to harvest. You must seek out the spiky roots, and the battle with them before you can claim the herbs for yourself. With these seeds you can skip some of that faff and instead grow them wherever you like, the very pinnacle of convenience.

GarouKing.src:
Those who complete the rite of the moon, and usurp their leaders, become the kings of the garou. The title of King is gender neutral, and kings of all genders are recorded across garou history. This is because the mantle of queen has belonged to only two beings, Lougrim and her devourer.

When Lougrim first visited the world of the garou, a place known as Antumnos, she was treated as prey. Her hunters were no match for a goddess, of course, and she assumed the forms of powerful predators, forcing them into submission.

She fell upon the capital of the garou nation, the city of Magrawn, where she called out a challenge to all the reigning kings of the garou clans. They answered the summons and she defeated each of them together in a single, decisive, battle. From then on, she held the mantle of High Queen of the garou.

A title she held until Kuldra devoured her, earning the dragon queen her moniker - God Eater.

FallenHopliteChest.src:
Those who joining the Fellhollow military, who were not from the more noble bloodlines, would join the force known as the hoplites. This force of warrior farmers named themselves after the hoplite forces of Hallow, legendary forces spoken of in some of the Saradominist text.

These hoplites would meet at the end of the week, to train and practice battle manoeuvres. They became walls of impenetrable shields, or terrifying spiked shells, moving with the sort of unity that only comes over years and years of training.

Their secret, so they claimed, was the weekly barbeque. Once training was resolved, if they had performed well enough, the retired members of the hoplites would cook them delicious meats and roasted vegetables, served with an overly generous helping of alcoholic beverages.

FallenHopliteHelm.src:
Those who joining the Fellhollow military, who were not from the more noble bloodlines, would join the force known as the hoplites. This force of warrior farmers named themselves after the hoplite forces of Hallow, legendary forces spoken of in some of the Saradominist text.

They were disciplined in a way that earned them great respect. Each of them acting as the shield for the person next to them and a spear for the enemy in front. They wore armour reflecting some of the style of Hallow, with plateskirts rather than sturdy grieves, allowing for more freedom of movement, a trait they took great advantage of.

FallenHopliteTassets.src:
Those who joining the Fellhollow military, who were not from the more noble bloodlines, would join the force known as the hoplites. This force of warrior farmers named themselves after the hoplite forces of Hallow, legendary forces spoken of in some of the Saradominist text.

When the withering began it was the hoplites that were most affected. Their unity and loyalty became a weakness, as members within their ranks fell to the affliction and then turned on the others. This shattered their synchronicity and spread paranoia and distrust among the ranks.

As their members fell, they would rise as the undead and immediately turn on their brethren, ripping the group apart from the inside.

At least in death they stand together again.

NecromancersCrown.src:
Those who wield the power over life and death have a tendency to crave control. They need to manage things in their life on a pathological level, and this need often grows into a desire to manage the lives of everyone else.

The most well known necromancer in Fellhollow was a man called Calius Waithe. He was one of the Children of Shadows until he decided that their policies of peaceful evil wasn’t what he was looking for. He was more an overtly evil sort of guy.

He decided, on one fateful autumnal eve, to raise an army of the undead and march them on Emberwood. He imagined the village cowering before him as he named himself their new king.

TinRock.src: Tin and copper are the classic double act, combining their essence to make the superior bronze.

Seeds.Harralander.src:
Tired of sinking into swamp-mud in search of these fragrant little herbs? Well now you can grow them yourself.

The fragrance of these herbs is even better without the swamp to dull it, and can be a very pleasant pick-me-up first thing in the day.

RuneLoggingAxe.src: To a tree, a human with a rune logging axe is their final boss. You are the ultimate test; the nemesis that they have been training for. They have been stretching their branches and aggressively photosynthesising for this moment. They have been fantastising about taking you down, so that they can be talked about in groves for centuries. 'The Lumberjack Ripper', they think. 'That's what they will call me.'

AnchovyBait.src: To attract fish with a preference for saltier bait, there’s little better than a nice anchovy strung up and offered as a sacrifice to those that dwell beneath the waves.

RawGiantKrill.src:
To its krill kin, this creature is a beast of epic proportions. The sort of monster of legend that would tower over mountains and shatter towers with a single swipe of its enormous claws.

Here, though, it’s a bit like a big shrimp. Much less intimidating.

DragonMedHelm.src:
To look at the legacy of the dragonkin, you would assume their creations are each of them wonderous. They built mighty cities of shimmering stone, they crafted alchemical horrors that the world fears to this day, and they created dragon armour, one of the mightiest feats of blacksmithing ever known. 

So, you would be forgiven with looking at the dragon medium helm in confusion. 

Oh, yes, there's a strong twinge of nostalgia to it.  Something about its blocky shape reminds you of the good old days, way back when. A simpler time, when everything was cubes and angles, and definition was an alien concept to be utterly abhorred. Yet, in the scintillating radiance of Ashenfall's blooming sunlight, it all just seems a little... square?

Still, it will deflect arrows and swords with great aplomb, and you'll be the envy of all those peasants that didn't get the deluxe edition of the game. So, all in all, you're winning here.

GoblinWarBanner.src:
To most goblins, war is like breathing. Every action a precursor to conflict. Every morning they wake with a focus on picking a fight. They rarely kill one another, it would be counterproductive, but they enjoy finding someone different enough that they can justify a spat.

This is what Bandos engineered them for. When the god arrived on Yu’Biusk, he urged the population into constant conflict. Nations became states, that were ground down into tribes. An entire civilisations reduced to platoons and squadrons.

This cape bears the symbol of Bandos, a weapon known as the kyzaj – a brutal blade designed to eviscerate an opponent.

Once this was a banner, praising the war god, but now it lies forgotten and the other banners defiled to worship a new Big High War God. Velgar, who defeated a god in single combat.

KotPack.src: To say that a Kot Pack is the belongings of a single KotHaar is something of a misrepresentation. You're actually holding the belongings of dozens of KotHaar, stretching back millennia. A KotHaar will carry the obsidian of their ancestors, which was reconstituted from their ancestors before them. The Kot Pack is a lineage, an ancestral record of the creature you killed. It puts things a little into perspective, and I'm sure you will treat it with the respect it deserves.

Ruby.src: To the followers of Zamorak, the ruby was the perfect stone to bedazzle their finery, their weapons, or their very confused pets. The redness of the stone was seen as recognition of their god, and the sparklines of the gemstone was… well, sparkly and pretty, and everyone likes sparkles, even evil wizards.

BeefAndTomatoStew.src: Tomatoes go well with just about everything. They enhance the flavours of anything they’re paired with and a nice beef stew is no exception. The combined flavours are comforting as well as filling, and almost make you forget that you’re a long way from home, on a continent filled with murderous dragons.

YewTree.src:
Towering over the oasis, the yew tree might seem a strange addition to the desert sands, yet it has a deep-rooted place in the lore of the region. 

Unfortunately, the trees are very secretive and delight in upsetting lorehounds, so they won’t share what that secret is. 

Just another excuse to cut them down, really.

SteelArrows.src:
Traditional wisdom says that to kill a zombie, you must destroy the brain. This is disappointingly untrue in Fellhollow, the animating force of Imaru’s hunger needs no thought to drive it forward.

No, a far better plan is to destroy the bones and muscles with sharp metal-tipped spikes launched at the creatures with as much force as you can manage. Steel arrows perform this task very nicely.

SummonShelter.src:
Transforming dirt, stone and nearby twigs and leaves into canvas, this spell has saved many a Wild Knight from a cold night in the rain. A favourite among those engaged in long hunts in the Highlands, it has helped fight in the constant battle against fatigue. 

One Wild Knight, a loner called Ansel, would use this spell to grant him shelter as he wandered round the lands. He would journey to the highest peaks or the deepest crevices, using this spell to grant him a pinch of comfort in the least comfortable of regions. Sadly, it would offer no protection against poison, so when he rested in the Blightblood Swamp, he never awoke again.

WhitePlatelegs.src:
Trapped by a shrine that stood atop a rocky island, surrounded by the hungry dead, Sir Lateef prayed to Saradomin with all his strength. He begged for salvation, for a miracle that might free him, but silence was his only answer.

He barricaded himself atop the monument, the dead scrabbling at his defences, their unholy growling keeping him from even a moment’s sleep.

As time drew on, and hunger and thirst took him, he turned to the symbol of Saradomin in defeated rage. Where was his god? Why was he abandoned? Had he not spent his life in service of the lord of light?

Enraged, he took his sword and cleaved Saradomin’s symbol from its plinth, causing it to crash to the floor. Filled with guilt, he hid the fallen piece from his sight. His last act was one of blasphemy, but perhaps an act justly performed.

StoneAxe.src:
Trees are arrogant creatures, standing tall in the forests and refusing to bow to the wind. For decades they spread their roots claiming dominion over the nearby soil. The claws of beasts are a mere distraction. Raging storms barely rustle their leaves. They refuse to move for anyone, arrogant to the core.

Yet, it is not the wind, nor the heavens that shatter their resolve. Indeed, it is the lowliest of stones, refined to an edge. No matter how old the tree, how sturdy its fame, a single stone, the size of your fist, can bring the mightiest ash low.  

The stone axe is an alliance of such a rock, working together with branches cast aside in the tree’s hubris. Proof that even the lowliest of us can make a difference.

Peach.src:
Try not to think too hard about the nature of transmutation as you consume this fruit. It's sweet, juicy and the pseudo-necromantic origins only make it a little disturbing. Oh, sure, it tastes nice and it goes surprisingly well in a crumble, but it's a little disturbing when you get that unexpected crunch. 

Best not to think about it. Ignorance is bliss.

Limestone.src:
Turn your limestone this way and that and you might spot a fossil. Lesser blue dragons have been in the region for some time, and there were the experiments that led to them. Being experiments, they weren't cognitively blessed, so it's entirely possible that you'll find the talon of a dragon that got trapped in a rockfall.

You could also find the odd chicken wing from the Second Age. The Children of Shadows loved a shake and bake.

WillowLongbow.src:
Ulv had many skills, but hunting was his strongest. He was inherently quiet, still as the night, and he could hold his position, in the trees or bushes, for hours at a time. Ravanna was never good at this. When the two of them hunted together, Ravanna would sneeze, cough or scream at the sight of an unexpected insect, and the two of them would watch their quarry disappear off into the night.

Although this would occasionally test their friendship, Ulv never really held it against Ravanna. Instead he continued attempting to teach the necromancer the ways of the forest, and the techniques the Wild Knights would use to track down game. It never took. Try as she might, Ravanna was never going to be silent as a shadow.

In apology, she looked for a way to create a weapon that would reduce the impact of her noisy nature. Longbows fired further and faster, meaning that less stealth was needed. She made her way into Fellhollow in search of a material strong enough, and returned with willow branches that she crafted into a longbow as a gift for her friend.

Their hunts improved dramatically afterward. That was, until they became the hunted.

UlvsLongbow.src:
Ulv was always the silent hunter, in more ways than one. While it was true that no word ever left his lips, his footsteps, breath and, most importantly, his arrows were all equally devoid of sound. The Wild Knights would jokingly call him the Silent Killer – though over time, the crueller among them called him Silent But Deadly – knowing he lacked the ability to argue back. The boy took these insults with quiet grace, never biting back, never reacting. He was used to such small cruelties, having faced them all his life. 

He had carved the bow himself and once walked Ravanna through the process. The two of them had as true a friendship as could ever be hoped for. No lingering romantic tensions. No transaction or debt. No honour chained them together. They were friends simply because they were. Because two lonely people had found each other and a comfort in the other's eccentricities. The wolf and the bat, platonic soulmates to the end. 

For one of his birthdays, Ravanna enchanted the bow with a simple spell. She took animal bones, skulls and hides and wove necromantic magic through them, wrapping them around the limb and grip of the bow, imbuing them with just enough of the Underworld to strip them of their sound and a little of their substance. Like ghosts, the arrows would sail silently through the air, dropping targets that never knew what hit them. 

It would have been the perfect birthday gift. If only Ulv had lived long enough to receive it. 

The garou can be brutal in their assaults, considering notions like mercy to be the domain of the weak and cowardly. Ulv was simply in the wrong place at the wrong time. He was ambushed by a patrol of young garou looking for the bloodmark that would grant them adulthood. There were six of them; Ulv reduced their number to four before claws tore his throat, silencing him forever. 

When Ravanna found his body, she went mad. An anger unlike any other, a rage more powerful than any storm, waged a war of light and the dark inside her. The darkness won. Using the souls of the slain garou, Ravanna's necromantic curse tore through the Highlands, twisting the clouds into screaming things filled with a mere sliver of her rage. As the ghosts of the dead garou crashed about within them, the clouds unleashed lightning and thunder upon the populace below, destroying countless settlements in an instant and countless more over the centuries that followed.

Attack.src:
Unfortunately, conflict is inevitable on Ashenfall. You will need to hit things with clubs, stab them with daggers and impale your foes with a volley of carefully crafted arrows.

There are three main combat styles, magic, ranged and melee, each one has its strengths and its weaknesses.

Magic attacks are capable of generating powerful side effects, air magic can knock something back, fire magic can burn your enemies to a crisp. However, you will need a steady supply of runes to keep casting spells.

Ranged attacks can snipe enemies from afar, but you’ll need to make sure you don’t run out of arrows.

Melee attacks get up close and personal, but you won’t need to worry about ammunition to lay the smackdown on that uppity little goblin – not Zanik – who’s been giving you lip.

When engaged in battle, keep an eye on your stamina, as each attack will cost you some of it. As you level up your combat skills, you’ll be able to deal longer combo chains to more efficiently use your stamina.

SuperLumberjackPotion.src:
Unfortunately, the lumberjack potion won't garb you in a checkered flannel shirt and a moustache. Apothecaries are still working on that one.

Instead, the lumberjack potion will fill you with energy and enthusiasm for woodcutting. You're a chopping machine.

Seeds.Snapdragon.src:
Unfortunately, these seeds do not grow adorable little scaly nightmares to terrorise your enemies.

Fortunately, they do grow into useful little medicinal herbs with various uses in herblore. So, an alright trade off, even if the tiny dragons would be better.

Seeds.Tomato.src: Unlock the plant that causes the most arguments amongst the truly bored, the humble tomato. Is it a fruit? A vegetable? A plague on sandwiches everywhere? Well, now you can start these arguments wherever you like, by planting one of these beauties in a fresh farming patch.

GrilledTrout.src:
Until recently, grilled trout was prescribed by doctors for its regenerative properties. "A grilled trout a day will keep the gout away" was the common phrase. However, a study commissioned by the Cooks' Guild in far-off Varrock found that regular imbibers of grilled trout were 20% more likely to contract gout.

Don't let that stop you enjoying the bitter notes of trout. The Cooks' Guild also did a study that found that 75% of gout-inflicted people thought it was totally worth it.

WeaponPoison.src:
Used in crafting Poison Arrows or to coat your equipped Melee Weapon with Poison for a short time.

There are times in life where you really want someone to regret ever meeting you. It could be a long-held grudge, it could be on the battlefield, or it could be in a never-ending meeting that could so easily have been an email but has now persisted past your lunchbreak and you had so been looking forward to that sushi… ahem… sorry, where was I? Oh, yes, pain!

Poison is sometimes considered to be a coward’s weapon. Personally, I prefer to think of it as the smart weapon choice, after all, honour is only worth anything if you’re the winner of the battle.
