You might be mistaken in thinking that an agility potion will make you an overnight athlete. The potion is still working with the body you have: there are no dramatic physiological changes. For physiological changes, you might want a trip to Dr Fenkenstrain.

An elder gentleman with dodgy hips will shuffle faster - and will likely experience incredible pain as they do so - but won't be able to perform backflips.

RuniteOre.src:
You might be surprised to hear that runite, as an ore, is soft. Like gold it is easily marked. Thank our ancestors that they didn't immediately toss the ore into a bin, though. They tinkered with alloys, working with luminite ore in the combustion process to create something remarkable.

You can see why they persisted. Runite ore has some funky properties - repelling materials, occasionally floating, spinning when you sing to it - that makes it an ore with clear potential.

KalphiteShellFragments.src: You might get some looks, but make sure you pocket the little scraps of kalphite that you find. These little exoskeleton offcuts may not be much on their own, but grab some acrid adhesive and you can glue them together to make kalphite shells. Where you go after that is up to you. We recommend magic carpet battles, tossing shells at each other as you race.

DesertCloth.src:
You might think that any cloth found in the desert could be called desert cloth, but you’d just be arguing semantics and that won’t win you many friends at parties. No, the desert cloth we refer to here is the sort of thing woven from desert weed and cacti fibres. It is forged of the desert, not simply found within it.

That said, explaining this at parties probably still won’t make you many friends.

RuneArrows.src:
You might think that rune is the last metal you would use for an arrow. Rune is a magical metal, and it has diamagnetic properties (meaning that it repels other metals, sometimes with force). You don't want to be aiming at a garou berserker, only to watch the arrow arc away from them.

As Vannaka would say, 'your problem is that you're thinking like an amateur'. Archers don't actually WANT arrows to hit other metals: they want to slip into the gaps between armour, puncturing an armpit or neck. The best archers also love a trick-shot, hitting an opponent through a sea of allies. The trick is to use the diamagnetism to your benefit, and that - again, to quote Vannaka - 'comes from the hardest skill of all. Practice'.

RuneWateringCan.src: You might wonder 'how can a watering can made of rune metal be different from any other watering can'? Well, that is a VERY good question, one which we have a cracking answer to. Honestly, it makes so much sense when you hear it.

StandardFishingPotion.src:
You often hear stories about great anglers who have that one marine animal they've never caught. A whale perhaps, or a darting salmon. Well, I had a friend once who had an enmity with a prawn. It was a big prawn, mind you, and every time he caught it, it would leap out of his net and get away. He accused that pawn of gloating: he believed it waited until he hauled in the net before scarpering.

It got to the point where my friend traded his week's wages for a fishing potion. Not a lesser or weak fishing potion: a third-tier, freshly made fishing potion. He was going to catch that prawn, even if he had to starve for days. 

But the potion didn't make him any better at catching the prawn. Instead, he became attuned to the prawn. He was so aware that he knew what it was thinking. Now, every time the prawn escapes, my friend can hear it cackle and let out a little "doofus!".

SergeantBlister.src:
You wanna know why they call me Blister? 'Course you do. You'd do well to listen up.

People love to gripe and fight in 'ere. Lotsa madness, lotsa grievances – it's gonna 'appen. But they know not to fight wiv'out Blister. I get called tout suite.

I'm the one who handles the bets. You wanna make some extra dirt from a fight? You come to me. I give fair odds.

Why Blister? I'm the one who grows fat an' happy from all the friction in this place. Like a blister on your foot, ain't it?

GreenDragonHatchlings.src:
You would be forgiven for uttering the words “cute” at the sight of one of these baby dragons - a sentiment that lasts for the few picoseconds before they attempt to eat your face. Make no mistake, these are Kuldra’s broodlings, and they are filled with as much rage and hatred as she is. From the moment they hatch, these dragons are instilled with a violent need to destroy any that might breach Kuldra’s lair.

They may be cute, but you should cast aside that word in favour of a much better hyphenated one: self-preservation.

LuminiteOre.src: You'd struggle to find a better catalyst than luminite ore. If it was a person it would be the life of the party, the guest who dances on the table, gets everyone enjoying themselves, and then promptly passes out upstairs. It burns brightly but briefly, enabling other ores - like runite - to realise their potential.

ArtisanSkillcapeTrimmed.src: You're a Master Maker, a Crafting Connoisseur, an Artisan Fartisan.

FishingSkillcapeTrimmed.src: You're a fishing colossus, conquering rivers and seas with nowt but your net and rod.

InspiringRingOfAgility.AthleteRing.src:
You've likely seen a garou in attack pose, holding its ground, but have you seen a garou in full pursuit? They can drop low, almost quadrupedal, and cover an incredible amount of ground.

The Inspiring Ring of Agility contains magic that reshapes the arms and legs to resemble the physiology of the garou. That terrifying prospect is as painful as it sounds, but it does mean that you can approximate their speed and guile.

Fuzan.src:
Youngest of Kuldra’s brood, Fuzan grew up spoilt and childish. Where other dragons sought strategy, family, or some loftier goal, Fuzan only cared about the next dopamine hit brought on my mindless destruction. We’ve all known kids like that.

As he grew older, he began to seek experiences in more dangerous places. He picked fights with other dragons. Bullied the monsters roaming the lands. He brought chaos everywhere he went, in the hopes that it might mildly alleviate some of his boredom.

In the heart of a volcano, as he gazed into the purest fires, he found something other than amusement to cling onto.

He found faith.

Faith in a being not of this world: born of celestial fire so bright that it made Fuzan’s own mighty flames seem like mere candlelight in comparison. This being spoke through flames. Her words were flickering embers. Her laughter the crackle of flames. Her platitudes swirled in the air, carried aloft by ashes.

She claimed to be a god, and she promised him that Fuzan would burn hotter, shine brighter, and ignite the world under his own light—rather then spend his life in his mother’s shadow. It was an offer too enticing to refuse.

Under her tutelage, Fuzan learned to better wield his own flames and the flames of others. He seized control of the gentle KotHaar and he began marking the garou, igniting their souls as kindling and taking their strength for his own.

It is better that he is dead. For everyone’s sake.

Sapphire.src:
Your eyes are like sapphires, sparkling in the night
Every syllable you utter creates pure delight
A day in your company is infinitely bright
Will you be my valentine tonight?

A poem by a lovestruck Bramblemead youth. It was not successful.

Aside from their use in terrible teenage poetry, Sapphires are a vital component in jewellery crafting. They can be found hidden among the metal ores around Ghornfell, or hidden in the various chests left behind by the old kingdom.

YewCrossbow.src:
You’ll be pleased to learn, dear adventurer, that the first person to make this crossbow in Ashenfall is, indeed, you… or your friend if there are a few of you around.

The techniques that create them are no different to the previous crossbows, but the wood is sturdier, stronger and capable of sufficiently more damage when wielded with skill.

The Moon Garou are traditionalists, preferring the art of archery in hunting and combat, so why not take this opportunity to show them how much they’re missing out.

ZamorakCape.src:
Zamorak never came to Dowdun Reach. Its gates were never graced by the Mahjarrat. No general came, or ambassador from the mainland. Even the ZMI failed to send an offshoot to the keep. 

How was that possible? Chaos taught them that by the simple laws of averages a high-ranking Zamorakian should have stumbled onto their shores. Ashenfall and Dowdun Reach were too much of an opportunity. Surely, greed would lead a Zamorakian highborn here. 

The silence was deafening. Everyone who lived or worked in the keep knew what this meant: Zamorak had forbid his inner circle from visiting Ashenfall, likely at pain of death. How else could Dowdun Reach have been left alone for so long?

But why? Why did Zamorak keep Ashenfall at arm's length? The answers differed, depending on the zeal of the follower. Zamorak feared something on Ashenfall. Zamorak knew that something made it worthless. Zamorak was already here, just without Dowdun's knowing. Zamorak is in all of us.

Remarkably, the mystery only strengthened the faith of the Dowdun Zamorakians. By being so contemptible to Zamorak, they were utterly important. They were main characters in Zamorak's performance. 

It suggests another reason why Zamorak might have left Ashenfall alone. Perhaps he wanted to show that nothing – not even his disdain – would soften his people's devotion.

ui.loading.body3.src:
During the Third Age, Gielinor became the battleground for a conflict between the gods. Mighty armies battled one another for control over powerful artefacts, such as the Stone of Jas and the God Sword – a weapon rumoured to be powerful enough to kill a god. 

The God Wars ended when the God of Chaos, Zamorak, used the Stone to set off a destructive blast that wiped the region of Forinthry from the map – creating what is now referred to as The Wilderness.

ui.loading.body4.src:
It is unknown why the people of Gielinor crave these paper hats, yet people have been murdered over them. There are no smiths, nor artisans of the modern age that seem to be able to recreate these designs, deceptively simple as they are. 

To this day, Santa regrets simply giving them away. If he'd just kept a handful, he might not be struggling to deal with his elves demand for a payrise.

ui.loading.body1.src:
The history of Gielinor is split into different ages, each representing a major event. Such as the  Third Age, the age of the God Wars. 

The Sixth Age was created with the death of Guthix, the god of balance and harmony. This age has seen a new conflict between the gods that led to them being banished from Gielinor by the World Guardian.

ui.loading.body2.src:
The legendary hero Dioynsius is a tale whispered to dwarven children about overcoming great evil. Wall carvings by a forgotten mountain tribe show him battling monsters and returning triumphant. 

Yet bank tellers talk of him in hushed, frightened, whispers ever since he went on a little killing spree. Never underestimate the lure of a Party Hat.

MessageInABottle_Everyone_Remembered.src: <The lost, the dead and the once forgotten, are finally laid to rest. A gentle peace washes over you and you are left with a gift from the dead.>

MessageInABottle_Warren_Remembered.src: <The wind smells briefly of grass and soil. A contented feeling fills your heart>

MessageInABottle_Finn_Remembered.src: <You hear the sound of children playing and a woman laughing with them>

MessageInABottle_Lazina_Remembered.src: <You hear the sound of laughter and the clash of blade against blade. You cannot help but smile>

MessageInABottle_Kay_Remembered.src: <You smell sausages, bacon and the sizzling of eggs on the pan. Your stomach rumbles in response>

MessageInABottle_GhostClue_Windmill.src: Blades that once whirled like a tornado, now lay still among crumbled stone. Find the lost who dwells there, set her free.

MessageInABottle_GhostClue_Swamp.src: Choking on swamp gas. Ruined timber, mouldy and splintered. Sinking moment by moment into bitter, bleak, mud. Find the name of the buried, set them free.

MessageInABottle_WindmillGhost_3.src: Dead within moments. Barely a day in this land. I never did have the best luck.

Objective_LayGhostsToRest.src: Find the restless spirits and help lay them to rest. They only appear at night.

MessageInABottle_CaveGhost_3.src: He knew of this place, that dragon. Poked his great scaley head through the entrance and grinned at me as he slowly drew in a breath. I watched my life unfold before me, until the poison put it all to an end. I wish I'd found that shield.

MessageInABottle_SwampGhost_3.src: Hurtling through the air, knowing everything was over. All I could think about was how I'd missed breakfast. Most important meal of the day, and I forgot it on my last one.

MessageInABottle_FarmGhost_3.src: I came to rebuild a farmstead. Now I'll serve as nothing but compost. Gran would be so upset with me.

MessageInABottle_FarmGhost_1.src: I never liked goblins, even though Zanik said they deserved our pity, more than hate.

MessageInABottle_CaveGhost_1.src: I thought I might be safe here, hidden away from the skies. As the dragon circled over me, I thought "maybe I'll be OK".

MessageInABottle_SwampGhost_2.src: I tried to row out by the lake near the temple, when that dragon whacked me with his tail. What had I ever done to him?

MessageInABottle_SwampGhost_1.src: I'm impressed it got this far, really, this boat. Because I never sailed it here.

QuestDescription.src: Lay to rest the spirits of the lost expedition members.

MessageInABottle_GhostClue_Cave.src: My brother lies buried in darkness, beneath a southern point rising high in the sky. Find his name, set him free.

MessageInABottle_SwampGhost_4.src: Names Kay, adventurer. Remember me, won't you? Give me a proper goodbye.

MessageInABottle_GhostClue_Memorial.src: Names to be remembered. Prayers for the dead. Whisper our memories at the place by the temple, so that we might finally rest.

MessageInABottle_GhostClue_Farm.src: Once it was homes, standing together. Now, nothing but ruins, falling apart. The last surviving memories trampled beneath angry hooves. Find the name of the forgotten, set him free.

MessageInABottle_FarmGhost_4.src: Remember me, adventurer. Help my spirit rest. Warren was my name, don't let it be forgotten.

MessageInABottle_WindmillGhost_4.src: Remember me, adventurer. I was Lazina, blade for hire and swordmaster supreme. Say a prayer for me, so that the gods will look on me fondly.

MessageInABottle_CaveGhost_4.src: Remember me, adventurer. Say a farewell to Finn, won't you? Tell ma I'm sorry, and tell my stepda he's an arse.

Objective_FindUseForAmulet.src: Search for a purpose for the Amulet of Ghostspeak.

MessageInABottle_FarmGhost_2.src: She was wrong, of course. They killed me. So I should hate them.

MoreGhostsLeft.src: The dead do not yet feel fully at peace. There may be more out that need help moving on.

Altar_All_Remembered.src: The lost, the dead and the once forgotten, are finally laid to rest. A gentle peace washes over you and you are left with a gift from the dead.

WellFoundAmulet.src: The well contains cold, stagnant water.

Altar_Warren_Remembered.src: The wind smells briefly of grass and soil. A contented feeling fills your heart.

MessageInABottle_WindmillGhost_2.src: Then a great bloody dragon messed everything up.

AltarDescription.src: This shrine is a place where the dead are remembered. So that they may move on to the afterlife they deserve.

MessageInABottle_WindmillGhost_1.src: Well this didn't work out for me, did it? I made this great stupid journey, leaving Al Kharid behind, because adventure awaited me. Glory and fame.

NotEnoughInventory.src: You do not have the space to receive your reward. You will need to make room in your backpack.

Altar_Finn_Remembered.src: You hear the sound of children playing and a woman laughing with them.

Altar_Lazina_Remembered.src: You hear the sound of laughter and the clash of blade against blade. You cannot help but smile.

WellNotFoundAmulet.src: You see something glinting in the bucket. Reaching into the cold water, you pull out a strange looking amulet that's even colder to the touch.

Altar_Kay_Remembered.src: You smell sausages, bacon and the sizzling of eggs on the pan. Your stomach rumbles in response.

Amulet_ExtraHint.src: [You'll need to find some way to understand what they're saying.]

Terrorbird.Default.Description.src: A bound nature spirit. Summon it to carry you across the lands, much faster than you could manage were you to rely on your own bandy, little, legs.

Red.2.Description.src: A breed created by a Zamorakian priest who found them far less terrifying than he had hoped. Instead of bringing fear to the masses, these terrorbirds would whimper and sob whenever forced to do any manual labour. He named the breed “crybaby” in frustration, though it remains disappointingly apt.

Carpet.Default.Description.src: A carpet, woven from enchanted thread. Summon it to carry you across the desert. Unlike terrorbirds, the carpet will glide smoothly across the desert, showing you a whole new world of sandy sights.

Blue.5.Description.src: A fancy name for these blue birds. They actually have never been near the mountains and they, like all terrorbirds, cannot fly.

Green.1.Description.src: A green-feathered variant of the terrorbird, popular with the Wild Knights back in the earliest days of Bramblemead. They would raise the raptor from the moment they hatched, so that the bird would imprint on the knight and create a bond of loyalty unlike any other.

Grey.3.Description.src: A quiet and gentle breed of terrorbird, the Starlit Whisperer is happy to just stay silently by your side.

Green.3.Description.src:
Bramblemead farmers named this breed of terrorbird after the horrifying sound it made at any given opportunity. Lunchtime? Screech! Danger? Screech? The day ends with a y? Long, piercing,  screech.

They were not a popular breed with the neighbours.

Purple.1.Description.src: Despite their sinister name, the Shadowsoul Talons are some of the most gentle and friendly breeds of terrorbird. They were given such a frightful name by their keeper, who was desperately trying to sell them on to the Black Knights of Dowdun Reach and figured scarier names might make more money.

Green.2.Description.src: Druids in Brynmoor would rear these birds not as mounts, but as guard dogs for their sacred sites. The terrorbirds were raised to be quick, silent and merciless in their defence of the groves.

ConsumableItem.Description.src: Grants access to a visual mount variant

Purple.5.Description.src: In the second age, the time of the Zarosian Empire, these terrorbirds were bred for nocturnal patrols. Their dark vision was excellent, and they were skilled trackers, and so proved popular with the Inquistion, as they hunted down the heretics.

Yellow.3.Description.src: Legend says that this breed of terrorbird appears only during a solar eclipse. They are said to possess magical powers; the exact nature of which varies with each telling. In truth, they can hatch just like any terrorbird does and possess no know metaphysical capabilities.

Carpet.Default.Teal.Description.src: Legend tells us that this carpet is woven from silk spun by the moon sprites of the Umbral Sands. It is said that they create those silken threads only on clear nights when the moon is full and the stars look down and give them permission. These rare carpets, therefore, only appear in times of great peace and tranquility. Traits that the Umbral Sands have not seen for some time.

Carpet.Default.Purple.Description.src: Made by crushing up the red vines around the desert, this rug is considered an omen of bad luck in certain households. The red colouring reminds people of the scorching effect of the sun, and the many friends they have lost to its cruel influence. Counter-intuitively, perhaps, the red colouring is also supposed to ward off danger, for the same reasons as some consider it bad luck. To that end many choose to hang this rug on the outside of their homes, to scare away any beasts that might seek to do them harm.

Yellow.1.Description.src: Named after the stars, rather than the runes, the Astralback Warblier is a strange beast. On nights where the sky is clear and the moon absent, this breed of terrorbird loves  nothing more than to raise its head to the heavens and warble strangely haunting melodies.

Red.5.Description.src: Popular with the Black Knights of Dowdun Reach due to the darkand sinister colour schemes. Many of the knights would ride into battle atop these creatures, screaming about the power of chaos as they went.

Yellow.5.Description.src: Raised along the beaches and coastal regions, the Sunbeak is a colourful terrorbird variant who enjoys a more fish heavy diet then most.

Blue.3.Description.src: Raised in colder regions, this breed of terrorbird was popular for its speed. Regular races would be held with various different terrorbirds, but the Rimekept Racer would almost always come first.

Grey.4.Description.src: Raised in the rockiest parts of Ashenfall, the Ashbelly Mountainclimber is no stranger to heights. They will happily walk up any incline, and stare down from even the tallest cliffs.

Purple.4.Description.src: Raised near the coasts of Ashenfall, this breed of terrorbird is prone to wanderlust. They will often go missing, only to be found a day or two later just aimlessly wandering along the beaches.

Carpet.Default.Blue.Description.src: Rare is it that the people of Manafem brave the dunes. The harsh light of day makes travel dangerous and at night there is the constant threat of their “great protector”, Fuzan, always happy for a meal delivered. So it was that they wove a carpet in the gentle blues of the night, so that they might blend in more easily with the midnight sands.

Purple.2.Description.src: So named because of the tuft if feathers on the top of the terrorbird’s head. A shade of deep blue, with hints of purple, creates an impression of mysterious midnight magic, or so the breeder claimed.

Grey.2.Description.src: Something is wrong with these creatures, they are gripped by some preternatural terror that causes them to scream incoherently for no reason. They are silent much of the time, but once in a blue moon, they will emit a sound so horrifying that it will chill you to your core.

Green.4.Description.src: The Springdown Runner was bred for the races. It was  quick, focused and not easily distracted by the various tricks of the watching crowd. While nowadays there’s less of that racing instinct, this breed of terrorbird still enjoys a good run around.

Terrorbird.Description.src: The nature spirits of Ashenfall serve a purpose, one denied to them by the encroaching Wither. It may seem counterintuitive to have to slay these spirits in order to bind them, but that's what nature is. It's hunt and be hunted. Kill and be killed, life in a perpetual cycle -- everything chained together.

Purple.3.Description.src: These are not the brightest of terrorbirds and they are named because they spend their days munching on leaves and blades of grass. This is unfortunate, as this particular breed have a carnivorous diet, so they spend a lot of their time being violently ill.

Yellow.2.Description.src: These bright yellow creatures love nothing more than ferreting out strange green herbs with their sharp claws. They enjoy running around plains, making screeching noises.

Grey.5.Description.src: These creatures enjoy little more than flitting about in campire smoke. Perhaps it’s because it’s the closest they will ever come to dancing in the clouds, yet, still, they dream.

Grey.1.Description.src: These terrorbirds like to hang out near volcanic areas. They enjoy the ash in their feathers, as they think it makes them look more attractive. The smouldering in their name comes not from any sort of flame, but from the disturbing looks they give their handlers when they’re trying to seem cool.

Red.4.Description.src: This breed is so named because the breeder’s daughter thought they were sunburned when she first saw the chicks. Bright pink and screeching, she immediately put them in buckets of water, only to face the wrath of their mother.

Blue.1.Description.src: This breed of terrorbird has an overly inflated sense of self-worth. They will barge to the front of any queue and will stamp over anything in their way.

Red.1.Description.src: This breed of terrorbird was the bane of most normal human residents. They would raid farms, culling livestock and devouring grain. They would storm through settlements, smashing to pieces anything within their reach. Only the Black Knights of Dowdun Reach had any success in training them, and only such madmen would even try to.

Red.3.Description.src: This brightly coloured breed of terrorbird gets its name from the apple orchards where the breed was first reared. The owner of the orchard had little imagination for colour combinations, so when he saw red and green together the only thing that came to mind were the apples right in front of him. This is in no way similar to the naming process used by narrative designers.

Yellow.4.Description.src: This friendly breed of terrorbird is so named because they wag their tails in the presence of their handlers. They delight in playful displays of affection, such as jumping up and down, or attempting to chew someone’s face off. Oh, how sweet.

Carpet.Default.Orange.Description.src:
This light umber tone is handcrafted by Uzzer children as part of their daily lessons. The youngsters gather round and work together to weave the complicated pattern throughout the tapestry as a means of teaching them patience as well as some useful life skills.

If you look very carefully, you can see where the garou cubs have found clever ways to sneakily weave in swear words, personal symbols and odd little doodles to amuse themselves. This way, each of the carpets is unique, if not entirely  desirable.

Green.5.Description.src: While many terrorbirds were bred for speed, the Mossbeak Hunter was bred to pursue. Wild Knight swould raise them to chase down dangerous prey, tiring their quarry out from the terrorbird’s almost limitless stamina.

Blue.4.Description.src: With electric yellow feathers along the wings and the back, this breed of terrorbird always stands out from the crowd. Perhaps this is why they are all naturally so shy. They got their name because they would always try and hide from their owners, lurking in all the dark places so that they might not be seen.

Blue.2.Description.src: With feathers of glacial blue, these terrorbirds were once prized as fashionable mounts of the rich and powerful. Unfortunately, however, they took a disturbing liking to the famous, leading to the second half of their name.

Warning.CannotEquip.src: You have not unlocked this type of mount yet

NarrativeIntroTextPart1.src: Dragons, always trouble, and Ashenfall has more than its share.

NarrativeIntroTextPart5.src: Get ready, hero! We're all counting on you.

NarrativeIntroTextPart4.src: So we called the best - yes, that's you - to hunt them down and end their threat.

NarrativeIntroTextPart3.src: The dragons didn't like that, not one little bit.

NarrativeIntroTextPart2.src: When the continent was suddenly discovered, explorers poured in to claim its secrets.

Zanik.FoundPutrilius.1.src: A cthonian demon... trapped in a chicken? Well that must be embarrassing. Still, you've got them to promise to reign in their infection and that means I can work on a cure.

Zanik.GatheredIngredients.2.src: Brilliant. Right, let's take a look at what we have here... hrmm... there's a lot of magical energy here, a bit like the dragonkin effigies we've seen...

Quest.Objective.3.src: Bring Zanik the ingredients: Dragon Blood, a Twilight Lily and some Unholy Water.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseWhat.4.src: But I had an idea. Where the rest of my kind went big, I went small... very, very small. Unbound as my kind are by your rather rigid notions of biology, I was able to split myself into little forms and crawled off to find my fortune.

Putrilius.PostQest.HasSamples.1.src: Bwaa... Oh, it's you. I don't need to do the clucky thing. Oh, you've got some essence on you? Here, let me take it off your hands. Here you go.

Putrilius.PostQest.NotGotSamples.1.src: Bwaa.. Oh, it's you. I don't need to do the clucky thing. What do you want? I've already agreed I'll do what I can to quell the infection.

Zanik.NotGatheredIngredients.Choices.Cho.src: Don't tell me you haven't seen the dragons roaming about? The blood of a dragon helps add strength to the solution. Unfortunately, you're going to need to kill one to get it.

Zanik.Has10Samples.src: Fantastic! You've got enough there for me to study. I'm going to need a few more things, though, before I can learn anything from them. If you're still willing to help.

Zanik.SpokenTo.Has10Samples.1.src: Fantastic! You've got enough there for me to study. I'm going to need a few more things, though, before I can learn anything from them. If you're still willing to help.

Quest.Objective.4.src: Find the source of the cthonian infection, somewhere high up in Dowdun Reach.

Zanik.NotGatheredIngredients.2.src: First, I'm going to need some dragon blood. You can get it from any dragon you find. Though, I'm sure they won't be willing to surrender it without a fight.

Zanik.SpokenTo.Has10Samples.2.src: First, I'm going to need some dragon blood. You can get it from any dragon you find. Though, I'm sure they won't be willing to surrender it without a fight.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseCause.6.src: Frustratingly, I am largely unable to regain control of the other bits of me, and now I am constrained to this feathered monstrosity.

Quest.Objective.1.src: Gather 10 biological samples from strange ravens in Dowdun Reach, and bring them to Zanik.

Player.PostQuest.Choice.GotAnyEggs.src: Got any eggs I can have?

Zanik.PostQuest.2.src: Hopefully, we can keep that demonic corruption contained in Dowdun Reach...

Putrilius.InBeat5.SourceOfCorruption.2.src: I am Putrilius. Once one of the last remaining cthonian demons who were the rightful rulers of Infernus, before it all went so very wrong.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseWho.1.src: I am Putriulius, grand-sub-sub-clerk of the great office of numerical records... which is to say that in the cthonian hierarchy, I was no one.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseWhat.1.src: I am a cthonian demon. Once we were the rulers of Infernus. It was an existence of complex contracts and even more complicated culinary practices.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseCause.3.src: I could nudge, but couldn't control, so I lived quite happily as a spectator. Watching life from the safety of someone else's skull. That was until that big stone got smashed.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseCause.2.src: I had made myself small and split myself into hundreds of little versions of myself, nestling inside what passes for a brain in avernic demons, later spreading to some humans.

Zanik.NotGatheredIngredients.1.src: I need you to get me some reagents so I can study this corruption.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseWhat.5.src: I nestled inside what you would call the physical forms of the avernics, and survived the great purge as a spectator, rather than a player. I lived, they died, so I call it a good plan.

Zanik.NotSpokenTo.StartedQuest.3.src: I see you've already found the weird ravens and I'm sure you can see how weird they are right now.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseWho.2.src: I was small, quiet and easily forgotten, which goes a long way to explain why I wasn't eaten. I lived my life the blandest way imaginable, but I was happy in my own little way.

Putrilius.InBeat5.EndCorruption.1.src: I would love to, honestly, I would. I got quite used to a life as little more than an observer, tagging along with the lesser demons.

Putrilius.InBeat5.SourceOfCorruption.1.src: I would say I am part of this madness, yes, though I do not exactly claim credit for it. It was that... thing... that Dreaming Stone's mind that sent this wildly out of control.

Zanik.NotGatheredIngredients.Choices.src: I'm going to need some Dragon Blood, Unholy Water and the leaves of a Twilight Lily.

Zanik.GatheredIngredients.5.src: If we can find that central intelligence, it would help in finding a cure down the line. Since ravens were most infected, maybe look for somewhere they frequent? Somewhere high up?

Zanik.NotFoundPutrilius.src: If we can find that central intelligence, it would help in finding a cure down the line. Since ravens were most infected, maybe look for somewhere they frequent? Somewhere high up?

Putrilius.PostQest.NotGotSamples.2.src: If you bring me more of that essence you've found in the ravens, I'll give you some infernal fragments for every ten essence you bring me.

Zanik.NotSpokenTo.4.src: If you can gather samples from, say... ten of them, I can maybe get a sense of what's been causing their strange behaviour. It might help me get to the bottom of the insanity in the keep.

Zanik.LessThan10Samples.src: If you can gather ten samples from them, I can study them to see if I can unlock any clues as to the nature of the madness infecting in Dowdun Reach.

Zanik.NotSpokenTo.LessThan10Samples.src: If you can get ten samples, I can study them to see if I can unlock any clues as to the nature of the madness infection in Dowdun Reach.

Putrilius.PostQest.HasSamples.HasSpace.src: If you find any more, I'll be happy to take it off your hands.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseEgg.2.src: If you were in my position, you would have gone mad long, long ago.

Quest.Description.src: Investigate the strange corruption afflicting the residents of Dowdun Reach.

Putrilius.InBeat5.EndCorruption.2.src: It was entertaining and I never needed to worry about being eaten by my fellow cthonians. But, unfortunately, the only part of me I can actually affect is.. well... this bit, in the chicken.

Zanik.FoundPutrilius.2.src: It'll take a while though, years probably, but we might see this place recover over time. Thanks for all your help. Here, something to thank you for your effort.

Putrilius.InBeat5.NotSure.1.src: It's a surprisingly complicated language considering the source... oh... err... I mean, bwakbwak bwaaaak?

Zanik.FoundPutrilius.3.src: It's not much, but it's very fashionable in these parts.

Zanik.NotSpokenTo.2.src: It's quieter here too, gives me time to think and look into stuff. This whole place, it's riddled with some sort of infection, or corruption, both magical and... well... more.

Zanik.NotSpokenTo.StartedQuest.2.src: It's quieter here too, gives me time to think and look into stuff. This whole place, it's riddled with some sort of infection, or corruption, both magical and... well... more.

Zanik.NotGatheredIngredients.4.src: Lastly, I'm going to need some unholy water... It's like holy water, only from Zamorak worshippers. There's probably a fountain somewhere near the cathedral that has some.

Zanik.SpokenTo.Has10Samples.4.src: Lastly, I'm going to need some unholy water... It's like holy water, only from Zamorak worshippers. There's probably a fountain somewhere near the cathedral that has some.

Putrilius.InBeat5.EndCorruption.4.src: Look, tell you what. That essence you've been collecting, if you find any more of it, bring it back here. For every ten essence, I'll exchange you some of these infernal fragments. Fair deal, no?

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseCause.1.src: Must you call it an infection? You make me sound like a common cold!

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseEgg.1.src: My existence is just a joke to you, isn't it? Can you imagine what it is like for a being that has watched the rise and fall of civilisations... to be bound in such a feathery prison?

Putrilius.InBeat5.AreYouDemon.1.src: No, very clearly, I am a chicken... err, I mean... bwak bwak, cockadoodlesomethingorother.

Putrilius.PostQest.HasSamples.HasNoSpace.src: Oh, but you're somewhat overburdened. Best come back when you've got some space free.

Zanik.NotSpokenTo.1.src: Oh, hey, don't mind the cell, it's oddly comforting. I've been on the surface so long, I'd almost forgotten what it's like under the ground.

Zanik.NotSpokenTo.StartedQuest.1.src: Oh, hey, don't mind the cell, it's oddly comforting. I've been on the surface so long, I'd almost forgotten what it's like under the ground.

Zanik.GatheredIngredients.6.src: Oh, right. Well I'll need them to continue. Let me know when you're ready to hand them over.

Zanik.FoundPutrilius.NoSpace.src: Oh, you've got your hands full right now. Come back and see me when you've got some space free.

Quest.Objective.5.src: Return to Zanik and explain the situation.

Zanik.NotGatheredIngredients.Choices.Cho.src: Shouldn't be a problem for a strong adventurer like you, right?

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseEgg.3.src: So, no, I do not have any eggs for you!

Quest.Objective.0.src: Speak to Zanik about the Corrupted Essence you got from a strange raven.

Putrilius.InBeat5.EndCorruption.3.src: Still, if you can get the Dreaming Stone under control, and its inhabitant can behave, I am willing to work to undo this nonsense. Though it might take some time.

Zanik.PostQuest.1.src: Thanks again for helping figure out what was going on!

Zanik.NotGatheredIngredients.Choices.Cho.src: The Twilight Lily is a special flower that grows in damp dark places. I think I saw one by that tree in the lake, further inside the cave.

Zanik.NotGatheredIngredients.3.src: Then I'm going to need a twilight lily. They grow deep in the dark, by underground lakes. There's one not far from here.

Zanik.SpokenTo.Has10Samples.3.src: Then I'm going to need a twilight lily. They grow deep in the dark, by underground lakes. There's one not far from here.

Zanik.NotSpokenTo.3.src: There are ravens around this keep that are... stranger than the rest. More vibrant, a little luminescent.

Zanik.GatheredIngredients.4.src: There's traces of cthonian demon here. See the way it wriggles? It's odd though, a bit like a parasite. It's part of a bigger whole though, there must be a central intelligence for it somewhere.

Putrilius.InBeat5.Bwak.1.src: Um... yes, well... I mean... bwak!

Putrilius.InBeat5.NotSure.2.src: Urgh, I just can't do it anymore. How far from grace I have fallen to spend my aeons pretending to be a common farm fowl.

Zanik.GatheredIngredients.3.src: Wait... there's more than one infection here. One magical, one biological and one distinctly demonic. Not avernic, though. Oh no, this is rare indeed.

Zanik.NotGatheredIngredients.Choices.Cho.src: Water that's been blessed by the priests of Zamorak. I'd look in the temple, maybe not everything there has been tainted?

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseCause.5.src: What resulted is something like a civil war inside the flesh. Energies and consciousnesses ran rampant, warping and changing the hosts into what you see now.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseWhat.3.src: When the rebellion happened, my people were destroyed, in part by the very contracts we had created. Legal loopholes became the noose around our protoplasmic necks.

Putrilius.InBeat5.SourceOfCorruption.3.src: When the war started I split myself up into teeny tiny little versions of myself and hid like a common parasite in the lesser, avernic demons. An excellent plan I thought, until I came here.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseWhat.2.src: Which is to say that we ate one another. In doing so, we gained strength, power, prestige, all the things a growing protean entity might need.

Putrilius.PostQuest.ChoseCause.4.src: With the energies that were released, so too was something else. An ancient consciousness. Not strong enough to infect the minds of individuals, but my fractured parts were less able to defend themselves.

ui.playerconsent.paragraph2.src:
1.	The data we collect

We would like to collect the following types of data (‘Player Activity Data’):

ui.playerconsent.paragraph12.src: I consent to the collection and use of Data for Internet-based Advertising.

ui.playerconsent.paragraph11.src: I consent to the collection and use of Data for Player Activity and Game Diagnostics

ui.playerconsent.paragraph13.src: I consent to the collection and use of Data for both Purposes.

ui.playerconsent.paragraph14.src: If you do give us your consent here, you can withdraw your consent at any time by changing your privacy options and preferences in the legal section of the settings menu. The processing of your personal data (including any third parties who we may share the Player Analytics Data with) will be carried out in accordance with our Privacy Policy – copy of which is available on request and also available here:

ui.playerconsent.paragraph10.src: Please choose what information you are comfortable sharing with us. If you do not opt in using the boxes below, that means we will not collect and use the Player Activity Data for these Purposes.

ui.playerconsent.paragraph5.src: We would like to use this data for the following purposes (‘Purposes’):

ui.playerconsent.paragraph1.src: You have the option to say yes or no to your data being used for either or both (a) player activity and game diagnostics and/or (b) internet-based advertising. If you say yes, we will automatically collect data through a plug-in developed by the Jagex Group. The collected data is securely stored and analysed on AWS servers in Europe. Your device will be equally secure and operate normally regardless of your decision. We may receive certain user data from the Third-Party Platform Provider's Network Services in order for us to provide our game to you. Jagex will not use this information for any marketing or online advertising purposes (including sharing with any advertising partner) where this is restricted by the Third-Party Platform Provider.

StrongProfanitiesFilteringType.Selector..src:
Select how entries of that strength are used by the profanity filter system.

- "Always" will always filter entries, even if they are in the middle of another word. For instance, if "cat" is a profanity, then "scatter" would be filtered to "s***ter" and "caterpilar" to "***erpillar".

- "Filter if full word" will only filter entries that are surrounded by blank spaces or punctuation. For instance, if "cow" is a profanity, then "coward" will be unaltered, but "cow" will be filtered to "***".

- "Ignore" will simply ignore this specific list.

Statue.Generic.src: A statue of Saradomin, there is a plaque with an engraving and an indentation that seems like something small would fit it.

Statue.MainText.src:
Blinded Saradomin still watches true, 
Three sentinels of stone each guard a key.

Statue.MainText.1.src:
Give each a gemstone eye of glistening hue,
And the lord of order will once more see.

Puzzle.Sapphire.1.src:
I glitter in the hue of the calmest sky, 
And the shimmering colours of the coldest deep.

Puzzle.Jade.1.src:
In ancient rituals I am considered wise, 
Though rigid as iron does my wisdom keep.

Puzzle.Jade.src:
In eastern lands is my green skin a prize, 
Though in other colours I am found in the deep.

Puzzle.Sapphire.src:
In terrible poetry does my power lie, 
Where young loves failure causes men to weep.

Puzzle.Opal.1.src:
To magpies, my flaws are a source of veneration, 
When my glittering skin is held up to the light.

Puzzle.Opal.src:
Within me dance all the colours in creation, 
Encased within a shell of gleaming white.

Optional.Book1.Text.NonbinaryAuthor.src:
Have you found the armour yet? Red, scarlet, crimson, glittering ruby-like metal that turns aside almost all blades?

No? Yes? Hard to remember the difference. You will find them, so you have found them?  Is time static to you?

I am in the room again. Cushions, lace, cloth and gemstones. Shining, sparkling, pretty sights to see. People stare through the lattice, waiting for me to say something, yet I do not know what they want to hear.

I am in the chamber as Rasthin offers the others a chance to become something more. To bond with elements, to transcend not to godly heights, but primordial forces in tune with the world. Lacrussa, my sister, asks me to join them, but I have already seen how this ends. I tell her I will miss her, she does not understand. Brakka and Avisk salivate over power, Rasthin sneers knowing the hold she will have over them forever.

I miss them. Will miss them. I have never met them.

Kuldra hatches from her egg, and I know she will kill everyone. She is innocent, she is guilty,  a monster forged by fate. I see my sister dissect Kuldra’s mate, as Kuldra daintily takes a treat from my hand. A gentle beast, destined to destroy us all.

I write this journal as you find this journal. You are here to kill Kuldra, have killed Kuldra, will kill her again.

Ashenfall will heal. Has healed. Will be destroyed.

CriticalPath.Book4.Text.FemaleAuthor.src:
I did not believe it possible, but Lacrussa’s genius continues to impress me. She has, to her great credit, managed to create a queen dragon of our own, a progenitor for our future army. The creature is chimeric in capability, with multiple heads, each able to absorb different aspects so that she might more easily create the required brood.

Lacrussa’s sibling, Viika, seems both enamoured and terrified of the creature in equal measure, but I have long since given up trying to work out the meaning of their strange mood shifts.

The queen has grown much over the last few centuries and has even taken a favoured broodmate - the two of them producing plentiful offspring for both experimentation and labour. While many are flawed, less than they could be, there are least three of note that promise a more powerful army once we iron out the kinks. I shall suggest the broodmate be dissected for study, I’m sure the weakness lies with him.

The timing is most convenient, as there is growing unrest among the talking mammals that wander these lands. One faction stands on the brink of extermination, and they have a deity fighting with them.

I wonder what I could do with a deity to study. Whilst they are false divinities, their powers are undeniable. I shall see if I can inspire them to our service, so that we might test our dragon army against her foes.

Oh, this shall be fun.

CriticalPath.Book5.Text.FemaleAuthor.src:
I have underestimated the queen we created. I thought her a mindless, cowardly beast, yet she is a cunning and vengeful creature. She waited. That’s the most terrifying thing. She waited! When we were distracted. When we were not expecting it. She waited and then she turned her brood against us and forced us into hiding.

She ate Brakka first. I won’t mourn him. He was an arrogant narcissist with little to offer beyond his masonry. Avisk has vanished into the aether, which isn’t a concern, but Lacrussa’s silence worries me. Of all my fellow Dragonkin, she is the only one worth my respect. It would be a genuine tragedy if the world lost her genius.

The garou goddess, this Lougrim, chooses to fight beside her people, believing she can stand against a queen dragon with divine blood in her veins - Lougrim’s blood! She will learn how well we make our dragons.

I will seal myself away here, within the heart of the Harmonic Resonator. I alone know the full capabilities of this device and I know how to weaponise it. If Kuldra is to kill me, then I shall take her and half of Ashenfall with me!

CriticalPath.Book3.Text.FemaleAuthor.src:
It is strange, to be one with an element - to feel it coursing through your veins, your cells, your very thoughts. Fire illuminates and strips bare. It cleanses and it scours, and it reveals parts of the universe I had never dared to gaze on before.

There are gaps, cracks if you will, in the skein of the universe and, through those gaps, wonders gaze back at us. Or horrors, perhaps, if you’re more prone to fear than joy. I have seen the crawling pests of the Void skittering at the edge of reality. The Aughra’s other shells gaze back at us from the Abyss, and - further, beyond that - are beasts so colossal that thinking on them gives me a headache.

Yet, of all the worlds I gaze at in wonder, this one is still the brightest of all. Gielinor, by the monkey’s tongue, is a perfect world. Not just by the measure of its creators, but in its possibilities. It is ripe with magic, filled with potential and the spark within me burns with inspiration at what it could become.

I need but the right tools to turn it toward greatness. I need an army strong enough to keep the rabble in check. Lacrussa can create them. It was easy enough to inspire her to do so, the spark of creativity is so very easy to ignite.

In Avisk I did the same with his obsession with the mind, for if I am to have an army of unstoppable beasts, I must be able to control them.

The world can be reshaped into something wonderful. A glorious regime, burning bright as a star.

Rasthin, Empress of Gielinor. Yes, I very much like the sound of that.

CriticalPath.Book6.Text.FemaleAuthor.src:
She is here: the pinnacle of dragon creation, the queen, fused with divine blood and now housing the elemental power of my kin. Kuldra stands at my gate and with each passing second she weakens the defences. She will kill me, I know this, but I will not go down without a fight.

The Resonator is charged, primed with the perfect discordance. If I had more time, I could build a shockwave strong enough to rip the entire continent apart, but I will settle on taking Kuldra with me.

Viika visited me earlier. How they are alive I do not know; they arrived to give me their standard cryptic prophecy and then left, just like always.

“She will turn the Veil against the world,” they said, as if that means anything.

If I had more time, I might try to care, but now… now I see no way out, except to end things on my terms. I shall ready a cataclysm that will fracture Ashenfall and take Kuldra and her brood with me.

With any luck, the backwash of the explosion will poison the anima of this planet, killing the Roakin and their eggs. Unlikely, true, but one can dream.

Curse you, Kuldra! You could have been the herald of a glorious new age for Gielinor, yet you fall to mindless vengeance like the beast you are!

I will spit my last breath upon you, wishing that it will be your last breath as well.

CriticalPath.Book1.Text.FemaleAuthor.src:
The Harmonic Resonator may be my greatest work. It is poetry forged into metal and wire, driven by a divine geometry that none of my kin have dreamed of before. Even Kerapac, the self-proclaimed genius, could not conceive of such technology.

The Roakin turned this place into a glorified wasteyard, venting their unwanted “tainted” anima back into the atmosphere so that the resonance might fade and it could return “pure”. They are fools, of course, for it is these resonances that allow anima to perform wonders. The green False User whom these mortals worship - he found a way to trap this resonant anima into stones and unleash them as magic tricks. With the Harmonic Resonator, we shall bind the magics into our very souls, allowing us to transcend the limitations of the Roakin’s curse.

Alas, our mortal shells are too frail to absorb a range of anima, so we must focus on a single attribute to embody. I have settled on the primal elements, earth, fire, water and air, rather than the more conceptual catalytic properties, as these will allow us the greatest ability to reshape Ashenfall to a glorious new Dragonkin empire.

All shall know the name of Rasthin, the first empress of the Dragonkin.

Optional.Book3.Text.MaleAuthor.src:
The dragonkin are real. Creatures we had heard of only in the most obscure legends, ancient beings of unfathomable power and terrible evil, and they’re here on Ashenfall.

It must be they who are responsible for the madness that infects my kin. Who else would engineer a curse that reaches into your mind and twists every thought into violence and cruelty? They turn us against one another and they watch as we do so. They sneer and laugh and cackle to the night sky.

Monsters. Every last one of them. Monsters.

They send dragons to hunt us down. Toying with us as we flee to safety. Each raid, our numbers dwindle. Each attack leaves less of us behind.

At least my brother on the mainland will be safe. Forinthry is impregnable: he’ll outlive us all.

PuzzleText.Book1.Text.FemaleAuthor.src:
The gods breathed life into all of creation.
They wept great tears at our cruel ministrations.
They buried their hopes for us, deep in the ground.
Then burned all the bridges that kept them around.

OptionalBook2.Text.MaleAuthor.src:
This land is full of wonders. Magic flows through this place like rivers of possibility, the spirits dance around everything, with more vibrancy than I have even seen on Abbinah. Armadyl is right to be concerned with this place: if someone were to seize control of the power here, they could tear the planet apart.

We are not the first to reach these deeper regions, either. There are structures, both hidden and overt, of designs that we’ve only seen previously in legends. They are not of human, mahjarrat or any other recognisable design, save for those whispered of in hidden corners of other worlds.

The difference here is that these are no mere ruins. Someone lives here and they are watching us. My squadron is tired, the magic here makes our heads spin, and the higher we fly, the sicker we get. It’s as if someone has put a curse on the clouds, and each time we breathe them in, we get weaker.

We’ve already lost several of our number and been forced to bury them in this strange soil. Perhaps the magic of this place will return them to us? One can dream.

CriticalPath.Book2.Text.FemaleAuthor.src:
We are not normally creatures of ceremony, we Dragonkin, yet I feel the need for it in our great endeavour. Perhaps the old priests, like that fool Kranon, have a point, for what better way to acknowledge something’s importance, than to dress it up in ritual?

Candles. Music. Well-tailored robes: these are the tools that I craft for my companions and myself, so that we may give this moment the reverence it requires. Even Avisk, with his constant sarcasm and flippancy, succumbs to the gravity of the moment.

We will not be gods.

We will not be False Users, claiming the power of the Roakin’s artifacts.

We will be something else, something more. We will be the earth, the wind, the blaze of the sun and the crashing waves of the ocean. We will be primordial forces incarnate.

There is music, a song from the old world, before it was lost in the Great Revision. It speaks of the passage of time, the solemnity of the stars and the eternity of creation. Nonsense, and proved terribly wrong, yet… fitting, all the same.

I wrote it. It is some of my best work.

The Harmonic Resonator builds into a great orchestra of anima. Dazzling threads of colour dance and writhe according to my grand design. I watch them spiral overhead, swirling in a scintillating circle and I smile at my last moment of mundane mortality, as fire and I become one.

Zilyana.Female.AttemptToReceiveReward.No.src: Ah, but your burden is too great right now. Come speak to me when you have divested yourself of some of what you carry.

Zilyana.Female.Intro.1.src: Ah, good you're here. Your allies have already filled me in on your exploits, and I must say I'm impressed.

Zilyana.Female.DefeatedKuldra.RepeatFigh.src: Ah, looking to relive your moment of glory? Come with me down memory lane to face Kuldra again?

Zilyana.SpokenTo.CompletedFirstRun.2.src: Alas, there will be no statues in your honour on the mainland. Nor will bards sing songs of your deeds, for Guthix's veil will prevent your legend escaping these isles for now.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Dragonki.src: And what have the dragonkin done with that time? With that impossible history? They create monsters.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Saradomi.src: As one of the oldest of the gods, his wisdom is honed across the aeons of discoveries,  unexpected crises and patient reflection.

Bandos wielded his power like a club. Zamorak uses his to form pacts with demonic creatures seeking to spread corruption and dismay. While Armadyl cowers from his, unwilling to fully shoulder  the burden of godhood.

Elder.Return.NoStaff.2.src: Be careful if you happen to use it with the Leggings of Lightness. I can't guarantee your safety.

Zilyana.Female.SpokenTo.NotStartedRun.2.src: Be sure you're as prepared as you can be. Are you ready to kill the queen?

Zilyana.Female.Intro.6.src: But if you think you're prepared enough, are you read to kill a queen?

Zilyana.SpokenTo.CompletedFirstRun.3.src: But the people here will remember the good you have done, and in time we will find a way to let the world know of your heroism.

Zilyana.Female.DefeatedKuldra.ReturnWith.src: Dragons, they seem to have so many heads, don't they? Let me take that one from you.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Kuldra.5.src: Each shockwave gets larger and more destructive by the hour and she threatens the mainland with destruction on a scale not seen since the end of the God Wars.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.AboutSel.src: For centuries I have served as the leader of his armies and herald of his divine wisdom.

Objective.ScornedWilderness.src: Gain access to the Scorned Wilderness.

DragonGate.FellHollowComplete.Genderless.src: Gentle Imaru, blessed by water, finally rests in peace.

Zilyana.Female.ImReadyResponse.1.src: Good. I will take you to Kuldra's island. I'll aid you where I can, and I'll extract you if you require it, but the bulk of the battle will fall to you.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Kuldra.2.src: Her power rivals just about anything on this planet, myself included. Were the gods still here, I'm sure they could deal with her, but sadly the so-called "World Guardian" foolishly put a stop to that.

Zilyana.Female.HandedOverHead.1.src: Here, it is a mere trifle compared to the gift you have given the rest of us with Kuldra's death, yet I hope it will serve you well.

Zilyana.SpokenTo.CompletedFirstRun.4.src: Here, let me take that vile trophy from you, so that I might reward you with something more fitting your stature than this... slimy mess.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Saradomi.src: His guidance helps us all to find our place in the world. That thing which each of us craves from the day of our birth, a need to belong and be useful.

Zilyana.GothereTooEarly.src: Hrmm, here a bit soon arne't you? Shouldn't you take out the generals before facing the queen?

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.AboutSel.src: I am of the icyene, a race of proud, winged warriors, from the world of Hallow. The seat of Saradomin's power.

PlayerChoice.GenderlessVoice.OptionalDia.src: I've asked everything I need to.

Zilyana.Female.DontHandOverHead.1.src: It is a grim tradition to carry the body parts of your slain enemy, but as a warrior I understand it. When you are ready to move on, come speak to me again.

Zilyana.Female.INeedMoreTimeResponse.1.src: It's wise to plan and prepare, but don't take too long. Kuldra's readying herself to unleash a catastrophe across Gielinor that could see the end of everything.

Zilyana.Female.ImReadyResponse.2.src: May Saradomin guide and watch over you! And may Kuldra know his wrath! TO BATTLE!

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Saradomi.src: My lord Saradomin is the one true god. While others may profess to possess divine power, they lack the wisdom and the foresight that true divinity requires.

Zilyana.Female.Intro.4.src: My lord, Saradomin, has called me here to help deal with the threat, but the anima here... it's like it drains me, I feel myself weakening the closer I get to her tower. So I'm afraid I have to pass the torch to you.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.AboutSel.src: My name is Commander Zilyana, and I allow myself the personal pride to call myself the right hand of Saradomin.

Elder.ReturnStaff.2.src: My natural instinct is to tell you to bring it to Uzzer or Manafem, that they have better claim to it, but things have changed in the Sands.

Zilyana.Female.Intro.2.src: Not many people could stand up to the dragons of Kuldra's brood, let alone survive in a place like this, yet you almost make it look easy.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Kuldra.3.src: Now she turns the dragonkin's technology on the rest of the world, seemingly fueled by a mindless hatred for the rest of us.

Objective.WhenReady.src: Once you are fully prepared, speak to Zilyana.

PlayerNotification.GenderlessVoice.Retur.src: Pause your run and return to Zilyana?

Elder.ReturnStaff.4.src: Please, I offer this in return. Perhaps Lougrim will guide you as much as she guided us.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Saradomi.src: Saradomin improves the lives of his followers. Through his wisdom he has turned civilisations away from tribal warfare and helped them to become thriving nations.

Zilyana.SpokenTo.CompletedFirstRun.1.src: Saradomin was right to put his faith in you, just as we all were. You have slain the God Eater and saved all of Gielinor in the process.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Kuldra.1.src: She has consumed more of the world's raw anima than anyone should be able to, and she has been forged with the blood of the garou's fallen deity.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Kuldra.4.src: She's turned their machine into some sort of weapon, building wave after wave of discordant anima and using the veil over this island like some sort of resonating chamber.

Quest.Description.src: Take the fight to Kuldra, and end this once and for all.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Dragonki.src: That tells you everything you need to know about them. With all the time in creation, and all the secrets they have uncovered in that time, they create armies of dragons to torture the rest of us with.

DragonGate.NotDoneDragonSlayer.Genderles.src: The blood of the four seal this gate. One of earth, one of water, one of air and one of flame.

PlayerNarration.Genderless.GoThroughDoor.src: The door opens with disturbing ease.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Dragonki.src: The dragonkin are older than the world. Indeed they are older than the universe, coming, as they do, from the iteration before.

The five who ventured to Ashenfall are no different. Whilst they labelled themselves as mavericks and visionaries, they simply repeat the mistakes of their kin, and add an extra layer or two of horror.

DragonGate.UmbralSandsComplete.Genderles.src: The gate stands open, destiny awaits.

DragonGate.NotDoneDragonSlayer.Genderles.src: The lord of the skies has fallen. Xikotal, slain by Kuldra's fury.

DragonGate.DragonSlayerComplete.Genderle.src: The scaled blight has been slain. Velgar's cruelty no longer infects the earth.

Icthlarin.PostKuldraDeath.1.src: There is a stillness in the Underworld. A quietude. You have achieved something remarkable.

Elder.ReturnStaff.3.src: They look to us now. Alcarrid leads. And we shall lead with the Staff of Lougrim.

Zilyana.Female.Intro.5.src: This island will make a vital base, take some time to set yourself up for success. There will be no raids or anything here, I'll see to that.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.AboutSel.src: Until comparatively recently I had been frozen in time, trapped in the God Wars even though the world had moved on.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Exit.1.src: Very well. I will be here when you're ready to face Kuldra.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Kuldra.6.src: We must stop her, at all costs.

Zilyana.Female.INeedMoreTimeResponse.2.src: We should put a stop to that, as soon as possible.

Elder.Return.NoStaff.1.src: Welcome back, friend of the Moon Garou. I hope the magic carpet is serving you well.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.AboutSel.src: Well... I say moved on, I sometimes wonder whether times ever really change.

PlayerChoice.GenderlessVoice.OptionalDia.src: What can you tell me about Kuldra?
What can you tell me about Saradomin?
What can you tell me about the dragonkin?

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Intro.1.src: What would you like to know?

Zilyana.Female.SpokenTo.NotStartedRun.1.src: When you're ready, I will take you as far to Kuldra's lair as I can. You'll need to fight your way to the centre of her stronghold yourself.

Zilyana.Female.CheckPointQuery.src: Where would you like me to take you?

Zilyana.Female.Intro.3.src: Which is why I need you to finish this threat, once and for all. Kuldra's threatening all of Gielinor now. Shockwaves of discordant anima have been blasting out from this place and they're getting stronger with each wave.

Icthlarin.PostKuldraDeath.3.src: While I may be immortal, I can be forgotten. In your case, there is no chance of being forgotten at all. Your legacy is cast in iron.

Zilyana.Female.OptionalDialogue.Dragonki.src: Yes, an iteration, there have been others. Countless others, stretching back across timelines so vast the entire history of Gielinor wouldn't even register as a dot.

Elder.ReturnStaff.1.src: You carry the Staff of Lougrim, our foremother! Bless the stars!

Icthlarin.PostKuldraDeath.2.src: You have not just become a legend. You have become THE legend of Ashenfall - the one that all the other stories build towards.

Zilyana.Female.SpokenTo.AttemptedRun.1.src: You made good progress. I have faith that you can see this through. Are you ready to try again?

PlayerNotification.GenderlessVoice.NoSpa.src: Your inventory is too full. You cannot collect Kuldra's head.
